# vibe.js

vibe.js: npm scope `@usevibejs`, CLI `vibejs` (never `vibe`). Not monday.com Vibe (`@vibe/*`), not the `@vibe.js/*` packages (a different project), not the npm packages `vibejs` or `vibe.js`.

A full-stack TypeScript framework where the UI, the server and the contract between them are type-checked end to end, and every tool speaks to coding agents as well as to people.

- [Getting started](https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/getting-started): create an app, run it and check it.
- [Tutorial](https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/tutorial): add an API resource and a page, catch a type error, then build and serve the app.
- [CLI reference](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/): every `vibejs` command, its options and examples.
- [Error codes](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/): every `VIBE####` code with its message and fixes.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/

---

# CLI and AI agents

Every `vibejs` command works the same for people and for coding agents. For an agent, it answers with one JSON object that says what happened and what to do next, it never prompts, and its docs ship with the installed version.

## Agent mode

`vibejs` switches to agent mode when it runs inside a known coding agent, detected from the environment, or when `VIBEJS_AGENT=1` is set. `VIBEJS_AGENT=0` turns it off. `--json` gives the same output without agent mode.

In agent mode, a command:

- prints a single JSON object to stdout (`vibejs dev` prints one JSON event per line);
- never prompts, and never overwrites a file without consent;
- keeps its output short, with limits on long lists.

## Results and exit codes

Every result has the same envelope:

```ts
interface JsonEnvelope {
  ok: boolean;
  command: string;
  version: string;
  /** Commands to run next. */
  next?: string[];
  error?: {
    code: string;
    message: string;
    /** The docs page of the code. */
    docs: string;
    fixes?: string[];
    /** The inputs that a command needs and did not get. */
    missing?: { name: string; flag?: string; values?: string[]; example: string }[];
  };
}
```

A command exits with:

| Code | Meaning                           |
| ---- | --------------------------------- |
| `0`  | Success.                          |
| `1`  | The work failed, such as a check. |
| `2`  | Wrong usage or configuration.     |

`vibejs check --json` adds `diagnostics`: each one has its `source` (`tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `vitest`, `coverage` or `vibejs`), `code`, `severity`, `file`, `loc` (`file:line:column`) and `message`, and for vibe.js codes the `docs` link and the `fixes`. Template errors in `.vibe` files are reported at their place in the `.vibe` file.

## AGENTS.md

A new app has an `AGENTS.md` with a block of vibe.js rules between two marker lines, and a `CLAUDE.md` that imports it with `@AGENTS.md`. The block holds:

- the exact commands to run, through the app's own CLI;
- the rules that agents most often get wrong in a vibe.js app;
- a one-line index of the docs in `node_modules/@usevibejs/cli/dist/docs`, so the agent reads the docs of the installed version instead of what it remembers.

```sh
vibejs agents sync
vibejs agents sync --check
```

`vibejs agents sync` rewrites the block for the installed version, and `vibejs dev` does the same when it starts. `--check` writes nothing and fails when a file is out of date. Your own notes go outside the markers and are kept. Malformed markers stop the sync with [VIBE8601](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8601).

## Docs and errors offline

Every `VIBE####` error carries its code, its fixes and a link to its page. The CLI answers from the docs that it bundles, without a network:

```sh
vibejs explain VIBE8601
vibejs docs guides/tutorial
vibejs docs template type error
```

`vibejs explain` prints the message, the fixes and the link of a code. `vibejs docs` takes a code, a page path or search words.

## The dev server

`vibejs dev` writes its state to `.vibejs/dev.lock` and every error and log line of the build, the browser and the server to `.vibejs/dev.log`. A second `vibejs dev` reports the running server instead of starting another one. While it runs:

- `vibejs errors` lists the current build errors and the latest runtime errors;
- `vibejs logs` shows the latest log entries, filtered by level, source, text or time;
- `vibejs request GET /api/users` calls a route through the running server, or in process when none runs;
- `vibejs di` shows the modules and providers of the server.

`vibejs routes` lists the API routes and the UI routes, and `vibejs components` lists the `.vibe` components with their props, models and type arguments. Neither needs a running dev server.

## MCP

`vibejs mcp` serves the commands to an agent as [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) tools over stdio. Each tool answers like its `--json` command:

| Tool                 | Command                                   |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `get_errors`         | `vibejs errors`                           |
| `get_logs`           | `vibejs logs`                             |
| `get_routes`         | `vibejs routes`                           |
| `get_di_graph`       | `vibejs di`                               |
| `get_component_tree` | `vibejs components`                       |
| `check`              | `vibejs check`                            |
| `request`            | `vibejs request`                          |
| `explain`            | `vibejs docs`: a code, a page or a search |

With `--read-only`, the `request` tool accepts only `GET`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`.

## Reference

The [CLI reference](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/) lists every command with its options and examples; `vibejs <command> --help --json` returns the same reference as JSON.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/ai-agents

---

# Coming from NestJS

Modules, providers, controllers, guards, interceptors, filters and lifecycle hooks work the way you expect. Three things differ, and most of the table below follows from them:

- **No reflected types.** vibe.js does not use `emitDecoratorMetadata` or `reflect-metadata`. Dependencies are fields initialized with `inject(Token)`, so they are explicit under every compiler.
- **Contracts instead of route decorators.** Routes, inputs, responses and errors are declared once with `defineContract`. The server handles them with `@Handle(route)`; the UI calls them with `createClient`, fully typed and without code generation.
- **One typed `ctx` instead of parameter decorators.** A handler takes `ctx: Ctx<typeof contract.route>`, which holds the validated params, query, headers and body.

## Idioms

| NestJS                                                                           | vibe.js                                                                                  | What catches the old form                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@Injectable()` on a provider                                                    | A plain class listed in `providers`                                                      | `@Injectable` is not exported, a compile error; see [Providers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/modules#providers)                                                                                                               |
| Constructor injection: `constructor(private db: Db)`                             | `private readonly db = inject(Db)`                                                       | [VIBE9104](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9104) at startup                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `@Inject(TOKEN)` with a string or symbol token                                   | `token<T>('Name')` and `inject(Token)`                                                   | `Inject` is not exported, a compile error; see [Injecting dependencies](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/modules#injecting-dependencies). A token nobody provides then fails with [VIBE9102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9102)                    |
| `@Global()`                                                                      | `@Module({ global: true })`                                                              | `Global` is not exported, a compile error; see [Modules](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/modules#modules). A missing `global: true` then surfaces as [VIBE9102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9102)                                                |
| `@Get()`, `@Post(':id')` on methods                                              | A route in `defineContract`, served by `@Handle(contract.route)`                         | [VIBE9303](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9303) for a route without a handler                                                                                                                                                    |
| `@Controller('users')`                                                           | `@Controller(contract)`; the path prefix is part of the contract                         | `@Controller` takes a contract, so a string is a compile error; see [Routes](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/contracts#routes)                                                                                                   |
| `@Body()`, `@Param()`, `@Query()`, `@Headers()`, `@Req()`                        | `ctx.body`, `ctx.params`, `ctx.query`, `ctx.headers`, `ctx.req`                          | [TS1241 on @Handle](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/handlers#ts1241-on-handle) for a signature that does not match the route                                                                                                     |
| `ValidationPipe`, DTO classes, `ParseIntPipe`                                    | Standard Schema schemas in the contract: `body`, `query`, `params`                       | `ValidationPipe` and `ParseIntPipe` are not exported, a compile error; see [Validation](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/handlers#validation)                                                                                     |
| `NotFoundException` and other exception classes                                  | `ctx.fail('CODE', detail?)` with `errors: { CODE: 404 }` in the contract, or `HttpError` | [VIBE9502](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9502) for a code that the route does not declare                                                                                                                                       |
| `NestFactory.create(AppModule)`                                                  | `VibeFactory.create(AppModule, appOptions)`, then `listen()`                             | `NestFactory` is not exported, a compile error; see [Creating the application](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/#creating-the-application)                                                                                   |
| `app.useGlobalGuards()`, `app.useGlobalInterceptors()`, `app.useGlobalFilters()` | `guards`, `interceptors` and `filters` in `AppOptions`                                   | `App` has no `useGlobal*` methods, a compile error; see [Global enhancers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/pipeline#global-enhancers)                                                                                            |
| `app.use()` and Express middleware                                               | `Middleware`: `(req, next) => Promise<Response>` on Fetch `Request` and `Response`       | `app.use()` does not exist, a compile error; see [Middleware](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/pipeline#middleware)                                                                                                               |
| `@SetMetadata()` and `Reflector`                                                 | `createMetadata<T>(name)` and `ctx.getMetadata(key)`                                     | `SetMetadata` and `Reflector` are not exported, a compile error; see [Metadata](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/pipeline#metadata)                                                                                               |
| `@nestjs/testing`                                                                | `Test.createTestingModule()` from `@usevibejs/server/testing`, with `overrideProvider()` | `@nestjs/testing` is not a dependency, an unresolved import; see [Testing the server](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/testing)                                                                                                   |
| Supertest against `app.getHttpServer()`                                          | `createClient(contracts, { baseUrl: '/api', fetch: app.fetch })`                         | `app.getHttpServer()` does not exist, a compile error; see [Testing](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/testing)                                                                                                                    |
| `@nestjs/swagger` decorators                                                     | `generateOpenApi(contracts, options)` from `@usevibejs/server/openapi`                   | The package is not a dependency, a compile error; see [OpenAPI](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/contracts#openapi)                                                                                                               |
| `@nestjs/config` and `ConfigService.get()`                                       | `defineConfig(schema)`, a typed config class to provide and inject                       | `@nestjs/config` is not a dependency, an unresolved import; see [Environment config](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/configuration#environment-config). Missing or invalid variables then fail with [VIBE9601](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9601) |
| `reflect-metadata` and `emitDecoratorMetadata`                                   | Neither; only `experimentalDecorators: true`                                             | Nothing: the server never reads the emitted metadata, so it is dead weight; see [TypeScript setup](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/configuration#typescript-setup)                                                               |
| `forwardRef()` for circular providers                                            | Move the shared part into a third provider that both `inject()`                          | [VIBE9103](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9103) for a provider cycle                                                                                                                                                             |
| `forRoot()` dynamic modules                                                      | The same: a static method that returns a `DynamicModule`                                 | [VIBE9201](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9201) when the module class lacks `@Module()`                                                                                                                                          |

## A controller, side by side

The NestJS controller

```text
@Controller('todos')
export class TodosController {
  constructor(private readonly todos: TodosService) {}

  @Get(':id')
  findOne(@Param('id') id: string) {
    const todo = this.todos.find(id);
    if (!todo) throw new NotFoundException();
    return todo;
  }
}
```

becomes a contract and a controller:

```ts
export const todos = defineContract('/todos', {
  findOne: get('/:id', { response: Todo, errors: { TODO_NOT_FOUND: 404 } }),
});

@Controller(todos)
export class TodosController {
  private readonly todos = inject(TodosService);

  @Handle(todos.findOne)
  findOne(ctx: Ctx<typeof todos.findOne>): v.InferOutput<typeof Todo> {
    return this.todos.find(ctx.params.id) ?? ctx.fail('TODO_NOT_FOUND');
  }
}
```

The UI calls the same route with `api.todos.findOne({ params: { id } })` and narrows the result to `TODO_NOT_FOUND` with status 404.

## Not in vibe.js v0.1

- Request-scoped and transient providers: every provider is a singleton. Per-request values go on `ctx.state`.
- Parameter decorators and custom pipes: a handler has one `ctx`, and schemas transform inputs.
- Microservices, WebSockets, GraphQL and the CLI schematics of NestJS.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/coming-from-nestjs

---

# Coming from Vue

Most of what you know from Vue 3 with `<script setup>` carries over:

- **Single-file components:** a `.vibe` file has `<script setup lang="ts">`, `<template>` and `<style scoped>` blocks, and the template uses the same directives: `v-if`, `v-for`, `v-show`, `v-model`, `v-bind`, `v-on`, `v-slot`, `v-html` and `v-text`, with the same shorthands and modifiers.
- **Reactivity:** `ref`, `shallowRef`, `reactive`, `readonly`, `computed`, `watch`, `watchEffect`, `effectScope`, `nextTick`, `toRef`, `toRefs` and `toValue` have the same signatures, types and semantics. They are imported from `@usevibejs/ui`.
- **Components:** `defineProps`, `defineEmits`, `defineSlots`, `defineModel`, `defineExpose` and `defineOptions` are macros, the lifecycle hooks have the same names, and `provide`/`inject` with an `InjectionKey`, `useTemplateRef`, `useAttrs`, `useSlots` and `useId` work as in Vue.
- **The app:** `createApp(App).mount('#app')`, `app.use()`, `app.provide()`, `app.config.errorHandler` and `app.config.warnHandler`.

The template compiles to code that creates DOM nodes directly and updates only the bindings whose state changed; there is no virtual DOM. Everything is TypeScript, and the compiler reports a Vue form that vibe.js does not support with a `VIBE####` code whose page shows the replacement.

## Idioms

| Vue                                                    | vibe.js                                                                                           | What catches the Vue form                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app.component('TodoItem', TodoItem)`                  | `import TodoItem from './TodoItem.vibe'` in each file that uses it                                | [VIBE5301](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5301)                               |
| `app.mixin({ ... })`                                   | a composable such as `useFeature()`                                                               | [VIBE5301](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5301)                               |
| `app.directive('focus', ...)`, `v-focus`               | `useTemplateRef('input')` with `onMounted()`                                                      | [VIBE2908](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2908), [VIBE5301](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5301) |
| `<script>` with `export default { data() {} }`         | `<script setup lang="ts">`                                                                        | [VIBE1004](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1004)                               |
| `<script setup>` without `lang`, or `lang="js"`        | `<script setup lang="ts">`                                                                        | [VIBE1005](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1005)                               |
| `<todo-item>`                                          | `<TodoItem>`                                                                                      | [VIBE2002](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2002)                               |
| `ref="input"` with `const input = ref(null)`           | `const input = useTemplateRef<HTMLInputElement>('input')`                                         | [VIBE2701](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2701)                               |
| `defineProps({ title: String })`                       | `defineProps<{ title: string }>()`                                                                | [VIBE3101](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3101)                               |
| `withDefaults(defineProps<Props>(), { size: 'md' })`   | `const { size = 'md' } = defineProps<Props>()`                                                    | [VIBE3006](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3006)                               |
| `const { title, ...rest } = defineProps<Props>()`      | `const { title } = defineProps<Props>()` and `$attrs`                                             | [VIBE3104](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3104)                               |
| `defineEmits(['pick'])`                                | `defineEmits<{ pick: [id: string] }>()`                                                           | [VIBE3201](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3201)                               |
| `defineEmits<{ (e: 'pick', id: string): void }>()`     | `defineEmits<{ pick: [id: string] }>()`                                                           | [VIBE3202](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3202)                               |
| `<script setup lang="ts" generic="T">`                 | `defineProps<{ items: Item[] }>()` with a concrete type                                           | [VIBE1013](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1013)                               |
| `<component is="TodoItem">`, `:is="'TodoItem'"`        | `<component :is="TodoItem">` with the imported component                                          | [VIBE2006](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2006), [VIBE5207](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5207) |
| `$el`, `$parent`, `$refs` or `this` in a template      | `useTemplateRef('name')` and bindings of `<script setup>`                                         | [VIBE2008](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2008)                               |
| `v-model="title"` where `title` is a prop              | `const title = defineModel<string>('title')`                                                      | [VIBE2504](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2504)                               |
| `v-for` without `:key`                                 | `v-for="item in items" :key="item.id"`                                                            | [VIBE2203](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2203)                               |
| `v-if` and `v-for` on one element                      | `<template v-for>` around the `v-if`, or a `computed` list                                        | [VIBE2103](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2103)                               |
| `<Teleport to="body">`                                 | a native `<dialog>` or the `popover` attribute                                                    | [VIBE2901](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2901)                               |
| `<KeepAlive>`                                          | `v-show`, or state kept in a composable                                                           | [VIBE2902](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2902)                               |
| `<Transition>`                                         | CSS transitions on a `:class` binding                                                             | [VIBE2903](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2903)                               |
| `<TransitionGroup>`                                    | CSS animations on keyed `v-for` items                                                             | [VIBE2904](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2904)                               |
| `<Suspense>`                                           | a `ref` filled when the data arrives, and `v-if`                                                  | [VIBE2905](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2905)                               |
| `v-memo`                                               | `computed`                                                                                        | [VIBE2906](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2906)                               |
| `v-once`                                               | a `const` of `<script setup>`                                                                     | [VIBE2907](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2907)                               |
| `v-cloak`                                              | a plain `<div id="app"></div>`: templates are compiled ahead of time, so no raw template is shown | [VIBE2909](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2909)                               |
| `@vue:mounted`, `@vnode-mounted`                       | `onMounted()` with `useTemplateRef()`                                                             | [VIBE2910](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2910)                               |
| `async setup()`, top-level `await` in `<script setup>` | `const data = ref()` filled by a promise                                                          | [VIBE3002](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3002), [VIBE5204](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5204) |
| `<style module>`                                       | `<style scoped>`                                                                                  | [VIBE1007](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1007)                               |
| `v-bind(color)` in `<style>`                           | `:style="{ '--color': color }"` and `var(--color)`                                                | [VIBE4003](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4003)                               |
| `>>> .child`, `/deep/ .child`, `::v-deep`              | `:deep(.child)`                                                                                   | [VIBE4004](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4004)                               |
| `<template src="./list.html">`                         | the content written inside `<template>`                                                           | [VIBE1006](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1006)                               |
| `@pick.once="onPick"` on a component                   | `@pick="onPick"` and the check inside `onPick`                                                    | [VIBE2305](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2305)                               |
| `v-on="{ click, focus }"`                              | `@click="click" @focus="focus"`                                                                   | [VIBE2302](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2302)                               |
| `<template #[name]>`                                   | `<template v-if="wide" #wide>` with static names                                                  | [VIBE2605](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2605)                               |

## Same API, different behavior

- `onBeforeMount` runs after the component's DOM is built and before it is inserted, so a child's runs before its parent's, and template refs are already set. See [Hook order](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/lifecycle#hook-order).
- Each read of a prop calls into the parent and evaluates the bound expression again; put expensive derivations in `computed`. See [Reading props](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components#reading-props).
- Slot fallback content renders only when the parent passes no content for the slot, not when the passed content renders nothing. See [Fallback content](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components#fallback-content).
- A template ref on a component holds only what the component passes to `defineExpose()`, never its instance. See [Exposing values](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components#exposing-values).
- Event listeners are attached to the elements themselves, without delegation. See [Events](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/template-syntax#events).
- In development, a template edit keeps the component's state but creates its child components again. See [Hot updates](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/#hot-updates).
- Calling a slot function in the script renders the slot and creates its DOM; test `$slots.name` instead. See [Slots in script](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components#slots-in-script).

## Not in vibe.js

Importing one of these from `@usevibejs/ui` fails to type-check with TS2305 (module has no exported member).

- `h()`, render functions and JSX: write a template; choose a component at runtime with `<component :is>`.
- `defineAsyncComponent`: the router loads a route component from `() => import('./Page.vibe')` itself.
- `customRef`: a `shallowRef` with a `watch`, or a `computed` with `get` and `set`.
- `proxyRefs`: templates unwrap the top-level refs of `<script setup>`; in script, use `.value` or `reactive()`.
- `effect`: `watchEffect` or `watchSyncEffect`.
- `getCurrentInstance`: `useAttrs()`, `useSlots()`, `useId()` and `inject()` cover the uses of the instance.
- `app.config.globalProperties`: `app.provide()` and a composable that injects the value.
- `defineCustomElement`: planned for a later version.
- `defineStore` and Pinia: module-scope state in a composable. See [Shared state](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/reactivity#shared-state).
- Server-side rendering and hydration: v0.1 renders in the browser only; server rendering is planned for a later version.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/coming-from-vue

---

# Coming from vue-router and Vue Test Utils

`createRouter`, `RouterView`, `RouterLink`, `useRoute`, nested routes, guards that return a location, `mount` and wrappers work the way you expect. What differs follows from four choices:

- **Typed routes from one file.** Routes are declared once with `defineRoutes()` and registered with `Register`, so names, params and every `to` are checked, in templates too. Routes are static: there is no `addRoute()`.
- **Explicit imports.** There are no global components and no instance properties in templates: `RouterLink` and `RouterView` are imported, and the route comes from `useRoute()`.
- **Guards return their decision.** A guard returns `false`, a location or nothing; there is no `next()`.
- **Tests drive the real tree.** `mount()` renders the real children with the real app; there are no stubs, no shallow mounting and no component instance to reach into. Tests query the DOM with CSS selectors.

## Router

| vue-router                                                                       | vibe.js                                                                                                           | What catches the old form                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `next()`, `next(false)`, `next('/login')` in a guard                             | `return`, `return false`, `return '/login'`                                                                       | [VIBE7107](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7107) for a guard with a third parameter                                           |
| `createWebHashHistory()`                                                         | `createWebHistory()`, with the server falling back to `index.html`                                                | Not exported, a compile error                                                                             |
| `alias`, `sensitive`, `strict`, `parseQuery` and the other deferred options      | A redirecting route instead of an alias; the fixed matching rules                                                 | [VIBE7103](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7103), which names the alternative                                                 |
| `router.addRoute()`, `router.removeRoute()`                                      | Every route in `routes.ts`; guards and `meta` for routes that depend on the user                                  | Not on `Router`, a compile error; see [Routes](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/routing#routes)                                   |
| Named views: `components: { default, sidebar }`                                  | Nested child routes, each with one component                                                                      | [VIBE7103](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7103)                                                                              |
| `<RouterView v-slot="{ Component }">` with `KeepAlive` or `Transition`           | `<RouterView />` without content                                                                                  | [VIBE7115](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7115)                                                                              |
| `<RouterLink custom v-slot="{ href, navigate }">`                                | `useLink({ to })` in your own link component                                                                      | `custom` is not a prop, a template type error; see [useLink](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/routing#routerview-and-routerlink)  |
| `<RouterLink to="https://example.com">`                                          | A plain `<a href>`                                                                                                | [VIBE7114](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7114)                                                                              |
| `<router-link>` and `<router-view>`                                              | `<RouterLink>` and `<RouterView>`                                                                                 | [VIBE2002](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2002) once the component is imported                                               |
| `RouterLink` used without an import (global registration)                        | `import { RouterLink, RouterView } from '@usevibejs/ui/router'`                                                   | [VIBE2001](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2001)                                                                              |
| `$route` and `$router` in a template                                             | `const route = useRoute()` and `const router = useRouter()` in `<script setup lang="ts">`                         | [VIBE2008](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2008)                                                                              |
| `beforeRouteEnter`, `beforeRouteLeave` and `beforeRouteUpdate` component options | `beforeEnter` on the record or `router.beforeEach()`; `onBeforeRouteLeave()` and `onBeforeRouteUpdate()` in setup | [VIBE1004](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1004) for an options `<script>`, [VIBE3331](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3331) in `defineOptions()` |
| Typed routes from a generated file or a `RouteNamedMap`                          | `defineRoutes([...])` and `interface Register { router: typeof router }`                                          | A wrong name or param is a type error; see [Typed routes](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/routing#creating-the-router)           |
| `useRoute()` with `route.params.id as string`                                    | `useRoute('user')`, whose params are typed                                                                        | [VIBE7113](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7113) when that route is not shown                                                 |
| Pinia `defineStore()` and `storeToRefs()`                                        | A module-scope composable that returns refs and functions                                                         | Not exported, a compile error; see [Shared state](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/data#shared-state)                             |

## Component testing

| Vue Test Utils                                   | vibe.js                                                               | What catches the old form                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mount(C, { global: { plugins: [router] } })`    | `mount(C, { plugins: [router] })`                                     | [VIBE7206](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7206)                                                                   |
| `global.provide`                                 | `provide`                                                             | [VIBE7206](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7206)                                                                   |
| `global.stubs`, `stubs`, `shallow: true`         | The real children, or `vi.mock('./Child.vibe', ...)` for one child    | [VIBE7206](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7206)                                                                   |
| `shallowMount()`                                 | `mount()`                                                             | Not exported, a compile error                                                                  |
| `wrapper.findComponent(Child)`, `getComponent()` | A CSS selector on what the child renders                              | Not on the wrapper, a compile error; see [Finding elements](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/testing#finding-elements) |
| `wrapper.vm.count`, `setData()`                  | Assert the DOM; start from `props`                                    | Not on the wrapper, a compile error; `data` is [VIBE7206](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7206)                    |
| `trigger('keydown.enter')`                       | `trigger('keydown', { key: 'Enter' })`                                | [VIBE7203](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7203)                                                                   |
| `enableAutoUnmount(afterEach)`                   | Nothing: every test unmounts what it mounted                          | Not exported, a compile error                                                                  |
| `attrs`                                          | Attributes in `props`                                                 | [VIBE7206](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7206)                                                                   |
| `findByRole()` and other Testing Library queries | CSS selectors on the wrapper, or any DOM library on `wrapper.element` | Not exported, a compile error                                                                  |
| `environment: 'happy-dom'`                       | `environment: 'jsdom'`, the environment the test API is tested in     | Nothing at compile time; see [Setup](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/testing#setup)                                   |

## A guard, side by side

The vue-router guard

```text
router.beforeEach((to, from, next) => {
  if (to.meta.requiresAuth && !isSignedIn()) next({ name: 'login' });
  else next();
});
```

returns its decision:

```ts
router.beforeEach((to) => {
  if (to.meta.requiresAuth && !isSignedIn()) return { name: 'login' };
});
```

## A test, side by side

The Vue Test Utils test

```text
const wrapper = mount(App, { global: { plugins: [router], stubs: { Chart: true } } });
expect(wrapper.findComponent(UserCard).props('id')).toBe(1);
```

drives the real tree and reads the DOM:

```ts
import { createMemoryHistory, createRouter } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';
import { flushPromises, mount } from '@usevibejs/ui/testing';
import { expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import App from './App.vibe';

vi.mock('./Chart.vibe', () => import('./test/ChartStub.vibe'));

const router = createRouter({ history: createMemoryHistory(), routes });
const wrapper = mount(App, { plugins: [router] });
await router.isReady();
await router.push('/users/1');
await flushPromises();
expect(wrapper.get('.user-card h2').text()).toBe('Ada');
```

## Where to go next

- [Routing](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/routing), [Testing components](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/testing) and [Data loading](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/data).

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/coming-from-vue-router

# Editor setup

`.vibe` files are type-checked by the TypeScript 7 language server (`tsc --lsp`). The server loads the project's `@usevibejs/language-tools`, a content mapper that turns each `.vibe` file into TypeScript, and maps every answer back to the exact position in the `.vibe` file. Hover, go to definition, find references, rename, completion and diagnostics work in the `<script setup>` block and in template expressions.

Every editor needs the same three things:

- the `contentMappers` entry in the tsconfig that includes the `.vibe` files (a new app has it):

  ```json
  {
    "contentMappers": [{ "package": "@usevibejs/language-tools", "extensions": [".vibe"] }]
  }
  ```

- `node` on the editor's `PATH`, because the server starts the content mapper with it;
- permission to run project code. The content mapper is project code, so the server runs it only when the editor passes `runExternalCode: true` in its initialization options. Enable it only for projects you trust.

Open the app root, the folder that contains `node_modules`, so that the server finds `@usevibejs/language-tools`.

## VS Code

Install two extensions (a new app recommends both in `.vscode/extensions.json`):

- **vibe.js** (`vibejs.vibejs`): highlighting and editing rules for `.vibe` files, and the hand-off of `.vibe` files to the TypeScript 7 extension;
- **TypeScript 7** (`TypeScriptTeam.native-preview`): the language server.

VS Code runs project code only in a trusted workspace. In Restricted Mode, `.vibe` files are highlighted but not type-checked, and the vibe.js extension shows [VIBE6102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6102). Trust the folder to turn type checking on.

## Neovim

Neovim 0.11 or later, with the built-in LSP client:

```lua
vim.filetype.add({ extension = { vibe = 'vibejs' } })
vim.lsp.config('tsc', {
  cmd = { 'node_modules/.bin/tsc', '--lsp', '--stdio' },
  init_options = { runExternalCode = true },
  filetypes = { 'typescript', 'typescriptreact', 'javascript', 'javascriptreact', 'vibejs' },
  root_markers = { 'tsconfig.json', 'package.json' },
})
vim.lsp.enable('tsc')
```

`init_options = { runExternalCode = true }` runs the project's content mapper: keep this configuration for projects you trust. The vibe.js test suite starts the language server with exactly this command and these options.

## Other LSP editors

Zed, Helix and other editors with an LSP client use the same setup:

- the command `node_modules/.bin/tsc --lsp --stdio`;
- the initialization options `{ "runExternalCode": true }`;
- a file type `vibejs` for the `.vibe` extension, handed to that server.

JetBrains IDEs are not supported: they do not load TypeScript content mappers.

## Known limitations

These come from the TypeScript language server and are tracked upstream.

- **Rename from the script does not update the template** ([#63879](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/63879)). Renaming a `<script setup>` binding edits the script only; the template keeps the old name, and the next type check reports it. Use find references first, or search and replace in the file. Renaming a tag, a prop key or an event name in the template is refused.
- **Auto-import completions** ([#64119](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/64119)). Completion in a `.vibe` file does not offer exports that the file does not import yet. Write the `import` yourself, or complete the name in a `.ts` file and copy the import.
- **Formatting** ([#64579](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/64579)). The language server does not format `.vibe` files. Format them with the app's formatter: `vibejs check` reports formatting problems.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem                                                                                  | Fix                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [VIBE6101](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6101): the TypeScript 7 extension is missing.                     | Install `TypeScriptTeam.native-preview` and reload the window.                                                                                                              |
| [VIBE6102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6102): the workspace is not trusted.                              | Trust the folder. In Restricted Mode the TypeScript 7 extension is off, so `.vibe` files are highlighted only.                                                              |
| [VIBE6002](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6002): the TypeScript host does not offer UTF-16 positions.       | Update `typescript` to the version that `@usevibejs/language-tools` supports.                                                                                               |
| [VIBE6010](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6010): an `<!-- @vibe-expect-error -->` suppresses no type error. | Remove the comment, or move it right before the element or interpolation whose error it expects.                                                                            |
| TS18068: content mappers require `--runExternalCode`.                                    | Run `tsc -b --runExternalCode` (`vibejs check` passes it). In an editor, pass `runExternalCode: true` in the initialization options.                                        |
| TS18099: the content mapper did not start.                                               | Run `pnpm install` so that `@usevibejs/language-tools` and its build are in `node_modules`, and make sure the editor finds `node` on its `PATH`.                            |
| TS18080: a problem in the code that the content mapper produced.                         | The `.vibe` file maps to invalid TypeScript, which is a vibe.js bug. Report it with the file at [github.com/vibejs/vibejs/issues](https://github.com/vibejs/vibejs/issues). |
| Diagnostics do not change after linking a local build of `@usevibejs/language-tools`.    | TypeScript caches the content mapper's output by package version. Run `tsc -b --force` once, and restart the language server.                                               |

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/editors

---

# Extending vibe.js

Everything an application uses to extend vibe.js is public API, so a feature can move from an app into a package without changes.

## Server

### Configurable modules

A module that needs options exposes a static `forRoot(options)` that returns a `DynamicModule`: the module class plus extra providers and exports. The options become a provider, so the module's own classes inject them:

```ts
export interface MailOptions {
  readonly from: string;
  readonly send: (message: { from: string; to: string; text: string }) => Promise<void>;
}

const MAIL_OPTIONS = token<MailOptions>('MailOptions');

export class Mailer {
  private readonly options = inject(MAIL_OPTIONS);

  send(to: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.options.send({ from: this.options.from, to, text });
  }
}

@Module({ providers: [Mailer], exports: [Mailer] })
export class MailModule {
  static forRoot(options: MailOptions): DynamicModule {
    return {
      module: MailModule,
      global: true,
      providers: [{ provide: MAIL_OPTIONS, useValue: options }],
    };
  }
}
```

An application imports `MailModule.forRoot({ ... })`. The providers, controllers, imports and exports of the returned object are added to those of `@Module()`. Each `forRoot()` call returns a new object, which is a separate module instance; import the result once and export it, or make it `global`, to share one instance. For options that come from other providers, provide them with `useFactory` and `inject` instead of `useValue`.

### Middleware packages

A middleware is a function, so a package exports a factory that takes options and returns a `Middleware`:

```ts
export function requireHeader(name: string): Middleware {
  return (req, next) => {
    if (!req.headers.has(name)) throw new HttpError(400, 'BAD_REQUEST', `Missing ${name}`);
    return next();
  };
}
```

The application adds it to `AppOptions.middleware`. An error thrown in a middleware is answered as a problem, like an error in a handler.

### Reusable guards, interceptors and filters

Enhancers are classes without constructor parameters that `inject()` what they need, so a package can export them next to a module that provides their dependencies. Configure them through an options token from `forRoot()`, as above, rather than through constructor arguments, which the container does not pass.

### Metadata

`createMetadata<T>(name)` gives a package a typed decorator and the key to read it back in its guards and interceptors with `ctx.getMetadata(key)`:

```ts
export const CacheFor = createMetadata<number>('cacheFor');

export class CacheHeaders implements Interceptor {
  async intercept(ctx: RequestContext, next: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
    const seconds = ctx.getMetadata(CacheFor);
    if (seconds !== undefined) ctx.responseHeaders.set('cache-control', `max-age=${seconds}`);
    return next();
  }
}
```

Applications then write `@CacheFor(60)` on a handler and register `CacheHeaders` globally or with `@UseInterceptors()`.

See [Modules and providers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/modules) and [Middleware, guards, interceptors and filters](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/pipeline) for the rules these building blocks follow.

## UI

### Plugins

A plugin is a function that receives the app, or an object with an `install(app)` method. `app.use(plugin, ...options)` installs it once, and checks the options against the plugin's `Plugin<Options>` type; a second call with the same plugin warns [VIBE5304](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5304) and does nothing. A plugin provides values to every component with `app.provide()`, and registers cleanup with `app.onUnmount()`.

The feature flags package of the example todo app exports a plugin factory: it takes options, loads the flags once, and provides them under a private injection key.

```ts
export interface FlagsPluginOptions {
  /** Where the API is mounted; `/api` by default. */
  baseUrl?: string;
  fetch?: ClientOptions['fetch'];
}

const FLAGS: InjectionKey<ShallowRef<Record<string, boolean>>> = Symbol('flags');

/** Loads the flags from `GET <baseUrl>/flags` once; until then, and after an error, every flag is off. */
export const flagsPlugin =
  (options: FlagsPluginOptions = {}): Plugin =>
  (app) => {
    const state = shallowRef<Record<string, boolean>>({});
    app.provide(FLAGS, state);
    const api = createClient(
      { flags },
      { baseUrl: options.baseUrl ?? '/api', fetch: options.fetch },
    );
    void api.flags.list().then((r) => {
      if (r.ok) state.value = r.data;
    });
  };
```

The application installs it next to the router:

```ts
createApp(App).use(flagsPlugin()).mount('#app');
```

### Provide and inject

`app.provide(key, value)` makes a value available to every component of the app; `provide(key, value)` in a component's setup makes it available to that component's descendants. `inject(key)` reads the nearest one, and `inject(key, fallback)` returns `fallback` when nothing provides `key`. Type keys with `InjectionKey<T>`, a symbol that carries the type of its value, so `inject()` returns that type.

### Composables

A composable is a function that setup calls to reuse stateful logic: it may read injections, create refs and computed values, and register lifecycle hooks of the calling component. The flags package reads its injection in a composable, so components never see the key, and an app without the plugin gets `false` for every flag:

```ts
/** Whether the flag `name` is on; always `false` in an app without `flagsPlugin()`. */
export function useFlag(name: string): Readonly<Ref<boolean>> {
  const state = inject(FLAGS, null);
  return computed(() => state?.value[name] === true);
}
```

A page then calls `useFlag('removeDone')` in its setup and uses the ref in its template.

### Limits

- There are no global components, custom directives, mixins or global properties: `app.component()`, `app.directive()` and `app.mixin()` throw [VIBE5301](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5301). Export components for import, element behavior as composables that take a template ref, and shared values through `app.provide()`.
- Packages that ship `.vibe` components are planned for v0.2. Until then, a package exports plugins, composables, injection keys and types.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/extending

---

# Getting started

A vibe.js app is one package with three parts: the UI, the server and the contracts between them. One command creates it, and one command checks all of it.

## Requirements

- Node.js `^24.15.0 || >=26`.
- A package manager: pnpm, npm, yarn or bun. The examples use pnpm.

## Create an app

```sh
pnpm create vibejs my-app
cd my-app
```

With another package manager, run `npm create vibejs@latest my-app`, `yarn create vibejs my-app` or `bun create vibejs my-app`. The scaffolder installs the dependencies with the package manager that ran it.

## Project layout

| Path         | What it holds                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `contracts/` | The API contracts: routes with their params, bodies, responses and errors. The UI and the server share them. |
| `server/`    | The server: modules, controllers that serve the contracts, and services.                                     |
| `ui/`        | The UI: `.vibe` components, pages, routes and the typed API client.                                          |
| `AGENTS.md`  | The rules and docs index for coding agents.                                                                  |

## Run it

```sh
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` serves the UI and the API on one port, the API under `/api`. Open the URL it prints: the home page shows the status that it loads from `/api/health`. UI changes reload in place, and server changes restart the server.

## Check it

```sh
pnpm vibejs check
```

`vibejs check` type-checks the TypeScript and the `.vibe` templates, lints, checks the formatting and runs the tests with coverage, all at once. It exits 0 when everything passes, and prints each problem with its file, line and column, and a link to its docs.

## Editor setup

Install the recommended VS Code extensions that the app lists in `.vscode/extensions.json`:

- **vibe.js** (`vibejs.vibejs`): syntax highlighting, and type checking, hover and go to definition in `.vibe` files.
- **TypeScript 7** (`TypeScriptTeam.native-preview`): the TypeScript language service that checks `.vibe` files through the app's `@usevibejs/language-tools`.
- **Oxc** (`oxc.oxc-vscode`): lint and format on save.

Type checking runs project code, so it needs a trusted workspace. Without the TypeScript 7 extension or trust, the editor shows [VIBE6101](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6101) or [VIBE6102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6102) and keeps highlighting.

For Neovim and other editors, the known limitations and troubleshooting, see [Editor setup](https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/editors).

## Coding agents

`AGENTS.md` holds a block of vibe.js rules for coding agents: the exact commands, the rules that agents get wrong most often, and an index of the docs that ship with the app in `node_modules/@usevibejs/cli/dist/docs`, so an agent reads the docs of the installed version. `vibejs agents sync` and `vibejs dev` keep the block current; write your own notes outside its markers. See [CLI and AI agents](https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/ai-agents).

## Next

Follow the [tutorial](https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/tutorial) to add an API resource and a page that shows it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/getting-started

---

# Tutorial

In this tutorial you add a `users` API to a new app, write a page that lists the users, let `vibejs check` catch a type error in a template, then build and serve the app. It takes about ten minutes. You need Node.js `^24.15.0 || >=26` and pnpm.

Every command and file on this page is run, in this order, by the vibe.js test suite on each change, so the steps work as written.

## 1. Create the app

```sh
pnpm create vibejs my-app
cd my-app
```

The app has three parts: `contracts/` for the API contracts, `server/` for the server and `ui/` for the UI. See [Getting started](https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/getting-started) for the layout and the editor setup.

## 2. Check it

```sh
pnpm vibejs check
```

`vibejs check` runs the type checker on the TypeScript and the `.vibe` templates, the linter, the format check and the tests with coverage. A new app passes with every file fully covered.

## 3. Generate a resource, a page and a component

```sh
pnpm vibejs g resource users
pnpm vibejs g page Users
pnpm vibejs g component UserCard
pnpm vibejs check
```

Each generator writes its files with tests, and registers them where they belong:

- `g resource users` writes the contract `contracts/src/users.contract.ts` with routes to list, get, create, update and remove users, and a server module with a controller, an in-memory service and a test. It adds the module to `server/src/app.module.ts` and the contract to the UI's API client in `ui/src/api.ts`.
- `g page Users` writes `ui/src/pages/UsersPage.vibe` with a test, and adds the route `/users` to `ui/src/routes.ts`.
- `g component UserCard` writes `ui/src/components/UserCard.vibe`, a component with a `title` prop, and its test.

A contract declares each route once, with its params, body, response and errors, and both sides are typed from it. The contract of the example todo app looks the same:

```ts
import { defineContract, del, get, patch, post } from '@usevibejs/contract';
import * as v from 'valibot';

export const Todo = v.object({ id: v.string(), title: v.string(), done: v.boolean() });

export const todos = defineContract('/todos', {
  list: get('/', { response: v.array(Todo) }),
  get: get('/:id', { response: Todo, errors: { TODO_NOT_FOUND: 404 } }),
  create: post('/', {
    body: v.object({ title: v.pipe(v.string(), v.trim(), v.minLength(1)) }),
    response: Todo,
  }),
  toggle: patch('/:id', { response: Todo, errors: { TODO_NOT_FOUND: 404 } }),
  remove: del('/:id', { errors: { TODO_NOT_FOUND: 404 } }),
});
```

The server handles each route of the contract with a typed handler ([Controllers and handlers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/handlers)), and the UI calls it through a typed client without code generation ([Contracts](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/contracts)). Generators never overwrite your changes: run one again and it skips the files that exist.

## 4. List the users

Make the page load the users from the API and show one `UserCard` per user, numbered. First, the test of the page: it mounts the app at `/users` with an API client whose `fetch` answers with one user.

```ts [ui/src/pages/UsersPage.test.ts]
import { createMemoryHistory, createRouter } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';
import { flushPromises, mount } from '@usevibejs/ui/testing';
import { expect, it } from 'vitest';
import App from '../App.vibe';
import { API, createApi } from '../api.ts';
import { routes } from '../routes.ts';

it('lists the users from the API at /users', async () => {
  const router = createRouter({ history: createMemoryHistory(), routes });
  const api = createApi(async () => Response.json([{ id: '1', name: 'Ada' }]));
  const wrapper = mount(App, { plugins: [router], provide: { [API]: api } });
  await router.push('/users');
  await flushPromises();
  expect(wrapper.get('h1').text()).toBe('Users');
  expect(wrapper.findAll('.user-card').map((card) => card.text())).toEqual(['1. Ada']);
});
```

Then the page. `useAsync` loads the list when the page mounts, and the client's result is either `{ ok: true, data }` or `{ ok: false, error }` ([Data loading](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/data)). This first version has a mistake:

```vibe [ui/src/pages/UsersPage.vibe]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, inject, useAsync } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import { API } from '../api.ts';
import UserCard from '../components/UserCard.vibe';

const api = inject(API)!;
// Loads the users on mount; a failed request shows an empty list.
const { data } = useAsync((signal) => api.users.list(undefined, { signal }));
const users = computed(() => (data.value?.ok ? data.value.data : []));
</script>

<template>
  <h1>Users</h1>
  <UserCard v-for="(user, index) in users" :key="user.id" :title="index + 1" />
</template>
```

## 5. Let check find the mistake

```sh exit=1
pnpm vibejs check
```

The check fails. Templates are type-checked like TypeScript, so the type error is reported at its line and column in the `.vibe` file. The page's test fails as well, because the card shows `1`:

```txt
ui/src/pages/UsersPage.vibe:14:60  error  TS2322  Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string'.
ui/src/pages/UsersPage.test.ts:8:1  error  test-failed  AssertionError: expected [ '1' ] to deeply equal [ '1. Ada' ]
```

`title` is a `string` prop and `index + 1` is a number. Your editor shows the same error while you type. Pass a string:

```vibe [ui/src/pages/UsersPage.vibe]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, inject, useAsync } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import { API } from '../api.ts';
import UserCard from '../components/UserCard.vibe';

const api = inject(API)!;
// Loads the users on mount; a failed request shows an empty list.
const { data } = useAsync((signal) => api.users.list(undefined, { signal }));
const users = computed(() => (data.value?.ok ? data.value.data : []));
</script>

<template>
  <h1>Users</h1>
  <UserCard v-for="(user, index) in users" :key="user.id" :title="`${index + 1}. ${user.name}`" />
</template>
```

```sh
pnpm vibejs check
```

The check passes again, tests and full coverage included.

## 6. Build and serve

```sh
pnpm vibejs build
pnpm start
```

`vibejs build` writes the UI to `ui/dist` and the server to `server/dist/main.js`. `pnpm start` runs the built server on port 3000, or on the port in `PORT`: `/api/health` answers `{"status":"ok"}` and `/api/users` answers the list of users, empty for now. Stop it with Ctrl+C. The two outputs are deployed separately: the UI as static files, the server as a Node.js process ([Deploying](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/#deploying)).

## 7. Develop

```sh
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` serves the UI and the API on one port and prints its URL; open `/users` on it. Keep it running while you work:

- Edit `ui/src/components/UserCard.vibe`, for example its markup: the page updates in place and keeps its state.
- Edit a file under `server/`, for example the service: the server restarts in well under a second and the next request reaches the new code.
- Errors of the build, the browser and the server go to `.vibejs/dev.log`; `pnpm vibejs errors` lists them.

A second `pnpm dev` in the same app reports the running server instead of starting another one.

## Next

- [Routing](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/routing) and [Testing components](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/testing) for the UI.
- [Server](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/) and [Modules and providers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/modules) for the server.
- [CLI and AI agents](https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/ai-agents) to let a coding agent work on the app with the same commands.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/tutorial

# UI essentials

The UI of a vibe.js app is made of components written in `.vibe` files and the reactive state they read. Everything a component imports comes from `@usevibejs/ui`; the compiler and the language tools type-check the script and the template together.

## A component

A `.vibe` file has up to three blocks: the setup script, the template and the scoped styles.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const { label = 'Count' } = defineProps<{ label?: string }>();

const count = ref(0);
const doubled = computed(() => count.value * 2);
</script>

<template>
  <button type="button" @click="count++">{{ label }}: {{ count }} (twice: {{ doubled }})</button>
</template>

<style scoped>
button {
  font-weight: 600;
}
</style>
```

- `<script setup lang="ts">` runs once for each instance of the component. Its top-level bindings and imports are available in the template, and refs are unwrapped there: the template writes `count`, the script writes `count.value`.
- `<template>` describes the DOM. It is compiled to code that creates the elements once and updates only the text, attributes and lists that read changed state.
- `<style scoped>` applies only to the elements of this component.

`defineProps` and the other `define*` calls are compiler macros: they are available without an import. [Components](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components) lists them.

## Mounting the app

`createApp()` takes the root component; `mount()` renders it into an element or the element a selector matches, replacing its content.

```ts
const app = createApp(App);

app.config.errorHandler = (err, instance, info) => {
  console.error(`Error in ${instance?.name ?? 'the app'} (${info})`, err);
};
app.config.warnHandler = (message, instance, trace) => {
  console.warn(message, trace);
};

app.mount('#app');
```

In a real app, `App` is the default import of `./App.vibe`.

- `errorHandler` receives every error that no `onErrorCaptured` hook stopped: errors thrown in setup, in a render, in a watcher, in an event handler or in a lifecycle hook. `info` names the source, such as `'setup function'` or `'native event handler'`. Without a handler, the error is logged as [VIBE5102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5102).
- `warnHandler` receives the development warnings instead of the console, with the trace of component names. Warnings are not emitted in production builds.
- `app.unmount()` unmounts the root component and removes its nodes.

## Hot updates

In development, saving a `.vibe` file updates the running page without a reload:

- An edit of the template re-renders each instance of the component and keeps its setup state. Child components rendered by that template are created again, so their own state starts over.
- An edit of the script mounts the component again, with new state.

## Where to go next

- [Reactivity](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/reactivity): `ref`, `reactive`, `computed`, `watch` and the other primitives.
- [Template syntax](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/template-syntax): interpolation, bindings, events, conditions, lists, `v-model` and template refs.
- [Components](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components): props, events, slots, models, attributes and exposed values.
- [Lifecycle](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/lifecycle): the lifecycle hooks, their order and error handling.
- [Provide and inject](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/provide-inject): passing values down the component tree.
- [Extending vibe.js](https://vibejs.org/v0/guides/extending): plugins and composables.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/

---

# Components

A component is a `.vibe` file. Its default export is imported where it is used, and its tag is written in PascalCase. There are no globally registered components.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import TodoItem from './TodoItem.vibe';
</script>

<template>
  <ul>
    <TodoItem title="Write docs" />
  </ul>
</template>
```

A kebab-case tag such as `<todo-item>` is an element, not a component ([VIBE2002](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2002)), and a tag that names no import is reported as [VIBE2001](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2001).

The macros below declare the interface of a component. They are available in `<script setup lang="ts">` without an import and take their declarations as type arguments, so the parent's template is type-checked against them.

## Props

`defineProps<Props>()` declares the props. Destructuring the result gives each prop a local name, and a default after `=` applies when the parent passes `undefined` or nothing.

```vibe [TodoItem.vibe]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const { title, done = false, tags = [] } = defineProps<{
  title: string;
  done?: boolean;
  tags?: string[];
}>();

const label = computed(() => `${title} (${tags.length} tags)`);
</script>

<template>
  <li :class="{ done }">{{ label }}</li>
</template>
```

- Props are read-only: assigning one is reported as [VIBE3106](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3106). Use a [model](#v-model) or emit an event to change a value of the parent.
- An optional boolean prop that the parent does not pass is `undefined`, and an attribute without a value, as in `<TodoItem done />`, passes `true`.
- A default is a literal or reads imports; it cannot read the bindings of the script ([VIBE3105](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3105)). An object or array default is created for each instance.
- Without destructuring, `const props = defineProps<Props>()` gives an object, and `props.title` reads a prop.

### Reading props

A destructured prop is not a copy: each read calls into the parent and evaluates the expression the parent bound, so it always sees the current value. Put an expensive derivation in a `computed`, as `label` above, so it runs only when its inputs change. To pass a prop to a function that tracks its argument, such as `watch` or `toRef`, pass a getter: `watch(() => title, ...)` ([VIBE3107](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3107)).

## Events

`defineEmits<Events>()` declares the events as a record whose keys are the event names and whose values are the payload tuples. The returned function emits them.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
const { id } = defineProps<{ id: number }>();
const emit = defineEmits<{
  remove: [id: number];
  rename: [id: number, title: string];
}>();
</script>

<template>
  <button type="button" @click="emit('remove', id)">Remove</button>
  <button type="button" @click="emit('rename', id, 'Untitled')">Reset title</button>
</template>
```

The parent listens with `@remove="handler"`. The handler receives the payload, not a DOM event, so event modifiers do not apply to component events ([VIBE2305](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2305)). Emitting an event that is not declared warns VIBE5202 in development.

## Slots

A component renders content from its parent where it places `<slot>`. Named slots take a `name`, and attributes on `<slot>` are passed to the parent as slot props. `defineSlots<Slots>()` declares the slots and their props.

```vibe [ItemList.vibe]
<script setup lang="ts">
defineSlots<{
  default?: (props: { item: string; index: number }) => unknown;
  header?: (props: {}) => unknown;
}>();

const { items } = defineProps<{ items: string[] }>();
</script>

<template>
  <section>
    <header><slot name="header">Items</slot></header>
    <ul>
      <li v-for="(item, index) in items" :key="item">
        <slot :item="item" :index="index">{{ item }}</slot>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </section>
</template>
```

The parent passes slot content with `<template #name>` and receives the slot props with `#name="props"`. Content outside named templates is the default slot.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import ItemList from './ItemList.vibe';
</script>

<template>
  <ItemList :items="['a', 'b']">
    <template #header>Letters</template>
    <template #default="{ item, index }">{{ index }}: {{ item.toUpperCase() }}</template>
  </ItemList>
</template>
```

Slot names are static ([VIBE2605](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2605)); to choose between slots, put `v-if` on the slot templates.

### Fallback content

The children of `<slot>` render when the parent passes no content for that slot. A slot that the parent passes renders the parent's content, even when that content renders nothing, such as a `v-if` that is false. To show the fallback in that case, put the condition on the `<template #name>` itself, so the slot is not passed.

### Slots in script

`useSlots()` returns the slots the component received, and `$slots` reads them in the template. Use them to test whether a slot was passed, as in `v-if="$slots.header"`. Calling a slot function renders its content and creates its DOM nodes, so a slot is only called by `<slot>`, not to inspect what it contains.

## v-model

`defineModel()` declares a two-way value. Reading the returned ref reads the prop, and assigning it emits the update event to the parent.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = defineModel<string>({ required: true });
const open = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: () => false });
</script>

<template>
  <input v-model="text" />
  <button type="button" @click="open = !open">{{ open ? 'Hide' : 'Show' }}</button>
</template>
```

The parent binds the default model with `v-model="text"` and a named one with `v-model:open="visible"`. `v-model` is the `modelValue` prop plus the `onUpdate:modelValue` event, and `v-model:open` is `open` plus `onUpdate:open`. Without `required` or a `default`, the model's type includes `undefined`. A model whose parent binds nothing keeps a local value.

## Attributes

Attributes and listeners that a parent passes but the component does not declare as props or events are its attributes. When the component renders a single root element, they are added to it: `class` and `style` are merged with the root's own, and listeners are added next to the root's. When the root is another component, they pass on to that component.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useAttrs } from '@usevibejs/ui';

defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false });
const { label } = defineProps<{ label: string }>();
const attrs = useAttrs();
console.log(Object.keys(attrs));
</script>

<template>
  <label>
    {{ label }}
    <input v-bind="$attrs" />
  </label>
</template>
```

`defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })` keeps the attributes off the root, so that `v-bind="$attrs"` can place them on another element. `useAttrs()` returns them in the script. A component with several root elements does not receive attributes and warns VIBE5201 in development when it is passed some.

## Exposing values

A template ref on a component holds the values the component passes to `defineExpose()`, with refs unwrapped. Nothing else of the component is reachable: not its props, not its other bindings and not its elements.

```vibe [SearchField.vibe]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, useTemplateRef } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const field = useTemplateRef<HTMLInputElement>('field');
const text = ref('');

defineExpose({
  focus: () => field.value?.focus(),
  clear: () => (text.value = ''),
});
</script>

<template>
  <input ref="field" v-model="text" />
</template>
```

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, useTemplateRef } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import SearchField from './SearchField.vibe';

const search = useTemplateRef('search');
onMounted(() => search.value?.focus());
</script>

<template>
  <SearchField ref="search" />
</template>
```

The ref's type is the exposed object of `SearchField`, so `search.value?.focus()` is checked. A component that calls no `defineExpose()` exposes an empty object.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components

---

# Data loading

`useAsync()` from `@usevibejs/ui` loads data in a component and keeps it current. Together with the typed API client, every request is aborted when it is no longer needed, and every outcome, failures included, is a typed value.

## useAsync

`useAsync(fn)` calls `fn(signal)` right away and returns four values:

- `data`: a ref with the value that the last run resolved to, or `undefined` before the first one finished.
- `error`: a ref with what the last run threw, or `undefined`.
- `loading`: a ref that is `true` while a run is in progress.
- `refresh()`: runs `fn` again; the promise resolves once that run is over and never rejects.

The todo page of the example app loads one todo by the id in the URL:

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { inject, useAsync } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import { useRoute } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';
import { API } from '../api.ts';

const api = inject(API)!;
const route = useRoute('todo');
const { data: todo } = useAsync((signal) =>
  api.todos.get({ params: { id: route.params.id } }, { signal }),
);
</script>

<template>
  <section>
    <h1 v-if="todo?.ok">{{ todo.data.title }}</h1>
    <p v-else-if="todo" class="error">{{ todo.error.code }}</p>
  </section>
</template>
```

`API` is the injection key under which the app provides its client.

`loading` and `refresh()` show progress and load again on demand:

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useAsync } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const { data, loading, refresh } = useAsync(async (signal) => {
  const res = await fetch('/api/health', { signal });
  return (await res.json()) as { status: string };
});
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="loading">Loading…</p>
  <p v-else>Status: {{ data?.status ?? 'unknown' }}</p>
  <button type="button" :disabled="loading" @click="refresh()">Reload</button>
</template>
```

## Tracking and reruns

`fn` runs again when a reactive value that it read **before its first `await`** changes. Above, `route.params.id` is read synchronously, so moving from `/todos/1` to `/todos/2` loads the new todo while the page stays on screen. A value read after an `await` is not tracked: read every input first, then await.

```ts
const query = ref('');
const page = ref(1);

const results = useAsync(async (signal) => {
  const q = query.value; // tracked
  const p = page.value; // tracked
  return search(q, p, signal);
});
```

## Aborting

Each run gets its own `AbortSignal`. When a new run starts, the previous signal aborts; when the component unmounts, the current one aborts. Pass the signal to the client call, `{ signal }`, or to `fetch`, so that the request stops. An aborted run never writes `data`, `error` or `loading`, so a slow response can never overwrite a newer one.

`useAsync()` belongs in setup or in a composable that setup calls; it needs a component or an effect scope that owns it ([VIBE7301](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7301)).

## Typed results

The API client never rejects for an HTTP or network failure: each call resolves to a result that is either `{ ok: true, data }` or `{ ok: false, error }`. So with the client, failures arrive in `data`, and `error` holds only real bugs, such as an exception in `fn`.

Narrow on `ok` before reading the payload: in the template with `v-if="data?.ok"`, and in the script with `data.value?.ok`.

```ts
const { data } = useAsync((signal) => health({ signal }));

const status = computed(() =>
  data.value?.ok ? data.value.data.status : (data.value?.error.code ?? 'checking'),
);
```

`error.code` is one of the codes that the route declares in its contract, or a client code such as `NETWORK_ERROR`, so a `switch` over it is checked by TypeScript.

## Shared state

State that several components read, such as the signed-in user or a cart, lives in a module: create it once at module scope and expose it through a composable.

```ts
import { computed, readonly, ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

interface Item {
  id: number;
  price: number;
}

const items = ref<Item[]>([]);
```
