```ts
const total = computed(() => items.value.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0));

export function useCart() {
  return {
    items: readonly(items),
    total,
    add(item: Item) {
      items.value.push(item);
    },
    clear() {
      items.value = [];
    },
  };
}
```

Every component that calls `useCart()` reads and changes the same state, and the template unwraps the refs as usual. Keep the writes in the composable's functions, so that every change goes through one place. In tests, reset the state with `clear()` in a `beforeEach`, because the module stays loaded between tests of the same file.

For state that belongs to one part of the tree, or that a test must replace, provide it with `provide()` and read it with `inject()` instead.

## See also

- [Routing](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/routing): params, guards and lazy pages.
- [Testing components](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/testing#waiting-for-async-work): `flushPromises()` after data loads.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/data

---

# Lifecycle

A component's setup runs once, when the component is created. The lifecycle hooks register functions that run at later points. They are called during setup, synchronously: a hook called anywhere else, such as after an `await`, warns VIBE5205.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, onUpdated, ref, useTemplateRef } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const box = useTemplateRef<HTMLDivElement>('box');
const width = ref(0);
const observer = new ResizeObserver(([entry]) => (width.value = entry?.contentRect.width ?? 0));

onMounted(() => {
  if (box.value) observer.observe(box.value);
});
onUpdated(() => console.log('rendered', width.value));
onBeforeUnmount(() => observer.disconnect());
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="box">{{ width }}px wide</div>
</template>
```

## The hooks

| Hook              | Runs                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onBeforeMount`   | after the component's DOM is created, before it is inserted into the document |
| `onMounted`       | after the DOM is inserted; template refs are set                              |
| `onBeforeUpdate`  | before a state change updates the component's DOM                             |
| `onUpdated`       | after the update, once per batch of changes                                   |
| `onBeforeUnmount` | before the component is removed; the DOM and template refs are still there    |
| `onUnmounted`     | after the component is removed and its watchers are stopped                   |
| `onErrorCaptured` | when a descendant throws; see [Errors](#errors)                               |

Effects that set up something outside the component, such as listeners on `window`, a timer or an observer, start in `onMounted` and stop in `onBeforeUnmount` or `onUnmounted`. Watchers and computed values created in setup stop by themselves. `onScopeDispose()` registers a cleanup that runs at unmount too, and also works in composables called outside a component.

## Hook order

- **Mounting:** each component creates its DOM, then runs `onBeforeMount`, then inserts the DOM. A child creates and inserts its DOM while its parent builds its own, so a child's `onBeforeMount` and `onMounted` run before its parent's. When `onMounted` runs, the whole subtree is in the document.
- **Updating:** a state change re-runs only the bindings that read it, in a batch before the browser paints. `onBeforeUpdate` and `onUpdated` run for each component whose template bindings run in that batch.
- **Unmounting:** a parent's `onBeforeUnmount` runs before its children's; `onUnmounted` hooks run after the DOM is removed.

`onBeforeMount` runs after the DOM is built, so template refs already point at the elements, which are not yet in the document: they have no layout and no size.

## Errors

An error thrown in setup, in a template binding, in a watcher, in an event handler or in a hook travels up the component tree:

1. Each ancestor's `onErrorCaptured(err, instance, info)` hook runs, nearest first. `instance` is the component where the error happened and `info` names the source, such as `'render effect'` or `'native event handler'`. Returning `false` stops the error there.
2. If no hook stopped it, `app.config.errorHandler` receives it.
3. Without an `errorHandler`, the error is logged as [VIBE5102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5102), with the component trace in development.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onErrorCaptured, ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import Chart from './Chart.vibe';

const failed = ref(false);

onErrorCaptured((err, instance, info) => {
  console.warn(`${instance?.name ?? 'A component'} failed in ${info}`, err);
  failed.value = true;
  return false;
});
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="failed">The chart is not available.</p>
  <Chart v-else />
</template>
```

A component whose setup or render throws renders nothing, and the rest of the page keeps working. Setup cannot be `async`, and `<script setup>` cannot `await` at the top level ([VIBE3002](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3002), [VIBE5204](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5204)): start the work in setup and store the result in a ref when it arrives.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/lifecycle

---

# Provide and inject

`provide(key, value)` makes a value available to every descendant of a component, and `inject(key)` reads the value of the nearest ancestor that provided `key`. The components in between do not pass it along as props.

## Typed keys

An `InjectionKey<T>` is a symbol that carries the type of its value, so `provide()` checks the value and `inject()` returns `T`. Export the key from a `.ts` module that both sides import:

```ts [theme.ts]
import { inject, type InjectionKey, type Ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

export interface Theme {
  mode: Ref<'light' | 'dark'>;
  toggle: () => void;
}

export const ThemeKey: InjectionKey<Theme> = Symbol('theme');

/** The nearest provided theme; `undefined` without a provider. */
export const useTheme = (): Theme | undefined => inject(ThemeKey);
```

The provider creates the value in its setup:

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { provide, ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import Toolbar from './Toolbar.vibe';
import { ThemeKey } from './theme.ts';

const mode = ref<'light' | 'dark'>('light');
provide(ThemeKey, {
  mode,
  toggle: () => (mode.value = mode.value === 'light' ? 'dark' : 'light'),
});
</script>

<template>
  <main :class="mode">
    <Toolbar />
  </main>
</template>
```

Any descendant injects it, here through the `useTheme()` composable of `theme.ts`:

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTheme } from './theme.ts';

const theme = useTheme();
</script>

<template>
  <button v-if="theme" type="button" @click="theme.toggle()">{{ theme.mode.value }}</button>
</template>
```

Provide a ref or a reactive object, as `mode` above, when descendants should see changes. A string key works too, but its value is not typed.

## Defaults

Without a provider, `inject(key)` returns `undefined` and warns VIBE5206 in development. A default makes the value required:

```ts
// A default value.
const locale = inject(LocaleKey, ref('en'));

// A factory, called only when nothing is provided.
const fallback = inject(LocaleKey, () => ref(navigator.language), true);
console.log(locale.value, fallback.value);
```

The third argument, `true`, tells `inject()` to call the default instead of returning the function itself.

## App-level values

`app.provide(key, value)` provides a value to every component of the app. A component's `provide()` of the same key takes precedence for its descendants.

```ts
const app = createApp(App);
app.provide(LocaleKey, ref('en'));
app.mount('#app');
```

## Outside setup

`provide()` and `inject()` work during a component's setup. `hasInjectionContext()` returns whether `inject()` can be called at that point, which lets a composable fail with a clear message or fall back. `app.runWithContext(fn)` runs `fn` with the app as the injection context, so code outside any component, such as a router guard or a test, can read the app's values:

```ts
const app = createApp(App).provide(LocaleKey, ref('de'));

const locale = app.runWithContext(() => {
  console.log(hasInjectionContext()); // true
  return inject(LocaleKey);
});
console.log(locale?.value); // 'de'
```

## UI and server

`inject(key)` in a component reads values provided in the component tree. It is unrelated to the server's field `inject(Token)` of `@usevibejs/server`, which resolves providers from the dependency injection container of a module. The two never share values.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/provide-inject

---

# Reactivity

Reactive values record who reads them. When a value changes, the computed values, watchers and template bindings that read it run again, and nothing else does. All of these functions are imported from `@usevibejs/ui`.

## ref

`ref()` holds one value in `.value`. An object value is made deeply reactive, so changes to its nested properties are tracked too.

```ts
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const count = ref(0);
count.value++;

const user = ref({ name: 'Ada', tags: ['admin'] });
user.value.tags.push('editor'); // tracked
```

`ref<T>()` without an argument holds `T | undefined`. In a template, and in a `reactive()` object, a ref is unwrapped: the template writes `count`, not `count.value`.

## shallowRef

`shallowRef()` tracks only the assignment of `.value`. Use it for large values that are replaced rather than changed in place, and for objects that must stay plain, such as class instances of a library.

```ts
import { shallowRef, triggerRef } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const rows = shallowRef<number[]>([]);
rows.value = [...rows.value, 1]; // tracked

rows.value.push(2); // not tracked
triggerRef(rows); // runs what reads rows now
```

`markRaw(object)` keeps an object plain wherever it is stored, even inside reactive state.

## reactive and readonly

`reactive()` returns a deeply reactive proxy of an object, an array, a `Map` or a `Set`. Nested refs are unwrapped when read.

```ts
import { reactive, readonly, ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const state = reactive({ count: ref(0), items: new Map<string, number>() });
state.count++; // no .value: the nested ref is unwrapped
state.items.set('a', 1);

const view = readonly(state);
// view.count++ fails to type-check, and warns VIBE5002 at runtime
```

- A proxy is not the original object: compare with `toRaw(value)` when identity matters.
- Replacing a whole `reactive()` object loses the connection; keep it in a `ref()` instead, or change its properties.
- `shallowReactive()` and `shallowReadonly()` apply only to the top-level properties.
- `isRef()`, `isReactive()`, `isReadonly()`, `isShallow()` and `isProxy()` test a value.

## computed

`computed()` derives a value from other reactive values. It runs only when read after one of its sources changed, and its result is cached until then.

```ts
import { computed, ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const first = ref('Ada');
const last = ref('Lovelace');

const full = computed(() => `${first.value} ${last.value}`);

const editable = computed({
  get: () => `${first.value} ${last.value}`,
  set(value: string) {
    [first.value = '', last.value = ''] = value.split(' ');
  },
});
editable.value = 'Grace Hopper';
```

A computed with only a getter is readonly. The getter receives the previous value, which helps return the same object when nothing relevant changed. A getter should not change state; use a watcher for that.

## watch

`watch(source, callback, options?)` calls `callback(value, oldValue, onCleanup)` when the source changes. A source is a ref, a computed, a getter, a reactive object or an array of these.

```ts
import { reactive, ref, watch } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const query = ref('');
const filters = reactive({ done: false });

watch(query, (value, oldValue) => {
  console.log(`query: ${oldValue} -> ${value}`);
});

// A getter watches part of an object.
watch(
  () => filters.done,
  (done) => console.log(done),
);

// An array watches several sources.
watch([query, () => filters.done], ([text, done]) => console.log(text, done));

// A reactive object is watched deeply.
watch(filters, (value) => console.log(value.done));
```

The options:

- `immediate: true` calls the callback once right away, with `undefined` as the old value.
- `deep: true` tracks nested values of a ref or getter source; a number tracks that many levels.
- `once: true` stops the watcher after the first call.
- `flush` sets when the callback runs: `'pre'` (the default) before the DOM updates, `'post'` after them, `'sync'` inside the assignment.

The returned handle stops the watcher when called, and has `stop()`, `pause()` and `resume()`. A watcher created in a component's setup stops when the component unmounts.

## watchEffect

`watchEffect(effect)` runs `effect` now and again whenever something it read changes. `watchPostEffect()` and `watchSyncEffect()` are the `'post'` and `'sync'` flush forms.

```ts
import { onWatcherCleanup, ref, watchEffect } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const id = ref(1);

watchEffect(() => {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  void fetch(`/api/items/${id.value}`, { signal: controller.signal });
  // Runs before the effect runs again, and when it stops.
  onWatcherCleanup(() => controller.abort());
});
```

`onWatcherCleanup()` registers a cleanup for the running watcher or effect. The `onCleanup` argument of the callback does the same and also works after an `await`.

## Effect scopes

Watchers and computed values created during `scope.run()` belong to the scope, and `scope.stop()` stops them all. A component's setup runs in its own scope, so most code never creates one. Use `effectScope()` for state that lives outside a component.

```ts
import { effectScope, onScopeDispose, ref, watch } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const scope = effectScope();

scope.run(() => {
  const width = ref(window.innerWidth);
  const update = () => (width.value = window.innerWidth);
  window.addEventListener('resize', update);
  onScopeDispose(() => window.removeEventListener('resize', update));
  watch(width, (value) => console.log(value));
});

scope.stop(); // stops the watcher and removes the listener
```

`onScopeDispose()` registers a cleanup on the current scope; in a component, it runs when the component unmounts. `getCurrentScope()` returns the current scope.

## nextTick

State changes update the DOM in a batch, before the browser paints. `await nextTick()` waits until the pending updates are applied.

```ts
import { nextTick, ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const open = ref(false);

async function show(): Promise<void> {
  open.value = true;
  await nextTick();
  document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#search')?.focus();
}
```

## toRef, toRefs and toValue

These convert between refs, getters and plain values:

```ts
import { computed, reactive, toRef, toRefs, toValue, type MaybeRefOrGetter } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const state = reactive({ x: 0, y: 0 });

const x = toRef(state, 'x'); // a ref that reads and writes state.x
const { y } = toRefs(state); // a ref for every property
const label = toRef(() => `(${state.x}, ${state.y})`); // a readonly ref of a getter
x.value++;
y.value++;

// A function that accepts a value, a ref or a getter.
function useDouble(input: MaybeRefOrGetter<number>) {
  return computed(() => toValue(input) * 2);
}
console.log(useDouble(x).value, useDouble(() => state.y).value, useDouble(2).value, label.value);
```

`unref(value)` returns the value of a ref and any other value as it is.

## Shared state

A composable is a function that creates and returns reactive state. State created at module scope, outside any function, is shared by every component that imports it:

```ts
import { computed, ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

interface Item {
  id: number;
  title: string;
}

// One cart for the whole app.
const items = ref<Item[]>([]);

export function useCart() {
  const count = computed(() => items.value.length);
  const add = (item: Item) => items.value.push(item);
  return { items, count, add };
}
```

Each call of `useCart()` returns the same `items`. Put the state inside the function instead to give each caller its own. For state that only part of the tree should share, [provide it](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/provide-inject).

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/reactivity

---

# Routing

The router maps the URL to a chain of route records and renders their components. It comes from `@usevibejs/ui/router`, and its types follow your routes: route names, params and links are checked by TypeScript, in scripts and in templates.

## Routes

Routes live in one file, `ui/src/routes.ts`. `defineRoutes()` returns the array unchanged and keeps its literal names and paths, which type the router.

```ts
export const routes = defineRoutes([
  { path: '/', name: 'home', component: HomePage },
  {
    path: '/users',
    component: UsersLayout,
    children: [
      { path: '', name: 'users', component: UserList },
      { path: ':id(\\d+)', name: 'user', component: () => import('./pages/UserPage.vibe') },
    ],
  },
  { path: '/people', redirect: { name: 'users' } },
  { path: '/:pathMatch(.*)*', name: 'not-found', component: NotFound },
]);
```

In the app, `HomePage` and the other components are default imports of `.vibe` files.

A record takes `path`, `name`, `component`, `props`, `children`, `redirect`, `meta` and `beforeEnter`. Any other key fails at startup with [VIBE7103](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7103), so a misspelled option is never ignored. Names are unique ([VIBE7102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7102)).

## Creating the router

`createRouter()` takes the history, the routes and an optional `scrollBehavior`. `app.use(router)` installs it and starts the first navigation.

```ts
const router = createRouter({ history: createWebHistory(), routes });

declare module '@usevibejs/ui/router' {
  interface Register {
    router: typeof router;
  }
}

createApp(App).use(router).mount('#app');
```

- `createWebHistory(base?)` uses the browser's URL and history. Pass `base` when the app is served under a path, such as `'/app'`.
- `createMemoryHistory(base?)` keeps the history in memory: for tests and for environments without a window ([VIBE7117](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7117)).

The `Register` declaration types every router API with your routes: `useRoute()`, `useRouter()`, `router.push()`, guards and the `to` of `RouterLink`. Declare it once per app, next to `createRouter()`.

## RouterView and RouterLink

`RouterView` renders the component of the matched record, and a `RouterView` inside that component renders the matched child. `RouterLink` renders an `<a>` that navigates inside the app. Both are imported where they are used; there are no global components.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { RouterLink, RouterView } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';
</script>

<template>
  <nav>
    <RouterLink to="/">Home</RouterLink>
    <RouterLink :to="{ name: 'user', params: { id: 42 } }">User 42</RouterLink>
  </nav>
  <main>
    <RouterView />
  </main>
</template>
```

- `to` is a path or a location object: `{ name, params, query, hash }` or `{ path, query, hash }`. A name that does not exist, a missing param or a param of the wrong type is a type error in the template.
- `replace` replaces the current history entry instead of adding one.
- The link gets the class `router-link-active` while its route is part of the current route, and `router-link-exact-active` and `aria-current="page"` while it is the current route. `activeClass`, `exactActiveClass` and `ariaCurrentValue` change them.
- Clicks with a modifier key, with the middle button, or on a link with `target="_blank"` are left to the browser.
- `to` is always a location inside the app. Use a plain `<a href>` for other sites ([VIBE7114](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7114)).
- `RouterView` takes no slot content ([VIBE7115](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7115)).

When a link needs other markup, build it with `useLink()`. It returns `href`, `isActive`, `isExactActive`, the resolved `route`, and `navigate(event)`, which applies the same click rules:

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useLink, type RouteLocationRaw } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';

const props = defineProps<{ to: RouteLocationRaw; label: string }>();
const { href, isActive, navigate } = useLink({ to: () => props.to });
</script>

<template>
  <li :class="{ selected: isActive }">
    <a :href="href" @click="navigate">{{ label }}</a>
  </li>
</template>
```

## Reading the route

`useRoute()` returns the current route; it is reactive, so templates and computed values that read it update on every navigation. `useRouter()` returns the router.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import { useRoute, useRouter } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';

const route = useRoute('user');
const router = useRouter();
const id = computed(() => Number(route.params.id));
</script>

<template>
  <h1>User {{ id }}</h1>
  <button type="button" @click="router.push({ name: 'user', params: { id: id + 1 } })">
    Next
  </button>
</template>
```

`useRoute('user')` types `params` by the `user` route. It throws [VIBE7113](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7113) when that route is not part of the current route, so call it only in the page of that route and its children. A route has `path`, `fullPath`, `name`, `params`, `query`, `hash`, `matched`, `meta` and `redirectedFrom`.

When the same page stays on screen for another param, such as from `/users/1` to `/users/2`, the component instance is kept: read the params reactively instead of copying them once in setup.

### Params as props

With `props: true` on a record, the page receives the params as props. Type them with `RouteParams`:

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { RouteParams } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';

const { id } = defineProps<RouteParams<'user'>>();
</script>

<template>
  <h1>User {{ id }}</h1>
</template>
```

`props` also takes an object of fixed props, or a function from the route to the props.

## Paths and params

A path is a list of segments separated by `/`. Each segment is static text or exactly one param ([VIBE7101](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7101)):

| Segment    | Matches                            | Param type         |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `:id`      | one segment                        | `string`           |
| `:id(\d+)` | one segment that matches the regex | `string`           |
| `:id?`     | an optional segment                | `string`, optional |
| `:parts+`  | one or more segments               | `string[]`         |
| `:parts*`  | zero or more segments              | `string[]`         |

Paths match case-insensitively, a trailing slash is optional, and the most specific path wins regardless of the order of the records. When you navigate, params also accept numbers. `/:pathMatch(.*)*` matches every path that no other route matches.

## Navigating

`router.push(to)` and `router.replace(to)` take the same locations as `RouterLink`. They resolve once the navigation is over: with `undefined` when it succeeded, or with a navigation failure when a guard cancelled it, a newer navigation replaced it, or the target is the current route. They reject only when a guard, a redirect or a lazy loader throws, after the error reached `router.onError()`.

```ts
const failure = await router.push({ path: '/users', query: { page: '2' } });
if (isNavigationFailure(failure, NavigationFailureType.aborted)) {
  console.log('A guard kept the current page.');
}
```

`router.back()`, `router.forward()` and `router.go(delta)` move through the history. `router.resolve(to)` returns the route and its `href` without navigating.

## Guards

A guard receives `to` and `from` and decides with its return value:

- nothing or `true`: continue;
- `false`: cancel, and stay on the current route;
- a location: redirect there.

A guard may be async. It never takes a third parameter ([VIBE7107](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7107)).

```ts
router.beforeEach((to) => {
  if (to.meta.requiresAuth && !isSignedIn())
    return { path: '/login', query: { next: to.fullPath } };
});
```

The guards of one navigation run in this order, each after the previous one finished:

1. `onBeforeRouteLeave` of the pages that are leaving, innermost first.
2. `router.beforeEach`.
3. `onBeforeRouteUpdate` of the pages that stay.
4. `beforeEnter` of the entering records.
5. The lazy components of the entering records load.
6. `router.beforeResolve`.

Then the route changes, the views render, and `router.afterEach(to, from, failure?)` runs. Guards, redirects, loaders and hooks run in the app's injection context, so they can call `inject()` for values that the app provides. A guard that throws cancels the navigation; the error reaches `router.onError()`, or the console when no handler is registered.

A page guards its own route with `onBeforeRouteLeave` and `onBeforeRouteUpdate` in its setup. They are removed when the page unmounts.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import { onBeforeRouteLeave } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';

const draft = ref('');
onBeforeRouteLeave(() => draft.value === '' || window.confirm('Discard the draft?'));
</script>

<template>
  <textarea v-model="draft"></textarea>
</template>
```

They work only in a component that a `RouterView` renders, and its children ([VIBE7112](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7112)).

## Lazy pages

A `component` that is a function is loaded on the first navigation to its route, before the route changes, and kept for later navigations: `() => import('./pages/UserPage.vibe')`. The build puts each lazy page in its own chunk.

After a deploy, an open tab can ask for a chunk that no longer exists. The navigation then fails with [VIBE7109](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7109); load the target as a full page to get the new version:

```ts
router.onError((error, to) => {
  if (isVibeError(error, 'VIBE7109')) window.location.assign(to.fullPath);
});
```

## Scroll behavior

With the web history, the router restores the scroll position on back and forward, scrolls to the element of a hash, keeps the position when only the query changes, and scrolls to the top otherwise. `scrollBehavior` replaces this: it returns a position, `{ el }` for an element, `false` to leave the scroll as it is, or nothing for the top.

```ts
const router = createRouter({
  history: createWebHistory(),
  routes,
  scrollBehavior(to, from, saved) {
    if (saved) return saved;
    if (to.hash) return { el: to.hash, behavior: 'smooth' };
    return { top: 0 };
  },
});
```

An element scrolls into view with its `scroll-margin-top`, which leaves room for a fixed header.

## Announcing route changes

A screen reader does not notice that the page changed. Announce the new page in a live region after each navigation, and give each page a `document.title`:

```ts
const status = document.createElement('p');
status.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
status.className = 'visually-hidden';
document.body.append(status);

router.afterEach((to, from, failure) => {
  if (failure) return;
  status.textContent = `${document.title}, page loaded`;
});
```

## See also

- [Data loading](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/data): load data for the current route with `useAsync`.
- [Testing components](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/testing#testing-with-the-router): test pages with a memory history.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/routing

---

# Template syntax

A template is HTML with expressions and directives. An expression reads the bindings and imports of `<script setup>`, the props, and `$attrs`, `$slots`, `$emit` and `$props`; refs are unwrapped. A name that is none of these is reported as [VIBE2007](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2007) when the file compiles.

## Text

`{{ expression }}` renders text. `null` and `undefined` render nothing; arrays and plain objects render as JSON.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const user = ref({ name: 'Ada', unread: 3 });
const html = '<em>Welcome back</em>';
</script>

<template>
  <p>{{ user.name }} has {{ user.unread }} unread {{ user.unread === 1 ? 'message' : 'messages' }}.</p>
  <p v-html="html"></p>
</template>
```

`v-text="value"` sets the text content of an element and `v-html="value"` its inner HTML. `v-html` renders the string as HTML: only pass it content you trust.

## Attributes

`:name="expression"`, short for `v-bind:name`, binds an attribute or a DOM property. `null` and `undefined` remove the attribute, and `false` removes a boolean attribute such as `disabled`. `v-bind="object"` spreads every key of an object.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const busy = ref(false);
const link = { href: 'https://vibejs.org', target: '_blank', rel: 'noopener' };
</script>

<template>
  <button type="submit" :disabled="busy" :aria-busy="busy">Save</button>
  <a v-bind="link">Docs</a>
</template>
```

The `.prop` modifier always sets a DOM property and `.attr` always an attribute; `.camel` camelizes the name.

## Class and style

`:class` takes a string, an object whose keys are added when their values are truthy, or an array of these. `:style` takes a string, an object of CSS properties in camelCase or kebab-case, or an array. CSS custom properties (`--name`) and `!important` work in both forms. A static `class` or `style` and the bound one are merged.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const active = ref(true);
const size = ref(16);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="card" :class="{ active, large: size > 20 }" :style="{ fontSize: `${size}px`, '--accent': 'teal' }">
    <span :class="['badge', active && 'badge-on']">On</span>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Events

`@event="handler"`, short for `v-on:event`, adds a listener. The value is a function, or a statement that runs when the event fires, where `$event` is the event.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const count = ref(0);
const text = ref('');
function add(step: number) {
  count.value += step;
}
function submit() {
  text.value = '';
}
function type(event: Event) {
  text.value = (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value;
}
</script>

<template>
  <button type="button" @click="add(1)">Add</button>
  <button type="button" @click.shift="add(10)">Add 10 with Shift</button>
  <form @submit.prevent="submit">
    <input :value="text" @input="type" @keydown.enter.exact="submit" />
  </form>
</template>
```

- Modifiers: `.stop` and `.prevent` call `stopPropagation()` and `preventDefault()`, `.self` ignores events from children, `.once`, `.capture` and `.passive` are listener options, `.ctrl`, `.alt`, `.shift` and `.meta` require the key, `.exact` requires exactly the keys listed, and `.left`, `.middle` and `.right` select the mouse button.
- On `keydown`, `keyup` and `keypress`, other modifiers name keys in kebab case: `.enter`, `.esc`, `.page-down`.
- Each listener is attached to its own element with `addEventListener`; events are not delegated to a common ancestor. `event.currentTarget` is the element, and `.stop` in a handler stops the event from reaching listeners of ancestors.
- The event name is static ([VIBE2303](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2303)), and there is one attribute per event ([VIBE2302](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2302)).

## Conditions

`v-if`, `v-else-if` and `v-else` render one of several branches. A branch that is removed is unmounted: its components run their unmount hooks and its state is gone. `<template v-if>` groups several elements without a wrapper.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const status = ref<'loading' | 'error' | 'ready'>('loading');
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="status === 'loading'">Loading…</p>
  <template v-else-if="status === 'error'">
    <h2>Something went wrong</h2>
    <button type="button" @click="status = 'loading'">Retry</button>
  </template>
  <p v-else>Ready</p>
</template>
```

## Lists

`v-for` renders an element for each item of an array, an iterable such as a `Map` or `Set`, the numbers from 1 to `n`, or the values of an object. Every element in a `v-for` needs a unique, stable `:key` ([VIBE2203](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2203)); only a numeric range needs none.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const todos = ref([
  { id: 1, title: 'Write docs', done: false },
  { id: 2, title: 'Ship', done: true },
]);
const scores = { ada: 3, grace: 5 };
</script>

<template>
  <ul>
    <li v-for="(todo, index) in todos" :key="todo.id" :class="{ done: todo.done }">{{ index + 1 }}. {{ todo.title }}</li>
  </ul>
  <dl>
    <template v-for="(score, name) in scores" :key="name">
      <dt>{{ name }}</dt>
      <dd>{{ score }}</dd>
    </template>
  </dl>
  <span v-for="n in 3">{{ n }}</span>
</template>
```

When the list changes, items with the same key keep their elements and state, and the fewest elements are moved. `v-if` and `v-for` cannot share an element ([VIBE2103](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2103)): filter the list in a `computed` instead.

## v-show

`v-show="condition"` sets `display: none` while the condition is false and keeps the element in the DOM. Use it for content that toggles often; use `v-if` for content that is rarely shown. It applies to elements only, not to components or `<template>`.

## v-model on elements

`v-model` binds a form element to a ref in both directions.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const name = ref('');
const age = ref(0);
const agree = ref(false);
const tags = ref<string[]>([]);
const plan = ref('free');
const color = ref('red');
</script>

<template>
  <input v-model.trim="name" />
  <input v-model.number="age" type="number" />
  <input v-model="agree" type="checkbox" />
  <input v-model="tags" type="checkbox" value="news" />
  <input v-model="tags" type="checkbox" value="offers" />
  <input v-model="plan" type="radio" value="free" />
  <input v-model="plan" type="radio" value="pro" />
  <select v-model="color">
    <option value="red">Red</option>
    <option value="blue">Blue</option>
  </select>
</template>
```

- Text inputs and `<textarea>` update on `input`. `.lazy` updates on `change` instead, `.trim` trims the value and `.number` converts it to a number (an `<input type="number">` always does). While an input method composes text, the model is updated when the composition ends.
- A checkbox binds a boolean, or adds and removes its `value` in an array or a `Set`; `true-value` and `false-value` replace `true` and `false`.
- A radio button sets the model to its `value`.
- `<select>` binds the selected option's value; `<select multiple>` binds an array of values.

[Components](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components#v-model) can take `v-model` too.

## Template refs

`ref="name"` on an element fills the template ref that the script declares with `useTemplateRef('name')`. Its value is `null` until the element is rendered and again after it is removed; inside `v-for` it is an array of elements.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, useTemplateRef } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const input = useTemplateRef<HTMLInputElement>('search');

onMounted(() => input.value?.focus());
</script>

<template>
  <input ref="search" type="search" />
</template>
```

A string ref without a matching `useTemplateRef()` is reported as [VIBE2701](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2701). A bound `:ref="(el) => ..."` calls the function with the element, and with `null` when it is removed. A ref on a component gives the values that component [exposes](https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/components#exposing-values).

## Dynamic components

`<component :is="value">` renders the component that `value` holds, and nothing for `null` or `undefined`. Changing the value unmounts the previous component.

```vibe
<script setup lang="ts">
import { shallowRef, type Component } from '@usevibejs/ui';

const props = defineProps<{ views: Record<string, Component> }>();
const current = shallowRef<Component | null>(null);

function open(name: string) {
  current.value = props.views[name] ?? null;
}
</script>

<template>
  <nav>
    <button v-for="(view, name) in views" :key="name" type="button" @click="open(name)">{{ name }}</button>
  </nav>
  <component :is="current" />
</template>
```

`:is` takes a component object, never a name: there is no global registry ([VIBE2006](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2006), [VIBE5207](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5207)). Keep a component in a `shallowRef`, which does not make it reactive.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/template-syntax

---

# Testing components

Component tests run in Vitest with jsdom. `@usevibejs/ui/testing` mounts a component in a real app, returns a wrapper to query and drive the rendered DOM, and cleans up after each test.

## Setup

The `vibe()` plugin compiles `.vibe` files for the tests as it does for the app:

```ts
import { vibe } from '@usevibejs/compiler/vite';
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [vibe()],
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    include: ['ui/src/**/*.test.ts'],
  },
});
```

The app template already has this config. Tests sit next to the component: `Counter.test.ts` next to `Counter.vibe`.

## Mounting

```ts
import { mount } from '@usevibejs/ui/testing';
import { expect, it } from 'vitest';
import Counter from './Counter.vibe';

it('counts clicks', async () => {
  const wrapper = mount(Counter, { props: { start: 1 } });
  await wrapper.get('button').trigger('click');
  expect(wrapper.get('button').text()).toBe('Count: 2');
});
```

`mount(component, options)` takes:

- `props`: the props, including `on*` listeners. Required when the component has required props.
- `slots`: slot content by name, as text, a component, or a function of the slot props that returns text or nodes.
- `provide`: values the app provides, by key, such as `{ [API]: api }` for an `InjectionKey`.
- `plugins`: plugins the app installs, in order, such as the router.
- `attachTo`: where the host element is appended, an element or a selector; `document.body` by default.

Other options fail with [VIBE7206](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7206), which names the replacement.

A component mounted in a test body or a `beforeEach` unmounts when the test finishes. When a test fails, its error ends with the rendered HTML of each mounted component. A component mounted in `beforeAll` stays until you call `wrapper.unmount()`.

## Finding elements

Wrappers query the rendered DOM with CSS selectors:

- `get(selector)` returns the first match, or fails with [VIBE7201](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7201) and the rendered HTML.
- `find(selector)` returns the first match, or a wrapper whose `exists()` is `false`; using it fails with [VIBE7202](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7202).
- `findAll(selector)` returns every match in document order.

A wrapper reads its element with `text()`, `html()`, `attributes(name?)`, `classes(name?)`, `isVisible()` and `exists()`, and `element` is the DOM element itself. Select by what the user sees and by stable hooks: element names, roles and labels as attributes, classes, or `data-test` attributes.

```ts
const wrapper = mount(TodoList);
expect(wrapper.findAll('li')).toHaveLength(3);
expect(wrapper.get('li.done').text()).toBe('Write the tests');
expect(wrapper.get('[aria-label="New todo"]').attributes('placeholder')).toBe('What next?');
expect(wrapper.find('.empty').exists()).toBe(false);
```

`wrapper.element` and every element of `findAll()` are plain DOM elements, so any DOM testing library works on them too.

## Events and input

`trigger(event, init?)` dispatches a bubbling, cancelable event of the right class, and `setValue(value)` sets an input, a textarea, a checkbox, a radio button or a select, then fires the events that `v-model` listens to. Both wait for the DOM update.

```ts
const wrapper = mount(TodoList);
await wrapper.get('input').setValue('Ship it');
await wrapper.get('input').trigger('keydown', { key: 'Enter' });
expect(wrapper.findAll('li').at(-1)?.text()).toBe('Ship it');
```

A key or a modifier goes in the event init, never in the event name: `trigger('keydown.enter')` fails with [VIBE7203](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7203). A disabled element receives no event.

## Props and events

`setProps(props)` assigns props and waits for the update. `emitted()` returns the arguments of every event the component emitted, by event name, typed by `defineEmits`.

```ts
const wrapper = mount(Picker, { props: { options: ['a', 'b'] } });
await wrapper.setProps({ options: ['a', 'b', 'c'] });
await wrapper.findAll('button')[2].trigger('click');
expect(wrapper.emitted('pick')).toEqual([['c']]);
```

## Waiting for async work

`flushPromises()` resolves after the pending promise callbacks ran, and with them the DOM updates they caused. Await it after anything that loads data. It also works with `vi.useFakeTimers()`.

```ts
const wrapper = mount(UserCard, { props: { id: 1 } });
await flushPromises();
expect(wrapper.get('h2').text()).toBe('Ada');
```

## Composables

`mountComposable(fn, options?)` runs `fn` as the setup of a component, so it can use `inject()`, lifecycle hooks and watchers, and returns its `result`. It takes `provide` and `plugins` and unmounts like `mount()`.

```ts
import { nextTick, ref, watch } from '@usevibejs/ui';
import { mountComposable } from '@usevibejs/ui/testing';
import { expect } from 'vitest';

function useHistory<T>(initial: T) {
  const value = ref(initial);
  const past: T[] = [];
  watch(value, (_, old) => past.push(old));
  return { value, past };
}

const { result } = mountComposable(() => useHistory(1));
result.value.value = 2;
await nextTick();
expect(result.past).toEqual([1]);
```

## Testing with the router

Install a router with a memory history through `plugins`, then wait for the first navigation with `router.isReady()`. Use the app's own routes, imported from `routes.ts`, so that the test covers the real records:

```ts
import { createMemoryHistory, createRouter } from '@usevibejs/ui/router';
import { flushPromises, mount } from '@usevibejs/ui/testing';
import { expect, it } from 'vitest';
import App from '../App.vibe';

it('opens a user from the list', async () => {
  const router = createRouter({ history: createMemoryHistory(), routes });
  const wrapper = mount(App, { plugins: [router] });
  await router.isReady();

  await wrapper.get('a[href="/users/1"]').trigger('click');
  await flushPromises();
  expect(router.currentRoute.value.fullPath).toBe('/users/1');
  expect(wrapper.get('h1').text()).toBe('User 1');
});
```

To start on another route, `await router.push('/users/1')` after `router.isReady()`. `await router.push()` waits for the guards and the lazy page; after a navigation that loads data, also await `flushPromises()`.

## Replacing a child component

Children render as they do in the app. To keep a heavy child out of a test, mock its module with Vitest:

```ts
import { vi } from 'vitest';

vi.mock('./Chart.vibe', () => import('./test/ChartStub.vibe'));
```

`ChartStub.vibe` is a small component with the same props, such as `<div class="chart-stub" />`.

## Coverage

`vibejs check` reports the coverage of every file and warns with [VIBE8302](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8302) below 100%. To make full coverage a requirement, uncomment the threshold line in `vitest.config.ts`:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      thresholds: { 100: true, perFile: true },
    },
  },
});
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/ui/testing

---

# Server

A vibe.js server is a tree of modules. The root module imports feature modules; each module lists its providers and controllers; each controller serves one contract. The server is built on the Fetch API: an application is a `fetch(Request): Promise<Response>` function that also listens on Node.

## Application layout

```
contracts/src/todos.contract.ts     the contract shared with the UI
server/src/app.module.ts            AppModule and appOptions
server/src/main.ts                  creates the app and listens
server/src/todos/todos.module.ts    a feature module
server/src/todos/todos.controller.ts
server/src/todos/todos.service.ts
```

`server/src/app.module.ts` exports the root module and the application options. The dev server, the tools and the tests import this file, so it has no side effects:

```ts
@Module({ imports: [] })
export class AppModule {}

export const appOptions: AppOptions = { basePath: '/api' };
```

`server/src/main.ts` is the production entry. It creates the application, closes it on `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT`, and listens:

```ts
const app = await VibeFactory.create(AppModule, appOptions);
app.enableShutdownHooks();
await app.listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
```

## Creating the application

`VibeFactory.create(root, options)` scans the module graph, creates every provider and controller, and runs the `onModuleInit` and `onApplicationBootstrap` hooks. It does not listen. A graph error, such as a missing provider ([VIBE9102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9102)) or an unhandled route ([VIBE9303](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9303)), rejects `create` before any request is served.

The created `App`:

| Member                          | What it does                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fetch(req)`                    | Handles one request. It is bound, so it can be passed on as a plain function.                                                                                                     |
| `request(path, init?)`          | Sends a request in process; `init.json` sets a JSON body.                                                                                                                         |
| `listen(port?, hostname?)`      | Serves the app over HTTP on Node; the port defaults to 3000.                                                                                                                      |
| `enableShutdownHooks(signals?)` | Calls `close()` on each signal, then re-raises it.                                                                                                                                |
| `close(signal?)`                | Rejects new requests with 503, waits for running ones up to `shutdownTimeout`, stops the server and runs `onModuleDestroy` and `onApplicationShutdown`. Calling it twice is safe. |
| `get(token)`                    | Reads a provider, for scripts and tests.                                                                                                                                          |
| `inspect()`                     | Lists the routes and modules, for tools.                                                                                                                                          |

`inspect(root, options)` returns the same description without creating the application: no provider, controller, enhancer or hook runs, so tools and tests can read the graph safely.

```ts
const { routes, modules } = inspect(AppModule, { basePath: '/api' });
console.log(routes.map((r) => `${r.method} ${r.path} -> ${r.handler}`));
console.log(modules.map((m) => m.path));
```

## Deploying

`vibejs build` writes two deployables:

- `ui/dist`: the static UI, served by any static file host or CDN.
- `server/dist/main.js`: the server, run with `node server/dist/main.js`. It reads `PORT` and answers under `/api`.

Route `/api` to the server and everything else to the static files. During development, `vibejs dev` serves both on one port.

## Next

- [Modules and providers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/modules)
- [Contracts](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/contracts)
- [Handlers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/handlers)
- [Middleware, guards, interceptors and filters](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/pipeline)
- [Configuration](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/configuration)
- [Testing](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/testing)

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/server/

---

# Configuration

## Environment config

`defineConfig(schema)` returns a class whose constructor validates the environment variables named by the schema keys. Provide it like any class and inject it where it is needed:

```ts
export class AppConfig extends defineConfig({
  DATABASE_URL: v.pipe(v.string(), v.url()),
  PORT: v.optional(v.pipe(v.string(), v.transform(Number)), '3000'),
}) {}

class Db {
  private readonly config = inject(AppConfig);

  url(): string {
    return this.config.DATABASE_URL;
  }
}

@Module({ global: true, providers: [AppConfig, Db], exports: [AppConfig, Db] })
export class CoreModule {}
```

The config is validated once, when the application is created. Every failing key is reported at once as [VIBE9601](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9601); the message names the keys and never prints the values. Schemas must be synchronous ([VIBE9602](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9602)). The validated object is frozen.

## Logging

The application logger is provided as `Logger` in every module. Inject it to log with the same sink as the framework:

```ts
class Mailer {
  private readonly log = inject(Logger);

  send(to: string): void {
    this.log.info('mail sent', { to });
  }
}
```

The default logger is `JsonLogger`, which writes one JSON line per entry: `{ time, level, msg, ...fields }`. Pass another one in `AppOptions.logger`:

```ts
export const appOptions: AppOptions = {
  basePath: '/api',
  logger: new JsonLogger({ level: 'debug', fields: { service: 'todo' } }),
};
```

Levels are `debug`, `info` (default), `warn`, `error` and `silent`. Each request is logged at `debug` with its method, path, status and duration. `ctx.log` in a handler is a child logger that adds the `requestId`. To send logs elsewhere, extend the abstract `Logger` class, or pass `write` to `JsonLogger`.

## CORS

`cors(options)` is a middleware. It answers preflight requests and adds the CORS headers to the responses for allowed origins:

```ts
export const appOptions: AppOptions = {
  basePath: '/api',
  middleware: [cors({ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true, maxAge: 600 })],
};
```

`origin` is `'*'`, a list of origins or a predicate. `'*'` together with `credentials: true` is rejected ([VIBE9404](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9404)), because browsers ignore it. When the UI and the API share an origin, which is the default layout, no CORS is needed.

## Cookies

`ctx.cookies` reads the request cookies and sets response cookies. New cookies are `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` and `Path=/` unless the options say otherwise:

```ts
@Controller(session)
export class SessionController {
  @Handle(session.start)
  start(ctx: Ctx<typeof session.start>): void {
    ctx.cookies.set('session', crypto.randomUUID(), { maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 });
  }

  @Handle(session.end)
  end(ctx: Ctx<typeof session.end>): void {
    ctx.cookies.delete('session');
  }
}
```

A cookie name must be an RFC 9110 token ([VIBE9504](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9504)).

## Limits and shutdown

| Option              | Default   | Meaning                                                                       |
| ------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `basePath`          | `''`      | Prefix of every route, such as `/api` ([VIBE9405](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9405)).         |
| `bodyLimit`         | 1 MiB     | The largest request body in bytes; larger bodies get 413.                     |
| `shutdownTimeout`   | 10 000 ms | How long `close()` waits for running requests ([VIBE9402](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9402)). |
| `validateResponses` | `true`    | Validates handler results; see [Handlers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/handlers#validation).          |

## TypeScript setup

The server decorators are TypeScript legacy decorators. The server `tsconfig.json` enables them:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "experimentalDecorators": true
  }
}
```

- Never enable `emitDecoratorMetadata` and never import `reflect-metadata`: dependencies are declared with `inject()`, not read from types.
- Without `experimentalDecorators`, the decorators throw [VIBE9301](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9301) when the decorated class is defined.
- Vite and Vitest compile decorators with Oxc, which imports its helpers from `@oxc-project/runtime`. Keep `@oxc-project/runtime` as a direct dependency of the server package so that the helpers resolve.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/server/configuration

---

# Contracts

A contract declares the routes of one resource: method, path, inputs, response and errors. The server serves it, the UI calls it, and both are type-checked against the same declaration, with no code generation.

```ts
import { defineContract, del, get, patch, post } from '@usevibejs/contract';
import * as v from 'valibot';

export const Todo = v.object({ id: v.string(), title: v.string(), done: v.boolean() });

export const todos = defineContract('/todos', {
  list: get('/', { query: v.object({ done: v.optional(v.string()) }), response: v.array(Todo) }),
  create: post('/', {
    body: v.object({ title: v.pipe(v.string(), v.trim(), v.minLength(1)) }),
    response: Todo,
    status: 201,
  }),
  toggle: patch('/:id', { response: Todo, errors: { TODO_NOT_FOUND: 404 } }),
  remove: del('/:id', { errors: { TODO_NOT_FOUND: 404 } }),
});
```

Contract files (`*.contract.ts`) import only `@usevibejs/contract` and a schema library, so the UI can import them without pulling in server code.

## Routes

The route helpers are `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `del`. Each takes a path and an optional definition:

| Field                    | Meaning                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `params`                 | A schema for the path params; without one they are strings.                                  |
| `query`                  | A schema for the query string. A key repeated in the URL, or typed as an array, is an array. |
| `headers`                | A schema for the request headers, with lowercase names.                                      |
| `body`                   | A schema for the JSON request body; not allowed on `get` ([VIBE9004](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9004)).     |
| `response`               | A schema for the JSON success body, or `raw()`. Without one the route answers 204.           |
| `status`                 | The success status: 200 (default), 201 or 202.                                               |
| `errors`                 | The error codes the route raises, each with its HTTP status.                                 |
| `summary`, `description` | Text for the OpenAPI document.                                                               |

Paths are `/` or segments such as `/users/:id/posts`; params start with `:` ([VIBE9001](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9001)). The full path of a route is the contract prefix followed by the route path, and the application's `basePath` is prepended when it is served.

`raw(contentType?)` declares a response that is sent as is, such as a file. The handler returns a `Response` or a body such as a string or a stream, and the client receives the `Response`:

```ts
export const reports = defineContract('/reports', {
  csv: get('/:year', { response: raw('text/csv') }),
});
```

## Errors

A route declares the errors a client should handle as `errors: { CODE: status }`. The handler raises them with `ctx.fail('CODE', detail?)`, and the client receives an `application/problem+json` response:

```json
{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Not Found",
  "status": 404,
  "code": "TODO_NOT_FOUND",
  "detail": "No todo 7",
  "requestId": "9a7c..."
}
```

Besides the declared codes, every route can answer the built-in codes `BAD_REQUEST`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `INVALID_JSON`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `BODY_TOO_LARGE`, `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, `INTERNAL_ERROR` and `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. A `VALIDATION_FAILED` problem lists each issue in `errors` as `{ in, pointer, message }`.

## Schema libraries

Any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) library works, and one contract may mix them.

- **valibot** is the recommended default for code that ships to the browser, because only the validators you use end up in the bundle.
- **zod** works as well. Dates travel as strings in JSON, so declare them with `z.iso.datetime()` rather than `z.date()`.

Schemas run on the server. It validates the request parts before the handler runs and passes the schema output to the handler, so `v.trim()` in a body schema trims on the server. The client sends its typed input as JSON without validating it, and types the response from the schema without validating it again.

## Calling a contract

`createClient(contracts, options)` returns one function per route. A call never throws for HTTP or network failures; it resolves to an `ApiResult` that you narrow on `ok`, then on `error.code`:

```ts
const api = createClient({ todos }, { baseUrl: '/api' });

const result = await api.todos.one({ params: { id: '7' } });
if (result.ok) {
  console.log(result.data.title);
} else if (result.error.code === 'TODO_NOT_FOUND') {
  const status: 404 = result.error.status;
  console.log(status, result.error.detail);
} else {
  console.log(result.error.code, result.error.status);
}
```

- The input object has `params`, `query`, `headers` and `body`, each typed from the route.
- The second argument takes `{ signal, headers }`. `options.headers` may be a function, called for every request, such as one that adds an authorization header.
- A network failure resolves with `code: 'NETWORK_ERROR'` and `status: 0`, an abort with `ABORTED`, and a failed response that is not a problem, or a body that is not JSON, with `UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE`.
- Tests pass `fetch: app.fetch` to call an application in process; see [Testing](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/testing).

## OpenAPI

`generateOpenApi(contracts, options)` from `@usevibejs/server/openapi` returns an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the same record of contracts the client takes. Serve it with a middleware. A middleware sees the full request path, base path included, so the recipe below answers `/api/openapi.json` under the base path `/api`:

```ts
const doc = generateOpenApi(
  { todos },
  { info: { title: 'Todo API', version: '1.0.0' }, servers: [{ url: '/api' }] },
);

export const openapi: Middleware = (req, next) =>
  new URL(req.url).pathname.endsWith('/openapi.json')
    ? Promise.resolve(Response.json(doc))
    : next();
```

Each schema is converted with its Standard JSON Schema converter. zod schemas carry one; wrap valibot schemas with `toStandardJsonSchema()` from `@valibot/to-json-schema`, or pass a `toJsonSchema(schema, io)` fallback. A schema that cannot be converted throws [VIBE9801](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9801), two different schemas with one name throw [VIBE9802](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9802), and an error status outside 400–599 throws [VIBE9803](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9803).

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/server/contracts

---

# Controllers and handlers

A controller serves one contract. Each route of the contract has exactly one handler method, marked with `@Handle(route)`:

```ts
@Controller(todos)
export class TodosController {
  private readonly todos = inject(TodosService);

  @Handle(todos.list)
  list(): Todo[] {
    return this.todos.list();
  }

  @Handle(todos.create)
  create(ctx: Ctx<typeof todos.create>): Todo {
    return this.todos.create(ctx.body.title);
  }

  @Handle(todos.remove)
  remove(ctx: Ctx<typeof todos.remove>): void {
    if (!this.todos.remove(ctx.params.id)) ctx.fail('TODO_NOT_FOUND', `No todo ${ctx.params.id}`);
  }
}
```

Register the controller in the `controllers` of a module. At startup the application checks that every route has one handler ([VIBE9303](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9303), [VIBE9304](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9304)), that each handler belongs to the controller's contract ([VIBE9305](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9305)) and that each contract has one controller ([VIBE9306](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9306)).

## The context

A handler receives one argument, `ctx: Ctx<typeof contract.route>`:

| Field                                | Value                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `params`, `query`, `headers`, `body` | The validated request parts; each exists only when the route declares it (params always). |
| `fail(code, detail?)`                | Ends the request with a declared error code of the route.                                 |
| `req`, `url`                         | The `Request` and its parsed URL.                                                         |
| `requestId`                          | The `x-request-id` header, or a generated id; it is sent back on the response.            |
| `log`                                | The application logger with the `requestId` attached.                                     |
| `cookies`                            | `get`, `set` and `delete`; see [Configuration](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/configuration#cookies).               |
| `responseHeaders`                    | Headers added to the response.                                                            |
| `signal`                             | Aborted when the client disconnects.                                                      |
| `state`                              | Values that guards and interceptors share with the handler.                               |
| `getMetadata(key)`                   | Metadata set with `createMetadata`; see [Pipeline](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/pipeline#metadata).               |

A handler may be async. It returns the route's response type: the schema's input type for a JSON response, nothing for a route without a response, and a `Response` or a body for a `raw()` route. Returning a `Response` from any handler sends it as is.

## Errors

- **Declared errors.** `ctx.fail('CODE', detail?)` throws an `HttpError` with the status the contract declares. The codes are typed: only the route's declared codes are accepted.
- **Other client errors.** `throw new HttpError(status, code, detail?)` from a handler, guard, interceptor or service. Prefer a declared code or a built-in one such as `NOT_FOUND`; an undeclared code is still sent, with the warning [VIBE9502](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9502).
- **Bugs.** Any other error is logged with its cause ([VIBE9503](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9503)) and answered with 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`, without details.

Every error response is `application/problem+json`: `{ type, title, status, code, detail?, errors?, requestId }`.

```ts
export function requireUser(id: string | undefined): string {
  if (!id) throw new HttpError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Sign in first');
  return id;
}
```

## Validation

Before the handler runs, the application validates `params`, `query`, `headers` and `body` against the route's schemas and puts the schema output on `ctx`. When any part fails, the client receives 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` with every issue in `errors`, and the handler does not run. A body that is not JSON is 400 `INVALID_JSON`; a body over `bodyLimit` is 413 `BODY_TOO_LARGE`.

With `validateResponses` (on by default), the handler's result is validated against the response schema and the schema output is sent. A mismatch is a server bug: it is logged as [VIBE9501](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9501) and answered with 500.

Sending the schema output means the schema decides which keys reach the client:

- valibot `v.object()` and zod `z.object()` drop keys the schema does not declare, so an internal field such as `passwordHash` is not sent.
- arktype keeps undeclared keys unless the type sets `"+": "delete"`.
- With `validateResponses: false`, the result is sent unchanged.

Declare an explicit response schema for every route that returns stored data, and keep `validateResponses` on.

## TS1241 on @Handle

`TS1241: Unable to resolve signature of method decorator when called as an expression` on a `@Handle(...)` line means that the method does not match the route. `vibejs check` reports it with this fix:

> the handler must be `(ctx: Ctx<typeof contract.route>)` and return the route response type; do not cast or use `any`

Check, in this order:

1. The parameter is `ctx: Ctx<typeof contract.route>` for the same route that `@Handle` names, or the method has no parameter.
2. The return type is the response type: a missing field or a wrong type in the returned object is the usual cause. Add an explicit return type to the method to see the exact field in the error.
3. A route without a `response` returns `void`.

```ts
@Controller(users)
export class UsersController {
  // @ts-expect-error -- TS1241: `id` must be a string
  @Handle(users.one)
  one(ctx: Ctx<typeof users.one>): { id: number } {
    return { id: Number(ctx.params.id) };
  }
}
```

The fix is to return `{ id: ctx.params.id }` with the return type `{ id: string }`. Never silence the error with a cast or `any`: the decorator is what keeps the handler and the client in sync.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/server/handlers

---

# Modules and providers

## Modules

A module is a class with `@Module()`. It lists what it provides, which controllers it registers, which modules it imports and which of its providers other modules may use:

```ts
class TodosService {
  list(): string[] {
    return [];
  }
}

@Module({ providers: [TodosService], controllers: [], exports: [TodosService] })
export class TodosModule {}

@Module({ imports: [TodosModule] })
export class AppModule {}
```

A module sees its own providers, the exports of the modules it imports and the exports of global modules. Anything else fails at startup with [VIBE9102](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9102), which names the module and the chain that asked for the token. Modules cannot import each other in a cycle ([VIBE9202](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9202)), and every imported class needs its own `@Module()` ([VIBE9201](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9201)).

A module can export an imported module, which passes that module's exports on to its own importers. `@Module({ global: true })` makes the exports visible everywhere without an import; use it for cross-cutting services such as a database client.

## Injecting dependencies

Dependencies are fields initialized with `inject(Token)`:

```ts
class TodosService {
  private readonly db = inject(Db);

  list(): string[] {
    return this.db.query('select * from todos');
  }
}
```

- Providers are created with `new Cls()`. A constructor with parameters is rejected with [VIBE9104](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9104); move each parameter to an `inject()` field.
- `inject()` works while the container builds an object: in field initializers, in the constructor body and in the synchronous part of a factory. Anywhere else it throws [VIBE9101](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9101).
- Make injected fields `private`. A public field is part of the class's declared type, so with `isolatedDeclarations` it needs an explicit type annotation (TS9012): `readonly db: Db = inject(Db)`.
- `inject(Token, { optional: true })` returns `undefined` when no provider is visible.

## Providers

A provider is a class, or an object that names a token in `provide` and says how to create its value:

```ts
const ApiUrl = token<string>('ApiUrl');
const Clock = token<() => number>('Clock');
const Now = token<() => number>('Now');

export const providers: Provider[] = [
  { provide: TodosService, useClass: MemoryTodosService },
  { provide: ApiUrl, useValue: 'https://api.example.com' },
  { provide: Clock, useFactory: () => () => Date.now() },
  { provide: Now, useExisting: Clock },
];
```

`token<T>(description)` creates a typed token for a value that is not a class. A class is its own token. When a module lists the same token twice, the last entry wins.

A factory receives the tokens listed in `inject` as parameters, and may be async:

```ts
const DatabaseUrl = token<string>('DatabaseUrl');
const Database = token<{ close(): Promise<void> }>('Database');

export const database: Provider[] = [
  { provide: DatabaseUrl, useValue: 'postgres://localhost/app' },
  { provide: Database, useFactory: (url: string) => connect(url), inject: [DatabaseUrl] },
];
```

Every factory settles before any class is created, so classes can inject a factory's value directly. A class that a factory needs while it is being built can only inject factories that have already settled; list such a dependency in the factory's `inject` array so it settles first ([VIBE9106](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9106)).

## Lifecycle hooks

A provider, controller, enhancer or module class can implement these hooks:

| Hook                             | When                                                                   |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onModuleInit()`                 | After every object is created, in module order (deepest import first). |
| `onApplicationBootstrap()`       | After every `onModuleInit`.                                            |
| `onModuleDestroy()`              | On `close()`, in reverse order.                                        |
| `onApplicationShutdown(signal?)` | After every `onModuleDestroy`.                                         |

```ts
class Migrations implements OnModuleInit, OnModuleDestroy {
  private readonly db = inject(Database);

  async onModuleInit(): Promise<void> {
    await this.db.connect();
  }

  async onModuleDestroy(): Promise<void> {
    await this.db.close();
  }
}
```

Init hooks are awaited one by one, and the first error stops startup. Shutdown hooks all run even when one fails; the failures are reported together as [VIBE9204](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9204).

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/server/modules

---

# Middleware, guards, interceptors and filters

A request passes through these steps:

1. **Middleware**, around everything, in the order of `AppOptions.middleware`.
2. **Routing**: 404, or 405 with `Allow`, when no route matches.
3. **Guards**: global, then controller, then method. The first one that returns `false` ends the request with 403 `FORBIDDEN`.
4. **Interceptors**: global, then controller, then method; the first one is the outermost.
5. **Validation** of the request parts, then the **handler**.
6. **Response** building and response validation.
7. **Filters** for any error of steps 3 to 6: method, then controller, then global.

`app.inspect()` and `inspect(root, options)` list each route's guards, interceptors and filters in exactly this order, globals included.

## Middleware

A middleware wraps the whole request at the Fetch level. It runs before routing, so it sees every request, including those that match no route:

```ts
export const timing: Middleware = async (req, next) => {
  const started = performance.now();
  const res = await next();
  // A copy has mutable headers, even for a redirect.
  const out = new Response(res.body, res);
  out.headers.set('server-timing', `app;dur=${Math.round(performance.now() - started)}`);
  return out;
};
```

`next(req?)` continues with the same request or with a replacement. Middleware is a plain function, so a package can export a factory of middleware, such as the built-in `cors()`.

## Guards

A guard decides whether a request may reach its handler:

```ts
export class SessionGuard implements CanActivate {
  canActivate(ctx: RequestContext): boolean {
    const id = ctx.cookies.get('session');
    if (id) ctx.state.user = { id };
    return id !== undefined;
  }
}
```

Apply it with `@UseGuards(SessionGuard)` on a controller or a handler, or globally with `AppOptions.guards`. To answer something other than 403, throw an `HttpError`, such as `new HttpError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED')`.

`ctx.state` carries values from guards and interceptors to handlers. Type its fields by augmenting `RequestState`:

```ts
declare module '@usevibejs/server' {
  interface RequestState {
    user?: { readonly id: string };
  }
}
```

## Interceptors

An interceptor wraps the handler. `next()` runs the rest of the chain and resolves to the handler's result, so an interceptor can measure, retry or replace it:

```ts
export class LogDuration implements Interceptor {
  async intercept(ctx: RequestContext, next: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
    const started = performance.now();
    try {
      return await next();
    } finally {
      ctx.log.info('handled', { ms: Math.round(performance.now() - started) });
    }
  }
}
```

## Filters

A filter turns an error into a response. It returns a `Response`, an `HttpError` to send as a problem, or `undefined` to pass the error to the next filter. Errors that no filter handles are answered as described in [Handlers](https://vibejs.org/v0/server/handlers#errors).

```ts
export class DbErrors implements ExceptionFilter {
  catch(error: unknown): HttpError | undefined {
    return error instanceof NotFoundInDb ? new HttpError(404, 'NOT_FOUND') : undefined;
  }
}
```

Guards, interceptors and filters are classes without constructor parameters. They are created once, in the scope of the module of their controller (globals in the root module), so they can `inject()` providers.

## Metadata

`createMetadata<T>(name)` creates a typed decorator that is also the key to read the value back. Method values override controller values:

```ts
export const Roles = createMetadata<readonly string[]>('roles');

class RolesGuard implements CanActivate {
  canActivate(ctx: RequestContext): boolean {
    const needed = ctx.getMetadata(Roles) ?? [];
    if (!needed.every((role) => ctx.state.roles?.includes(role))) {
      throw new HttpError(403, 'FORBIDDEN', `Needs ${needed.join(', ')}`);
    }
    return true;
  }
}

@Controller(admin)
@UseGuards(RolesGuard)
@Roles(['admin'])
export class AdminController {
  @Handle(admin.stats)
  stats(): void {}
}
```

## Global enhancers

`AppOptions` applies middleware and enhancers to every route:

```ts
export const appOptions: AppOptions = {
  basePath: '/api',
  middleware: [cors({ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true })],
  guards: [SessionGuard],
  interceptors: [LogDuration],
  filters: [DbErrors],
};
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/server/pipeline

---

# Testing the server

Server tests run in process: no port, no network. `Test.createTestingModule()` from `@usevibejs/server/testing` builds the same `App` as production from the modules you list, and `app.fetch` serves the requests.

```ts
const app = await Test.createTestingModule({
  imports: [TodosModule],
  basePath: '/api',
  logger: new JsonLogger({ level: 'silent' }),
}).compile();
const api = createClient({ todos }, { baseUrl: '/api', fetch: app.fetch });

const result = await api.todos.list();
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(result.error.code);
expect(result.data).toEqual(['write tests']);

await app.close();
```

`createTestingModule()` takes module options (`imports`, `providers`, `controllers`) and application options (`basePath`, `logger`, `guards`, …) in one object. Spread `appOptions` from `app.module.ts` to test with the production options.

Calling routes through `createClient` checks the contract too: a test fails to compile when a route, an input or a response type changes. Narrow the result as the UI does:

```ts
const api = createClient({ todos }, { baseUrl: '/api', fetch: app.fetch });
const removed = await api.todos.remove({ params: { id: 'missing' } });
if (removed.ok || removed.error.code !== 'TODO_NOT_FOUND') throw new Error('expected a 404');
expect(removed.error.status).toBe(404);
```

For requests outside a contract, such as a missing route or a malformed body, use `app.request(path, init?)`; `init.json` sends a JSON body.

## Replacing providers

`overrideProvider(token)` replaces a provider by its token in every module that provides it, before anything is created:

```ts
const sent: string[] = [];
const app = await Test.createTestingModule({
  imports: [MailModule],
  logger: new JsonLogger({ level: 'silent' }),
})
  .overrideProvider(Mailer)
  .useValue({ send: (to: string) => (sent.push(to), to) })
  .compile();

app.get(Mailer).send('ada@example.com');
```

`useValue`, `useClass` and `useFactory` are available. Overriding a token that no module provides fails with [VIBE9701](https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9701). `app.get(token)` reads a provider, such as a service whose state a test checks.

## Logs

Pass `logger: new JsonLogger({ level: 'silent' })` to keep test output clean, or a `JsonLogger` with a `write` function to assert on log entries. The framework's own request, error and lifecycle logs go to this logger; overriding `Logger` reaches only the code that injects it.

## Checking the graph

`inspect(root, options)` lists the routes and modules without creating anything. A snapshot of it catches an unintended route, guard or module change:

```ts
expect(inspect(AppModule, appOptions)).toMatchSnapshot();
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/server/testing

---
