Run `vibejs <command> --help --json` for the same reference as JSON.

| Command | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`vibejs explain`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/explain) | Explain a VIBE error code from the bundled catalog, offline. |
| [`vibejs docs`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/docs) | Look up a VIBE code, open a docs page by path, or search the bundled docs, offline. |
| [`vibejs check`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/check) | Type-check, lint, format-check and test the project with coverage, concurrently. |
| [`vibejs dev`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/dev) | Serve the UI and the backend on one port, restarting the backend on server changes. |
| [`vibejs build`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/build) | Build the UI into ui/dist and the server into server/dist/main.js. |
| [`vibejs errors`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/errors) | List the unresolved build errors and the latest runtime errors from .vibejs/dev.log. |
| [`vibejs logs`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/logs) | Show the newest .vibejs/dev.log entries, filtered by level, source, text and time. |
| [`vibejs agents`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/agents) | Write the vibe.js rules into AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, the vibejs-* skills into .agents/skills and .claude/skills, and the vibejs server into .mcp.json. |
| [`vibejs routes`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/routes) | List the API routes and the UI routes, without starting a server or running UI code. |
| [`vibejs di`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/di) | Show the modules and providers of the backend, without constructing any provider. |
| [`vibejs components`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/components) | List the .vibe components with their props, models and types, without running them. |
| [`vibejs request`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/request) | Call an API route: through the running dev server, or in process when none runs. |
| [`vibejs generate`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/generate) | Add a resource, a component or a page with its tests, and register it. |
| [`vibejs mcp`](https://vibejs.org/v0/cli/mcp) | Serve the --json commands to coding agents as MCP tools over stdio. |

## Global options

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | Print one JSON object (on by default in agent mode). |
| `--help`, `-h` | boolean | Describe the commands and their options. |
| `--version` | boolean | Print the vibejs version. |

| `name` | yes |  |

# vibejs logs

Show the newest .vibejs/dev.log entries, filtered by level, source, text and time.

```sh

```

## Options

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--limit` | string | Show at most N entries (default 50). |
| `--level` | string | The lowest level shown: error, warn, info or debug. |
| `--source` | string | Only this source: vite, browser, server or vibejs. |
| `--grep` | string | Only messages that contain TEXT, ignoring case. |
| `--since` | string | Only entries since an ISO time or &lt;n>s, &lt;n>m, &lt;n>h ago. |

## Examples

```sh

vibejs logs --source server --since 5m
```

# Error codes

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/

---

# VIBE1001: Missing template block

> The component has no `<template>` block.

Every `.vibe` file renders its `<template>` block. A file with only a script or a style has nothing to render.

### Fix

- Add a `<template>` block with the markup of the component.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1001

---

# VIBE1002: Second template block

> The component has a second `<template>` block, and only the first one is used.

A component has exactly one template. The compiler keeps the first `<template>` block and ignores the others.

### Fix

- Merge the markup of both blocks into the first `<template>` block.
- Move the second template into its own `.vibe` file and use it as a component.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1002

---

# VIBE1003: Second script setup block

> The component has a second `<script setup>` block, and only the first one is used.

All of a component's code lives in one `<script setup lang="ts">` block. The compiler keeps the first `<script setup>` block and ignores the others.

### Fix

- Merge the code of both blocks into the first `<script setup lang="ts">` block.
- Move shared code into a `.ts` module and import it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1003

---

# VIBE1004: Script block without setup

> The `<script>` block has no `setup` attribute.

A component's script always runs as its setup function, so the block must be `<script setup lang="ts">`. Component options such as the name or `inheritAttrs` go in `defineOptions()`.

### Fix

- Write the block as `<script setup lang="ts">`.
- Move component options into a `defineOptions()` call inside `<script setup lang="ts">`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1004

---

# VIBE1005: Script language is not TypeScript

> The `<script setup>` block needs `lang="ts"` but has {lang}.

Component scripts are TypeScript, so templates and props can be type-checked. Plain JavaScript is valid TypeScript, so existing code keeps working after adding `lang="ts"`.

### Fix

- Write the block as `<script setup lang="ts">`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1005

---

# VIBE1006: Block with a src attribute

> The `<{block}>` block has a `src` attribute.

A block's content is written inside the `.vibe` file. Loading it from another file with `src` is not supported.

### Fix

- Move the content of the referenced file into the `<{block}>` block and remove `src`.
- Import TypeScript from another module inside `<script setup lang="ts">`, or CSS with `@import` inside `<style>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1006

---

# VIBE1007: CSS module style

> The `<style>` block has a `module` attribute, and CSS modules are not supported.

Component styles are global or `scoped`. CSS modules, which expose class names to the script, are not available.

### Fix

- Remove `module` and use `<style scoped>` to keep the styles local to the component.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1007

---

# VIBE1008: Template language

> The `<template>` block has `{attr}`, but templates are plain HTML.

Templates are written in HTML. Template preprocessors are not supported.

### Fix

- Remove `lang` and write the template in HTML.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1008

---

# VIBE1009: Unknown style language

> The `<style>` block has `{attr}`, which is not one of `css`, `scss`, `sass`, `less`, `styl`, `stylus` or `postcss`.

The style language selects the CSS preprocessor that compiles the block. Without `lang`, the block is plain CSS.

### Fix

- Use one of `css`, `scss`, `sass`, `less`, `styl`, `stylus` or `postcss` as `lang`.
- Remove `lang` for plain CSS.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1009

---

# VIBE1010: Unknown block attribute

> The `<{block}>` block does not accept the attribute `{name}`.

`<template>` takes no attributes, `<script>` takes `setup` and `lang`, and `<style>` takes `scoped` and `lang`.

### Fix

- Remove `{name}` from the `<{block}>` block.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1010

---

# VIBE1011: Unknown root block

> `<{tag}>` is not a component block.

At the top level, a `.vibe` file holds one `<template>`, one `<script setup lang="ts">` and any number of `<style>` blocks. Other blocks are not supported.

### Fix

- Move `<{tag}>` into the `<template>` block if it is markup.
- Remove the `<{tag}>` block.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1011

---

# VIBE1012: Text outside of a block

> Text is outside of every block.

At the top level, a `.vibe` file holds only blocks, comments and whitespace.

### Fix

- Move the text into the `<template>` block.
- Wrap the text in an HTML comment `<!-- -->`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1012

---

# VIBE1013: Generic script

> The `<script setup>` block has a `generic` attribute, and generic components are not supported.

A component's props have one type. Type parameters on a component are not available.

### Fix

- Remove `generic` and give the props a concrete type, such as a union of the supported types.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1013

---

# VIBE1101: CDATA section in HTML

> A CDATA section `<![CDATA[ ]]>` is allowed only inside `<svg>` or `<math>`.

This is the HTML parse error `cdata-in-html-content`. In HTML content, the browser reads a CDATA section as a comment, so its text is dropped.

### Fix

- Write the text without `<![CDATA[` and `]]>`, escaping `<` as `&lt;` and `&` as `&amp;`.
- Move the CDATA section inside an `<svg>` or `<math>` element.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1101

---

# VIBE1102: Duplicate attribute

> The attribute `{name}` appears more than once on this element.

This is the HTML parse error `duplicate-attribute`. An element has each attribute at most once.

### Fix

- Remove the second `{name}`.
- Merge both values into one `{name}` attribute.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1102

---

# VIBE1105: End of file after `<`

> The file ends after `<` before a tag name.

This is the HTML parse error `eof-before-tag-name`.

### Fix

- Complete the tag, as in `<div>`.
- Write `&lt;` for a literal `<`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1105

---

# VIBE1106: End of file in a CDATA section

> The file ends inside a CDATA section that has no `]]>`.

This is the HTML parse error `eof-in-cdata`.

### Fix

- Close the CDATA section with `]]>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1106

---

# VIBE1107: End of file in a comment

> The file ends inside a comment that has no `-->`.

This is the HTML parse error `eof-in-comment`. Everything after `<!--` became part of the comment.

### Fix

- Close the comment with `-->`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1107

---

# VIBE1109: End of file in a tag

> The file ends inside a tag that has no `>`.

This is the HTML parse error `eof-in-tag`. The unfinished tag is dropped.

### Fix

- Close the tag with `>`.
- Close the quote of the last attribute value.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1109

---

# VIBE1113: Missing attribute value

> The attribute `{name}` has `=` but no value.

This is the HTML parse error `missing-attribute-value`.

### Fix

- Write the value after `=`, as in `{name}="value"`.
- Remove `=` for an attribute without a value.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1113

---

# VIBE1114: End tag without a name

> `</>` is an end tag without a tag name.

This is the HTML parse error `missing-end-tag-name`. The parser ignores it.

### Fix

- Write the name of the element to close, as in `</div>`.
- Remove `</>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1114

---

# VIBE1117: Unexpected character in an attribute name

> The attribute name contains `{char}`, which is not allowed in attribute names.

This is the HTML parse error `unexpected-character-in-attribute-name`. Attribute names cannot contain `"`, `'` or `<`; the character is often a missing `=` or a missing space.

### Fix

- Add the missing `=` before the quote of the value.
- Add a space between two attributes.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1117

---

# VIBE1118: Unexpected character in an unquoted attribute value

> The unquoted attribute value contains `{char}`.

This is the HTML parse error `unexpected-character-in-unquoted-attribute-value`. Unquoted values cannot contain `"`, `'`, `<`, `=` or `` ` ``.

### Fix

- Quote the value, as in `name="value"`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1118

---

# VIBE1119: Attribute name starting with `=`

> An attribute name starts with `=`.

This is the HTML parse error `unexpected-equals-sign-before-attribute-name`. The `=` has no attribute name before it.

### Fix

- Write the attribute name before `=`, as in `id="main"`.
- Remove the extra `=`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1119

---

# VIBE1121: Processing instruction in HTML

> `<?` is allowed only inside `<svg>` or `<math>`.

This is the HTML parse error `unexpected-question-mark-instead-of-tag-name`. In HTML content, the browser reads `<?…>` as a comment.

### Fix

- Remove the `<?…>` instruction, such as an XML declaration.
- Write `&lt;?` for literal text.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1121

---

# VIBE1122: Unexpected `/` in a tag

> A `/` inside a tag is not followed by `>`.

This is the HTML parse error `unexpected-solidus-in-tag`. Only a self-closing tag ends with `/>`.

### Fix

- Write `/>` with no space between `/` and `>`.
- Remove the `/`, or quote the attribute value that contains it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1122

---

# VIBE1123: End tag without a start tag

> The end tag `</{tag}>` has no matching start tag.

No open element is named `{tag}`, so the parser ignores the end tag. The start tag may be misspelled, or the element may already be closed.

### Fix

- Remove `</{tag}>`.
- Add the missing `<{tag}>` start tag, or fix the spelling of the end tag.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1123

---

# VIBE1124: Element without an end tag

> The element `<{tag}>` has no end tag.

The element is closed when an outer element closes or at the end of the file, so its content may extend further than intended.

### Fix

- Add `</{tag}>` where the element ends.
- Write `<{tag} />` for an element without content.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1124

---

# VIBE1125: Unclosed interpolation

> An interpolation has no closing braces.

Everything after the opening double braces, up to the end of the parent element, became part of the expression.

### Fix

- Close the interpolation with two closing braces after the expression.
- Wrap the text in `<span v-pre>` to show the braces as literal text.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1125

---

# VIBE1126: Directive without a name

> The attribute `{name}` is a directive without a name.

An attribute that starts with `v-` names a directive, as in `v-if` or `v-for`.

### Fix

- Write the directive name after `v-`, as in `v-if="ok"`.
- Remove the attribute.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1126

---

# VIBE1127: Dynamic argument without `]`

> The dynamic argument has no closing `]`.

A dynamic argument is written `:[name]="value"`, and it cannot contain spaces.

### Fix

- Close the argument with `]`.
- Remove the spaces from the argument, or compute the name in the script.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1127

---

# VIBE1201: Invalid expression

> The expression is not valid TypeScript: {reason}.

Interpolations and directive values such as `:title`, `v-if` and the source of `v-for` hold exactly one TypeScript expression. Statements, several expressions separated by `;`, and unbalanced brackets or quotes are rejected.

### Fix

- Correct the syntax at the reported position, such as a missing `)` or quote.
- Move multi-step logic into a `computed` value or a function in `<script setup lang="ts">` and use its name in the template.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1201

---

# VIBE1202: Invalid event handler

> The event handler is not valid TypeScript: {reason}.

A `v-on` value is a function name or member path such as `save` or `form.submit`, a function or arrow such as `(e) => save(e)`, or a list of statements such as `count++` or `select(item); close()`. Statements can read the event as `$event`.

### Fix

- Correct the syntax at the reported position.
- Move the handler into a function in `<script setup lang="ts">` and write its name, as in `@click="save"`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1202

---

# VIBE1203: Invalid parameters

> The parameter list is not valid TypeScript: {reason}.

The aliases of `v-for` (`item`, `(item, index)`, a destructuring pattern) and the props of `v-slot` are parameter lists, written as in the parentheses of an arrow function.

### Fix

- Write plain names or a destructuring pattern, as in `v-for="(item, index) in items"`.
- Correct the syntax at the reported position, such as an unclosed pattern.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE1203

---

# VIBE2001: Unknown component

> `<{tag}>` is not a component of this file.

A PascalCase or dotted tag names a component that the template can reach: an import or a binding of `<script setup>`, a namespace binding for a dotted tag such as `Form.Input`, or the file itself by its own name. There are no globally registered components.

### Fix

- Import the component in `<script setup lang="ts">`, as in `import {tag} from './{tag}.vibe'`.
- Fix the spelling of `<{tag}>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2001

---

# VIBE2002: Component tag not in PascalCase

> `<{tag}>` refers to the component `{name}`, and component tags are written in PascalCase.

A tag in kebab case or in lowercase is an element. When the PascalCase form of the tag names a component of the file, the tag is almost certainly meant as that component.

### Fix

- Write the tag as `<{name}>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2002

---

# VIBE2003: Unknown element

> `<{tag}>` is not an HTML, SVG or MathML element.

A lowercase tag without a hyphen must be a standard element. Custom elements have a hyphen in their name, and components are written in PascalCase.

### Fix

- Fix the spelling of `<{tag}>`.
- Write a component tag in PascalCase and import the component.
- Give a custom element a name with a hyphen, as in `<my-{tag}>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2003

---

# VIBE2004: Template without a directive

> A `<template>` element needs `v-if`, `v-else-if`, `v-else`, `v-for` or `v-slot`.

A nested `<template>` only groups content for a directive and renders no element of its own. Without one of those directives it has no meaning.

### Fix

- Add the directive that the group needs, as in `<template v-if="ok">`.
- Replace `<template>` with an element such as `<div>`, or remove it and keep its children.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2004

---

# VIBE2005: Text inside a table or select element

> Text cannot be a direct child of `<{tag}>`.

The HTML parser moves text out of table structure elements and drops it inside `<select>`, so the rendered page would not match the template.

### Fix

- Move the text into a cell, as in `<td>`, or into an `<option>`.
- Remove the text.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2005

---

# VIBE2006: Component without a dynamic is

> `<component>` needs a bound `:is` with a component value.

`<component>` renders the component object its `:is` expression returns. A static `is` attribute or a string literal names no component, because there is no global registry.

### Fix

- Import the component and bind it, as in `<component :is="Item" />`.
- Write the component tag directly, as in `<Item />`, when it never changes.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2006

---

# VIBE2007: Unknown identifier

> `{name}` is not defined in the template.

A template reads the bindings and imports of `<script setup>`, the props, the aliases of `v-for`, the props of `v-slot`, `$attrs`, `$slots`, `$emit`, `$props`, and these globals: `Infinity`, `undefined`, `NaN`, `isFinite`, `isNaN`, `parseFloat`, `parseInt`, `decodeURI`, `decodeURIComponent`, `encodeURI`, `encodeURIComponent`, `Math`, `Number`, `Date`, `Array`, `Object`, `Boolean`, `String`, `RegExp`, `Map`, `Set`, `JSON`, `Intl`, `BigInt`, `console`, `Error` and `Symbol`. When the name is close to one in scope, the first fix names it.

### Fix

- Fix the spelling of `{name}`.
- Declare or import `{name}` in `<script setup lang="ts">`.
- Declare `{name}` as a prop in `defineProps`.
- Read another global, such as `window`, in `<script setup lang="ts">` and use that binding in the template.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2007

---

# VIBE2008: Instance access

> `{name}` is not available in templates.

A template has no component instance: `this` and instance properties such as `$refs`, `$el`, `$nextTick` and `$watch` do not exist. Everything a template reads comes from `<script setup>`, the props, and `$attrs`, `$slots`, `$emit` and `$props`.

### Fix

- Reach an element or a child component with `useTemplateRef('name')` in `<script setup lang="ts">` and a matching `ref="name"`.
- Import `nextTick` or `watch` from `@usevibejs/ui` and call it in `<script setup lang="ts">`.
- Write `$attrs`, `$slots`, `$emit` or a binding of `<script setup lang="ts">` instead of `this`.
- Read the route with `const route = useRoute()` and the router with `useRouter()` in `<script setup lang="ts">`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2008

---

# VIBE2009: is attribute

> The `is` attribute is not supported on `<{tag}>`.

Elements are never replaced by components through `is`. Only `<component>` takes a bound `:is`.

### Fix

- Write the component tag directly, as in `<Item />`.
- Use `<component :is="Item" />` for a component chosen at runtime.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2009

---

# VIBE2010: Reserved local name

> `{name}` is reserved and cannot name a template local.

Names that start with `_` are reserved for generated code in `v-for` aliases and `v-slot` props. `$setup`, `$props` and `$ctx` are the parameters of the render function, so no local in a template, including a parameter or variable inside an expression, may use them.

### Fix

- Rename `{name}`, as in `v-for="item in items"` instead of `v-for="_item in items"`.
- Give a destructured slot prop a new local name, as in `_id: id`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2010

---

# VIBE2011: Script or style in a template

> `<{tag}>` cannot appear inside the template.

Templates render markup only. Code belongs in `<script setup>` and styles in a top-level `<style>` block.

### Fix

- Move the code into `<script setup lang="ts">`.
- Move the styles into a `<style>` or `<style scoped>` block of the file.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2011

---

# VIBE2012: Attribute on a template

> `{name}` has no effect on a `<template>` element.

A `<template>` with `v-if`, `v-else-if`, `v-else`, `v-for` or `v-slot` renders only its children, so attributes, bindings, listeners, `v-model` and `ref` on it would be lost. Only `:key` is kept, as the key of a `v-for` or keyed block.

### Fix

- Move `{name}` onto an element inside the `<template>`.
- Replace the `<template>` with an element such as `<div>` that carries `{name}`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2012

---

# VIBE2101: Condition without expression

> `{directive}` needs a condition.

`v-if` and `v-else-if` render their element when the expression is truthy, so the expression is required.

### Fix

- Write the condition, as in `{directive}="items.length"`.
- Write `v-else` for the last branch of a chain.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2101

---

# VIBE2102: Branch without v-if

> `{directive}` has no `v-if` or `v-else-if` element right before it.

`v-else-if` and `v-else` continue the chain of the previous sibling element. Only whitespace and comments may stand between the branches.

### Fix

- Move the element right after the element with `v-if` or `v-else-if`.
- Replace `{directive}` with `v-if` to start a new chain.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2102

---

# VIBE2103: v-if and v-for on one element

> `v-if` and `v-for` cannot be on the same element.

Which directive applies first is easy to misread, so the two must be on separate elements.

### Fix

- Wrap the element in `<template v-for="…">` and keep `v-if` on the element.
- Filter the list in a `computed` value and loop over that.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2103

---

# VIBE2104: v-else with a value

> `v-else` takes no value.

`v-else` is the last branch of a chain and renders when no earlier condition holds.

### Fix

- Remove the value of `v-else`.
- Write `v-else-if` to test a condition.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2104

---

# VIBE2201: v-for without expression

> `v-for` needs an expression.

`v-for` renders its element once per item of a source, written as `item in items`.

### Fix

- Write the loop, as in `v-for="item in items"`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2201

---

# VIBE2202: Malformed v-for

> The `v-for` expression must have the form `alias in source`.

The aliases name the item and optionally its key and index, as in `(item, index) in items`, and the source follows `in` or `of`.

### Fix

- Write the loop as `item in items` or `(item, index) in items`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2202

---

# VIBE2203: v-for without key

> Elements rendered by `v-for` need a `:key`.

The key identifies each item, so moved items keep their elements and state. Only a numeric range such as `n in 10` needs none.

### Fix

- Add a unique, stable key, as in `:key="item.id"`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2203

---

# VIBE2204: Key on a child of template v-for

> `:key` belongs on the `<template v-for>`, not on its child.

The children of `<template v-for>` render together as one item, which is identified by the key of the `<template>` element.

### Fix

- Move `:key` to the `<template v-for>` element.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2204

---

# VIBE2301: v-on without expression

> `{name}` needs a handler.

An event listener calls its handler: a function name, a function or a statement list.

### Fix

- Write the handler, as in `{name}="save"`.
- Remove `{name}`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2301

---

# VIBE2302: v-on with an object

> `v-on` needs an event name and cannot take an object of listeners.

Each event is written as its own attribute, so the listeners of an element are visible in the template.

### Fix

- Write one `@event="handler"` attribute per event.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2302

---

# VIBE2303: Dynamic event name

> The event name of `v-on` must be static.

Listeners are attached for names known at compile time.

### Fix

- Write a static event name and decide inside the handler what to do.
- Attach the listener with `addEventListener` from a template ref.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2303

---

# VIBE2304: Unknown event modifier

> `.{modifier}` is not an event modifier.

The modifiers are `stop`, `prevent`, `self`, `exact`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`, `meta`, `left`, `middle`, `right`, `once`, `capture` and `passive`. Key names such as `enter` or `page-down` are modifiers only on `keydown`, `keyup` and `keypress`.

### Fix

- Fix the spelling of `.{modifier}`.
- Check the key inside the handler.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2304

---

# VIBE2305: Modifier on a component event

> `.{modifier}` cannot modify a component event.

A component event calls its handler with the emitted values, not with a DOM event, so event modifiers do not apply.

### Fix

- Remove `.{modifier}` and handle the case inside the handler.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2305

---

# VIBE2401: v-bind without value

> `{name}` needs a value.

A bound attribute takes an expression. The same-name shorthand, as in `:id` for `:id="id"`, works only when the name is a valid identifier.

### Fix

- Write the value, as in `{name}="value"`.
- Remove the binding.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2401

---

# VIBE2402: Unknown v-bind modifier

> `.{modifier}` is not a `v-bind` modifier.

The modifiers are `prop`, `attr` and `camel`; on components only `camel` applies.

### Fix

- Remove `.{modifier}`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2402

---

# VIBE2501: v-model without expression

> `v-model` needs a target.

`v-model` reads and writes a value, so it needs a variable or a property to bind.

### Fix

- Write the target, as in `v-model="text"`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2501

---

# VIBE2502: v-model target not assignable

> The `v-model` target must be a variable or a property.

The target is written on every change, so it must be an assignable name or member, as in `text` or `form.name`.

### Fix

- Bind a `ref` or a property, as in `v-model="form.name"`.
- Bind a computed value with `:value` and update its source in an `@input` handler.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2502

---

# VIBE2503: v-model on a template local

> `{name}` is a `v-for` or `v-slot` local and cannot be assigned.

Assigning a local would replace the local copy only, not the item in the list or the slot prop.

### Fix

- Bind a property of the item, as in `v-model="item.text"`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2503

---

# VIBE2504: v-model on a prop

> `{name}` is a prop and cannot be assigned.

Props are owned by the parent component.

### Fix

- Declare a two-way value with `defineModel()` and bind it.
- Copy the prop into a `ref` and bind that.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2504

---

# VIBE2505: v-model on a constant

> `{name}` cannot be assigned, because it is an import or a constant that holds no ref.

Only refs, `let` bindings and properties can take the new value.

### Fix

- Hold the value in a `ref`, as in `const {name} = ref(…)`.
- Bind a property of a reactive object.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2505

---

# VIBE2506: v-model on an unsupported element

> `v-model` is not supported on `<{tag}>`.

`v-model` works on `<input>`, `<textarea>`, `<select>` and on components.

### Fix

- Use `<input>`, `<textarea>` or `<select>`.
- Bind the value and listen to the event of the element, as in `:value` and `@input`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2506

---

# VIBE2507: v-model with a dynamic type

> `v-model` cannot be used on an `<input>` with a bound `:type`.

The kind of binding, text, checkbox or radio, is chosen at compile time from the `type` attribute.

### Fix

- Write a static `type`.
- Render one `<input>` per type with `v-if`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2507

---

# VIBE2508: v-model on a file input

> `v-model` cannot be used on `<input type="file">`.

A file input is read-only from scripts.

### Fix

- Listen to `@change` and read the files in the handler, as in `(event.target as HTMLInputElement).files`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2508

---

# VIBE2509: v-model argument

> The `v-model` argument `{arg}` is allowed only as a static name on a component.

An argument selects which model of a component to bind. Native elements have a single value, and a model name must be known at compile time.

### Fix

- Remove the argument on native elements.
- Write the model name statically, as in `v-model:title`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2509

---

# VIBE2510: Unknown v-model modifier

> `.{modifier}` is not a `v-model` modifier for this element.

Text inputs and `<textarea>` take `lazy`, `number` and `trim`; `<select>` takes `number`; checkboxes and radio buttons take none.

### Fix

- Remove `.{modifier}`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2510

---

# VIBE2511: Value next to v-model

> `:value` cannot be combined with `v-model` on a text input.

`v-model` already sets the value of the input.

### Fix

- Remove `:value`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2511

---

# VIBE2601: Misplaced v-slot

> `v-slot` can only be used on a component or on a `<template>` that is a direct child of a component.

Slot content belongs to the component that renders it.

### Fix

- Move `v-slot` to the component or to a `<template>` directly inside it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2601

---

# VIBE2602: Mixed v-slot usage

> `v-slot` on the component cannot be combined with `<template v-slot>` children.

With `v-slot` on the component, all its children are that slot. With named slots, every slot needs its own `<template>`.

### Fix

- Move the content of the component slot into a `<template #default>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2602

---

# VIBE2603: Duplicate slot

> The slot `{name}` is passed more than once.

Each slot of a component is passed once. Conditional slot templates with `v-if` and `v-else` may share a name.

### Fix

- Merge the content of both slots.
- Rename one of the slots.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2603

---

# VIBE2604: Extraneous default slot content

> The default slot is passed both as `<template #default>` and as loose children.

Content outside named slot templates becomes the default slot.

### Fix

- Move the loose children into `<template #default>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2604

---

# VIBE2605: Dynamic slot name

> Slot names must be static.

Slots are passed by names known at compile time.

### Fix

- Write a static name, and use `v-if` on slot templates to choose between them.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2605

---

# VIBE2606: v-for on a slot

> `v-for` cannot be used on a slot template.

A component receives a fixed set of slots.

### Fix

- Put the `v-for` on an element inside the slot template.
- Pass the list as a prop and let the component render its slot per item.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2606

---

# VIBE2607: Dynamic slot outlet name

> The name of a `<slot>` must be static.

Slot outlets are rendered by names known at compile time.

### Fix

- Write a static `name`, and use `v-if` to choose between outlets.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2607

---

# VIBE2608: Unsupported attribute on slot

> `{name}` cannot be used on `<slot>`.

A `<slot>` takes its `name`, props passed to the slot, `v-bind`, `v-if`, `v-else-if`, `v-else` and `v-for`. It renders no element of its own.

### Fix

- Move `{name}` to an element inside the slot content.
- Remove `{name}`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2608

---

# VIBE2701: Template ref without useTemplateRef

> `ref="{name}"` has no matching `useTemplateRef('{name}')`.

A string ref fills the template ref declared with the same key.

### Fix

- Declare it in `<script setup lang="ts">`, as in `const {name} = useTemplateRef('{name}')`.
- Fix the spelling of the ref name.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2701

---

# VIBE2702: Invalid function ref

> A bound `:ref` must be a function or a member path that holds one.

A function ref is called with the element or component instance when it mounts and with `null` when it unmounts.

### Fix

- Pass a function, as in `:ref="(el) => (input = el)"`.
- Use a string ref with `useTemplateRef`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2702

---

# VIBE2703: Directive without value

> `{directive}` needs a value.

`v-html` sets the inner HTML and `v-text` the text content of the element from the expression.

### Fix

- Write the value, as in `{directive}="content"`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2703

---

# VIBE2704: Directive on an element with children

> `{directive}` replaces the content of the element, which must be empty.

The children would be overwritten.

### Fix

- Remove the children of the element.
- Remove `{directive}` and render the value as a child.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2704

---

# VIBE2705: v-show without value

> `v-show` needs a condition.

`v-show` hides the element while the condition is falsy.

### Fix

- Write the condition, as in `v-show="open"`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2705

---

# VIBE2706: Element directive on a non-element

> `{directive}` can only be used on an element, not on `<{tag}>`.

`v-show` sets the `display` style, and `v-html` and `v-text` the content, of one element. Components, `<template>` and `<slot>` have no single element of their own.

### Fix

- Wrap the content in an element and put `{directive}` on it.
- Use `v-if` instead of `v-show`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2706

---

# VIBE2901: Teleport is not supported

> `<Teleport>` is not supported.

`<Teleport>` is not a built-in component and no binding of the file has this name.

### Fix

- Render the content where it belongs, or move it with `document.body.append` from a template ref in `onMounted`.
- Import a component named `Teleport` if the file should render one.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2901

---

# VIBE2902: KeepAlive is not supported

> `<KeepAlive>` is not supported.

`<KeepAlive>` is not a built-in component and no binding of the file has this name.

### Fix

- Keep the state in a parent component or a shared module and render the children with `v-if`.
- Import a component named `KeepAlive` if the file should render one.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2902

---

# VIBE2903: Transition is not supported

> `<Transition>` is not supported.

`<Transition>` is not a built-in component and no binding of the file has this name.

### Fix

- Animate with CSS transitions or animations on a class bound with `:class`.
- Import a component named `Transition` if the file should render one.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2903

---

# VIBE2904: TransitionGroup is not supported

> `<TransitionGroup>` is not supported.

`<TransitionGroup>` is not a built-in component and no binding of the file has this name.

### Fix

- Animate list items with CSS animations on their class.
- Import a component named `TransitionGroup` if the file should render one.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2904

---

# VIBE2905: Suspense is not supported

> `<Suspense>` is not supported.

`<Suspense>` is not a built-in component and no binding of the file has this name.

### Fix

- Load async data with `useAsync` and render a loading state with `v-if`.
- Import a component named `Suspense` if the file should render one.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2905

---

# VIBE2906: v-memo is not supported

> `v-memo` is not supported.

Templates update only the bindings whose values change, so a memo is not needed.

### Fix

- Remove `v-memo`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2906

---

# VIBE2907: v-once is not supported

> `v-once` is not supported.

Every binding of a template stays reactive.

### Fix

- Remove `v-once`.
- Read the value once in `<script setup lang="ts">` and render that constant.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2907

---

# VIBE2908: Custom directive

> `v-{name}` is not a built-in directive, and custom directives are not supported.

The built-in directives are `v-bind`, `v-on`, `v-model`, `v-if`, `v-else-if`, `v-else`, `v-for`, `v-slot`, `v-show`, `v-html`, `v-text` and `v-pre`.

### Fix

- Reach the element with `useTemplateRef` and run the code in `onMounted` or a `watch`.
- Move reusable element logic into a composable that takes the template ref.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2908

---

# VIBE2909: v-cloak is not supported

> `v-cloak` is not supported.

Templates are compiled ahead of time, so uncompiled markup is never shown.

### Fix

- Remove `v-cloak`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2909

---

# VIBE2910: Lifecycle listener

> `{name}` is an element lifecycle listener, and lifecycle listeners are not supported.

Element lifecycle listeners such as `@vue:mounted` and `@vnode-mounted` are not events of the rendered element.

### Fix

- Use `onMounted` or `onUnmounted` with a template ref in `<script setup lang="ts">`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE2910

---

# VIBE3001: Value export

> A `<script setup>` block cannot export values.

The block becomes the setup function of the component, so its values exist once per instance and cannot be exported. Types can be exported with `export type` and `export interface`.

### Fix

- Move the exported value into a `.ts` module and import it here and wherever else it is used.
- Export only types, with `export type` or `export interface`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3001

---

# VIBE3002: Top-level await

> `await` cannot be used at the top level of `<script setup>`.

The setup function of a component runs synchronously, so it cannot wait at its top level.

### Fix

- Start the work inside an `async` function and store the result in a `ref` when it arrives.
- Await inside a function that an event or a `watch` callback calls.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3002

---

# VIBE3003: Invalid script

> The script is not valid TypeScript: {reason}.

The script could not be parsed, so its bindings and macros are unknown. The reason is the parser's own message, and the range points at the token where parsing stopped.

### Fix

- Correct the syntax at the reported position, such as a missing bracket, quote or comma.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3003

---

# VIBE3004: Misplaced macro

> `{macro}()` must be a top-level statement or the initializer of a top-level `const`.

The compiler macros run while the component compiles, so each call stands on its own at the top level of the script, as a statement or as the only initializer of a `const` declaration. `{macro}` is the name of the macro.

### Fix

- Move the call to the top level of the script and assign it with its own `const`, as in `const emit = defineEmits<Events>()`.
- Split a declaration with several variables so the macro call has its own `const`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3004

---

# VIBE3005: Macro called twice

> `{macro}()` is called more than once.

A component declares its props, events, slots, exposed value and options once. `{macro}` is the name of the macro.

### Fix

- Merge both declarations into the first `{macro}()` call and remove the second one.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3005

---

# VIBE3006: withDefaults

> `withDefaults()` is not supported.

Prop defaults are written in the destructuring pattern of `defineProps`, where each default sits next to its prop.

### Fix

- Destructure the props and write each default after its name, as in `size = 'medium'` inside the pattern.

### Example

```ts
const { size = 'medium' } = defineProps<{ size?: 'small' | 'medium' }>();
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3006

---

# VIBE3007: Reserved name

> `{name}` is reserved for the compiled component.

The compiled component declares names such as `__props`, `__ctx`, `_setup`, `_defaults`, `_sfc`, `$setup`, `$props`, `$ctx` and an underscore before each runtime helper, as in `_createIf`. A top-level binding with one of these names would collide with them. `{name}` is the binding.

### Fix

- Rename `{name}`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3007

---

# VIBE3008: Macro imported or declared

> `{macro}` is a compiler macro and cannot be imported or declared.

The compiler macros are available in every `<script setup lang="ts">` block without an import, and the compiler replaces each call. An import or a declaration with the same name would hide the macro. `{macro}` is the name.

### Fix

- Remove the import or the declaration of `{macro}` and call the macro directly.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3008

---

# VIBE3009: Binding shadows a prop

> `{name}` is a prop and also a binding of the script.

The template reads `{name}` from one place only, so a prop and a script binding cannot share a name.

### Fix

- Rename the binding of the script.
- Rename the prop in its type and in the parent components that pass it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3009

---

# VIBE3010: Namespace or import alias

> `{syntax}` declarations cannot be used in `<script setup>`.

The block becomes the body of the setup function, and TypeScript allows namespace declarations and `import x =` aliases only at the top level of a module. `{syntax}` is the declaration.

### Fix

- Move the namespace into a `.ts` module and import it here.
- Write `import x = N.y` as `const x = N.y`, and `import x = require('m')` as an `import` declaration.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3010

---

# VIBE3101: Runtime props declaration

> `defineProps()` takes no arguments; the props are declared by its type argument.

Props are declared with a TypeScript type, as in `defineProps<Props>()`, and defaults are written in the destructuring pattern.

### Fix

- Remove the argument and declare the props as the type argument.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3101

---

# VIBE3102: Missing type argument

> `{macro}()` needs a type argument.

`defineProps`, `defineEmits` and `defineSlots` read their declaration from their type argument, as in `defineProps<Props>()`. `{macro}` is the name of the macro.

### Fix

- Add the type argument, as in `{macro}<Declaration>()`, with `Declaration` declared in this file.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3102

---

# VIBE3103: Unknown prop names

> The prop names cannot be read from the type argument of `defineProps`.

The compiler lists the props of a component without running the type checker. It reads them from a type declared in this file (a type literal, an interface, an alias, `&`, `|`, `Partial`, `Required`, `Readonly`, `Pick` or `Omit` over such types) or from the destructuring pattern.

### Fix

- Destructure the props, so each name is written in the script.
- Declare the props type in this file, as an interface or a type literal.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3103

---

# VIBE3104: Rest element in props

> `...{name}` collects the remaining props, which is not supported.

A props destructure names each prop it reads. Attributes that are not props fall through to the root element and are available as `$attrs`. `{name}` is the rest binding.

### Fix

- Name each prop in the destructuring pattern and remove `...{name}`.
- Read attributes that are not props with `$attrs` in the template.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3104

---

# VIBE3105: Default reads a script binding

> The default of `{prop}` reads `{name}`, which is declared in the script.

Prop defaults are evaluated outside the setup function, where the bindings of the script do not exist yet. Literals, globals and imports are available.

### Fix

- Write the default as a literal, or compute it from imported values.
- Move `{name}` into a `.ts` module and import it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3105

---

# VIBE3106: Assignment to a prop

> `{name}` is a destructured prop and cannot be assigned.

Props belong to the parent component and are read-only inside the child.

### Fix

- Declare a two-way value with `defineModel()` and assign its `value`.
- Emit an event and let the parent change the value it passes.
- Copy the prop into a `ref` for a local value that starts from the prop.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3106

---

# VIBE3107: Destructured prop passed by value

> `{name}` is a destructured prop passed directly to `{fn}()`, which receives its current value only.

A destructured prop reads the current prop value each time it is used. Passed to `{fn}()`, it is read once, so later changes are not seen.

### Fix

- Pass a getter instead, as in `{fn}(() => {name})`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3107

---

# VIBE3108: Unsupported props pattern

> A props destructure supports only names, renames and defaults.

Each property of the pattern names a prop (`title`), renames it (`title: heading`) or gives it a default (`title = 'Untitled'`). Computed keys and nested patterns are not supported.

### Fix

- Destructure the prop by its name and read nested values from it in the code.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3108

---

# VIBE3201: Runtime events declaration

> `defineEmits()` takes no arguments; the events are declared by its type argument.

Events are declared with a TypeScript type whose properties are the event names and whose values are the payload tuples.

### Fix

- Remove the argument and declare the events as the type argument.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3201

---

# VIBE3202: Events type is not a record of tuples

> The events type must be a record of payload tuples.

Each property of the events type is an event name, and its type is the tuple of arguments the event passes. Call signatures, method signatures and other value types are not supported.

### Fix

- Write each event as a property whose type is the tuple of its arguments, such as `pick: [id: string]`.

### Example

```ts
const emit = defineEmits<{ pick: [id: string]; close: [] }>();
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3202

---

# VIBE3203: Events type from another file

> The events type `{type}` is not declared in this file.

The compiler lists the events of a component without running the type checker, so it reads them from a type declared in this file. `{type}` is the type argument.

### Fix

- Declare the events type in this file, as an interface or a type literal.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3203

---

# VIBE3311: Runtime slots declaration

> `defineSlots()` takes no arguments; the slots are declared by its type argument.

Slots are declared with a TypeScript type whose properties are the slot names and whose values are functions of the slot props.

### Fix

- Remove the argument and declare the slots as the type argument.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3311

---

# VIBE3321: Unsupported defineModel call

> This `defineModel()` call is not supported: {reason}.

A model is assigned to a `const`, optionally named by a string literal, and optionally configured by an object literal with a boolean `required` and a `default` function, as in `const title = defineModel<string>('title', { required: true })`. `{reason}` says which part is not supported.

### Fix

- Assign the model to a `const`, as in `const value = defineModel<string>()`.
- Name the model with a string literal and pass only `required: true` or `default: () => value` as options.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3321

---

# VIBE3322: Duplicate model

> `{name}` is already declared as a model or a prop.

Each model adds a prop named after it, so its name is unique among the models and the props. `{name}` is the model name.

### Fix

- Give the model another name.
- Remove the prop or the second model of the same name.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3322

---

# VIBE3331: Unsupported component options

> `defineOptions()` takes an object literal with only a string `name` and a boolean `inheritAttrs`.

The options are read while the component compiles, so they are literals.

### Fix

- Pass literal values, such as `name: 'TodoList'` and `inheritAttrs: false`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE3331

---

# VIBE4001: CSS syntax error

> The CSS of a scoped style block has a syntax error: {reason}.

A `<style scoped>` block is parsed as plain CSS after any preprocessor has run, so the position points into the CSS that the compiler received. Typical causes are an unclosed `{`, string, comment or bracket, and text that is not a declaration, rule or at-rule.

### Fix

- Close the block, string, comment or bracket that starts at the reported position.
- Write a declaration as `property: value;` inside a rule.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4001

---

# VIBE4002: Slot content selector

> `{selector}` is not supported in component styles.

A selector that targets the content a parent passes into a slot is not available. The parent styles its own slot content.

### Fix

- Style the slot content in the `<style scoped>` block of the component that passes it.
- Wrap the selector in `:global()` to write a global rule.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4002

---

# VIBE4003: Binding in CSS

> `v-bind()` is not supported in component styles.

Style values cannot read component state from CSS. Bind the value in the template instead.

### Fix

- Set a CSS custom property such as `--color` with `:style` in the template, and read it with `var(--color)`.
- Bind a class or style in the template with `:class` or `:style`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4003

---

# VIBE4004: Deprecated deep selector

> `{selector}` is not supported in component styles.

The `>>>`, `/deep/`, `::v-deep` and `::v-global` forms are not available. Scoped styles reach into child components with `:deep()` and write global rules with `:global()`.

### Fix

- Write `:deep(.child)` to style `.child` inside child components.
- Write `:global(.name)` for a rule that is not scoped.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4004

---

# VIBE4005: Malformed :deep() or :global()

> {escape} needs exactly one selector as its argument.

`:deep(selector)` styles elements of child components, and `:global(selector)` writes a selector without the component scope. Each one takes exactly one selector. Without an argument, with an empty argument or with a comma-separated list, the compiler cannot tell which part of the selector to leave unscoped.

### Fix

- Wrap exactly one selector, such as `:deep(.child)` or `:global(.theme-dark)`.
- Split a list into one escape per selector, such as `:deep(.a), :deep(.b)`.

### Example

```css
.list :deep(.item) {
  color: red;
}
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4005

---

# VIBE4901: Component imported on the server

> `{file}` is imported by server code, but `.vibe` components run only in the browser.

vibe.js renders components on the client. A server environment, such as server-side rendering or a Node test environment, cannot load a `.vibe` file.

### Fix

- Import `.vibe` files only from client code.
- Run component tests in a DOM environment such as jsdom, happy-dom or browser mode.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4901

---

# VIBE4902: Package version mismatch

> `@usevibejs/ui` is at version {ui}, but `@usevibejs/compiler` is at version {compiler}.

Compiled components call the runtime of `@usevibejs/ui` through an interface that changes with each release, so the compiler and the runtime must have the same version. The version `none` means that `@usevibejs/ui` is not installed in the project.

### Fix

- Install the same version of every `@usevibejs/*` package.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE4902

---

# VIBE5001: Value cannot be made reactive

> {api}() received {value}, which is not an object, so it was returned as-is.

Only objects can be wrapped in a reactive or readonly proxy. A primitive value is returned unchanged and nothing tracks it.

### Fix

- Wrap a primitive value in `ref()` instead of {api}().
- Pass an object, an array, a `Map` or a `Set` to {api}().

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5001

---

# VIBE5002: Mutation of a readonly target

> Cannot {operation} {key}: the target is readonly.

A proxy created by `readonly()` or `shallowReadonly()` ignores writes, deletes and collection mutations, so the target keeps its value and nothing is triggered. The message quotes the key, or says `all entries` for `clear()`.

### Fix

- Mutate the reactive source that the readonly proxy wraps.
- Pass the source to `reactive()` instead of `readonly()` where it must be writable.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5002

---

# VIBE5003: Write to a readonly computed

> Cannot assign to the value of a computed ref that was created with a getter only.

A computed ref created with `computed(getter)` derives its value from the refs its getter reads, so assigning to its `value` has no effect.

### Fix

- Write to the refs that the getter reads instead.
- Pass an object with `get` and `set` functions to `computed()` when it must be writable.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5003

---

# VIBE5004: toRefs on a non-reactive object

> toRefs() received a plain object, so its refs will not track changes.

`toRefs()` creates one ref per key that reads and writes the source object. Without a reactive source, nothing tracks reads, so a change made through the object directly does not update readers of the refs.

### Fix

- Pass the object to `reactive()` first and call `toRefs()` on the result.
- Use `ref()` for each value when the object does not need to stay in sync.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5004

---

# VIBE5005: Run on a stopped effect scope

> Cannot run a function in an effect scope that has already been stopped.

`run()` on a stopped scope returns `undefined` without calling the function, because effects created there could never be stopped.

### Fix

- Create a new scope with `effectScope()` and run the function in it.
- Call `stop()` only after the last `run()` of the scope.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5005

---

# VIBE5006: Cleanup registered with no owner

> {api}() was called with no active effect scope or watcher, so its cleanup will never run.

A cleanup belongs to the effect scope or watcher that is running when it is registered. Outside of one, nothing calls it.

### Fix

- Call {api}() synchronously inside `effectScope().run()`, a component's setup or a watcher.
- Pass `true` as the second argument of {api}() when running without an owner is expected.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5006

---

# VIBE5007: Invalid watch source

> watch() cannot watch a source of type {type}: it is not a ref, a getter, a reactive object or an array of these.

`watch()` tracks what its source reads. A plain value, or an object that is not reactive, has nothing to track, so the watcher never fires. In an array of sources, each invalid item reads as `undefined`.

### Fix

- Pass a getter that reads the value, as in `watch(() => state.count, callback)`.
- Pass the object through `reactive()` before watching it, or watch a ref.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5007

---

# VIBE5101: Too many recursive updates

> A scheduled job ({component}) ran 100 times in one flush and was queued again, so it was skipped: a watcher or an update writes a value that it also reads.

Each write to a value that a job reads queues the job again. When the job writes to that value every time it runs, the queue never empties. In development builds the scheduler stops such a job after 100 runs in one flush and reports this error, so that the rest of the flush still runs.

### Fix

- Derive the value with `computed()` instead of writing it from a watcher of its own source.
- Guard the write with a condition that becomes false once the value is settled.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5101

---

# VIBE5102: Unhandled error

> An error thrown in a {info} was not handled.

The scheduler and watchers catch the errors of the code they run, so that the remaining jobs of the flush still run. An error that nothing handles is printed with this message, and the original error is its `cause`.

### Fix

- Catch the error inside the {info} where it can be handled.
- Read the `cause` of this error for the original error and its stack.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5102

---

# VIBE5201: Attributes not inherited

> The component {name} received attributes, but its template has no single root element to put them on.

Attributes and listeners that a parent passes and the component does not declare as props or events fall through to its root: an element, a component that is the only root, or a `v-if` branch that renders one element. A component with several roots, a `v-for` root or a text root has no single place for them, so they are dropped and this warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Bind the attributes where they belong with `v-bind="$attrs"`, and turn off inheritance with `inheritAttrs: false` in `defineOptions()`.
- Wrap the roots of the template in one element.
- Declare the attribute as a prop with `defineProps()` or the listener as an event with `defineEmits()`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5201

---

# VIBE5202: Undeclared event

> The component {name} emitted {event}, which it does not declare.

`defineEmits()` declares the events of a component. A parent listens to them with `@event`, and the listener of a declared event is not passed down as a fallthrough attribute. An undeclared event still calls a matching listener, but it is missing from the type of the component and its listener also falls through to the root element. This warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Add {event} to the record passed to `defineEmits()`.
- Check the spelling of the event name.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5202

---

# VIBE5203: Prop mutation

> Cannot assign to the prop {key}: props are readonly.

Props flow from the parent to the child. The child reads them and cannot assign to them, so the write is ignored and this warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Emit an event and let the parent change the value it passes, or use `defineModel()` for a two-way binding.
- Copy the prop into a local `ref()` when the child keeps its own value.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5203

---

# VIBE5204: Async setup

> The setup of the component {name} returned a promise: components cannot have an async setup.

A component renders synchronously when it is created, so its `<script setup>` cannot use top-level `await` or return a promise. This error is thrown in every build.

### Fix

- Load async data with `useAsync()` in setup, and render a loading state until `loading` is false.
- Move the `await` into a function that the component calls instead of awaiting in setup.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5204

---

# VIBE5205: Setup-only API called outside setup

> {api}() can only be called synchronously inside a component's setup.

Lifecycle hooks, `provide()`, `inject()`, `useTemplateRef()`, `useAttrs()`, `useSlots()`, `useId()` and `useModel()` belong to the component whose setup is running. Called anywhere else, such as after an `await` or in a timer, there is no component to attach them to, so the call does nothing and this warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Call {api}() at the top level of `<script setup>` or of a composable called from it.
- Call {api}() before the first `await` of the setup code.
- Use `app.runWithContext()` to call `inject()` outside a component.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5205

---

# VIBE5206: Injection not found

> Nothing provides the injection key {key}.

`inject()` looks up the key in the values provided by the parent components and by the app. When no parent and no plugin provides it and no default is given, `inject()` returns `undefined` and this warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Call `provide()` with {key} in a parent component, or `app.provide()` before mounting.
- Pass a default value as the second argument of `inject()`.
- Use the same key object for `provide()` and `inject()`: two `Symbol()` calls create two different keys.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5206

---

# VIBE5207: Invalid dynamic component

> `<component :is>` received {type}, which is not a component.

`<component :is>` renders the component it receives, and nothing for `null` or `undefined`. Any other value, such as a string or a plain object without a render function, cannot be rendered. This error is raised in every build and, like any error of a render, goes to `onErrorCaptured` and `app.config.errorHandler`.

### Fix

- Import the component and pass it to `:is`, not its name as a string.
- Render a native element with its own tag and `v-if` instead of `<component :is>`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5207

---

# VIBE5208: Template ref misuse

> The template ref {key} is registered twice, or a template uses it without a matching useTemplateRef().

Each template ref needs exactly one `useTemplateRef()` with its key in the component that owns the template. A second registration of the same key would leave the first ref empty, and a `ref` attribute without a registration has nowhere to store the element. This warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Call `useTemplateRef('{key}')` once in the setup of the component whose template has `ref="{key}"`.
- Give each template ref its own key.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5208

---

# VIBE5301: Unsupported app API

> app.{api}() is not supported.

A vibe.js app has no global components, custom directives or mixins. Components are imported where they are used, element behavior goes in composables that use template refs, and shared logic goes in composables. The method exists only to report this error, which is thrown in every build.

### Fix

- Import the component in the `<script setup>` that uses it.
- Move the shared logic into a composable, a function that calls the composition API.
- Use `useTemplateRef()` with `onMounted()` instead of a custom directive.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5301

---

# VIBE5302: App already mounted

> The app is already mounted, so the second app.mount() did nothing.

An app renders its root component once. Calling `mount()` again, even after `unmount()`, does not render it again, and this warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Call `createApp()` again for each mount.
- Call `app.mount()` once, after every `app.use()` and `app.provide()`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5302

---

# VIBE5303: Mount target not found

> app.mount() could not find the element {target}.

`app.mount()` takes an element or a CSS selector for one. When the selector matches nothing, the app has nowhere to render, so this error is thrown in every build.

### Fix

- Check that the page has an element that matches {target}, such as `<div id="app"></div>`.
- Run the script after the element exists, for example as a module script, which runs after the document is parsed.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5303

---

# VIBE5304: Invalid or repeated plugin

> app.use() received {problem}.

A plugin is a function or an object with an `install` function, and `app.use()` installs each plugin once. An invalid value or a second install of the same plugin is ignored, and this warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Pass the plugin function or the object with `install` to `app.use()`, not the result of calling it.
- Call `app.use()` once per plugin.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5304

---

# VIBE5305: Unmount before mount

> app.unmount() was called on an app that is not mounted.

An app is unmounted after it was mounted, once. Unmounting an app that was never mounted, or a second time, does nothing, and this warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Call `app.unmount()` only after `app.mount()`.
- Keep track of whether the app is mounted when several places may unmount it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5305

---

# VIBE5401: Invalid v-for source

> v-for cannot iterate over a value of type {type}, so it rendered nothing.

`v-for` iterates over arrays, iterables such as `Map` and `Set`, strings, plain objects (as value, key and index) and a non-negative integer `n` (as `1` to `n`). `null` and `undefined` render nothing without a warning. Any other value, such as a boolean, a function, a negative or a fractional number, renders nothing and reports this warning in development builds.

### Fix

- Pass an array, an iterable, a string, a plain object or a non-negative integer to `v-for`.
- Use `v-if` to skip the list while its source is not ready, or default the source to `[]`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5401

---

# VIBE5402: Duplicate keys in v-for

> Two items of a v-for have the key {key}.

`v-for` matches items across updates by their `:key`. When two items share a key, it cannot tell which DOM nodes belong to which item, so it may recreate nodes or keep the state of the wrong item. This warning is reported in development builds.

### Fix

- Key each item by a value that is unique within the list, such as its id.
- Remove the duplicate items from the source before rendering it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5402

---

# VIBE5501: HMR record missing

> Hot module replacement found no record for the component {id}, so the page was reloaded.

In development builds, each `.vibe` module registers its component for hot module replacement when it first loads, and later edits update the live instances through that record. An update for a component without a record cannot be applied in place, so the page reloads instead.

### Fix

- Save the file again, or reload the page, to load the component with its record.
- Load the `.vibe` module through the vibe.js Vite plugin, which adds the registration to each component in development.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5501

---

# VIBE5900: Tooling module executed

> @usevibejs/ui/tooling only declares types for .vibe type checking and cannot run.

`@usevibejs/ui/tooling` holds the macros and the helpers that the type checker sees in the virtual code of a `.vibe` file. The compiler replaces the macros, so a built app never loads this module.

### Fix

- Import runtime APIs from `@usevibejs/ui`.
- Call macros only inside a `.vibe` `<script setup>`, where the compiler replaces them.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE5900

---

# VIBE6001: Unknown content mapper option

> The `@usevibejs/language-tools` content mapper takes no options, but the `contentMappers` entry sets `{option}`.

The content mapper has no settings: every `.vibe` file is type-checked the same strict way. An `options` object in the `contentMappers` entry of `tsconfig.json` is not read.

### Fix

- Remove `{option}` from the `options` of the `@usevibejs/language-tools` entry in `contentMappers`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6001

---

# VIBE6002: UTF-16 positions not offered

> The TypeScript host does not offer UTF-16 positions, which the content mapper needs.

The content mapper reports every position as a UTF-16 offset, the unit of JavaScript strings. A TypeScript version that offers only other position encodings cannot use it.

### Fix

- Update `typescript` to the version that `@usevibejs/language-tools` supports.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6002

---

# VIBE6010: Unused @vibe-expect-error directive

> This `<!-- @vibe-expect-error -->` suppresses no type error.

A `<!-- @vibe-expect-error -->` comment in the template expects a type error in the element or interpolation right after it (whitespace and other comments in between are skipped). It reports itself when there is no error to suppress:

- No error below it: the code it covers type-checks, for example after the error was fixed.
- Nothing to cover: the next sibling is text, there is no next sibling, the comment is inside the element of another `@vibe-expect-error`, or the element is not type-checked (a plain `<template>`).

### Fix

- Remove the comment when the error below it is fixed.
- Move the comment right before the element or interpolation whose error it expects.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6010

---

# VIBE6090: Internal content mapper error

> The content mapper failed on this file: {reason}

This is a bug in vibe.js, not in your code. The file is type-checked as an empty module until the bug is fixed.

### Fix

- Report the bug with this file at https://github.com/vibejs/vibejs/issues.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6090

---

# VIBE6101: TypeScript 7 extension missing

> Install the {extension} extension to type-check .vibe files.

The extension hands `.vibe` files to the TypeScript 7 extension, which runs the project's content mapper. Without it, `.vibe` files are highlighted but not type-checked.

### Fix

- Install `TypeScriptTeam.native-preview` from the Marketplace or Open VSX, then reload the window.
- Keep working without it: highlighting and editing rules work on their own.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6101

---

# VIBE6102: Untrusted workspace

> Trust this workspace to type-check .vibe files.

Type checking runs the project's content mapper, which is project code, so VS Code allows it only in a trusted workspace. In Restricted Mode, `.vibe` files are highlighted but not type-checked.

### Fix

- Run "Manage Workspace Trust" and trust the folder.
- Open the repository root, the folder that contains the project's `node_modules`, so that trust covers the whole project.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE6102

---

# VIBE7101: Invalid route path

> The route path {path} is invalid: {reason}.

A route path is a list of segments separated by `/`. Each segment is either static text or exactly one param: `:name`, then an optional `(regex)`, then an optional `?` (optional), `*` (zero or more) or `+` (one or more). `createRouter()` checks every path, so an invalid one fails at startup.

### Fix

- Give each param its own segment: `/files/:name` instead of `/file.:ext` or `/:a-:b`.
- Remove `\` escapes and any `/` from param regexes, and close every parenthesis.
- Give a param at most one non-empty regex: `:id(\d+)`, not `:id()` or `:id(a)(b)`.
- Remove `?` and `#` from static text, and `.` and `..` segments, which a URL removes or reads as a query or a hash.
- Check that the param regex compiles with `new RegExp()`.
- Start every top-level path with `/`; only child paths are relative.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7101

---

# VIBE7102: Duplicate route name

> The route name {name} is used by more than one route.

Navigation by name needs every name to point to exactly one route.

### Fix

- Rename one of the routes named {name}.
- Remove the `name` of a route that is only reached by its path.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7102

---

# VIBE7103: Unsupported router option

> {option} in {where} is not supported: {deferral}.

`createRouter()` accepts `history`, `routes` and `scrollBehavior`, and a route record accepts `path`, `name`, `component`, `props`, `children`, `redirect`, `meta` and `beforeEnter`. Any other key fails, so that a misspelled or unsupported option is never ignored silently.

### Fix

- Remove {option} from {where}.
- Check the spelling of {option} against the supported keys.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7103

---

# VIBE7104: Missing route param

> The route {route} needs a value for its param {param}.

A named navigation builds the path from `params`. A required param must have a non-empty value.

### Fix

- Pass the param {param} in `params` when navigating to {route}.
- Mark the param optional in the route path with `?` or `*` when the route works without it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7104

---

# VIBE7105: Unknown route name

> No route is named {name}.

A navigation by `name`, `router.resolve()` and `RouterLink` look the name up among the routes passed to `createRouter()`, nested children included. A name that no route declares cannot be turned into a path, so the navigation throws.

### Fix

- Use the `name` of a route passed to `createRouter()`.
- Navigate by path when the route has no name.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7105

---

# VIBE7106: No route matches

> No route matches the path {path}.

The navigation continues with an empty `matched` list, so nothing is rendered for it. This is a warning, printed in development builds only.

### Fix

- Add a route for {path}.
- Add a catch-all route last, such as `/:pathMatch(.*)*`, to show a not-found page.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7106

---

# VIBE7107: Guard with a next parameter

> The navigation guard {guard} declares {count} parameters, but a guard takes only to and from.

A navigation guard decides with its return value, so there is no third callback parameter to call.

### Fix

- Return `false` to cancel the navigation, a location to redirect, or nothing to continue.
- Remove the third parameter of {guard}.

### Example

```ts
router.beforeEach((to) => {
  if (to.meta.requiresAuth && !isSignedIn()) return { name: 'login' };
  if (to.meta.locked) return false;
});
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7107

---

# VIBE7108: Redirect loop

> The navigation to {path} redirected more than 10 times.

Route redirects and guard redirects share one counter per navigation. More than 10 redirects usually mean that two routes or guards redirect to each other.

### Fix

- Make the guard return nothing when `to` is already the redirect target.
- Remove the `redirect` that points back to a route that redirects to it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7108

---

# VIBE7109: Lazy route component failed to load

> The component of the route {path} failed to load.

The `cause` of the error is the rejection of the loader. After a deploy, an open page can request a chunk that no longer exists.

### Fix

- Handle the error in `router.onError()`, for example by loading `to.fullPath` as a full page.
- Check that the loader of {path} imports an existing file.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7109

---

# VIBE7110: Lazy loader returned no component

> The loader of the route {path} resolved to {type}, not a component.

A lazy `component` is a function that returns a promise of a component or of a module whose `default` export is a component.

### Fix

- Return the module from the loader, as in `() => import('./Page.vibe')`.
- Export the component as the `default` export of the loaded module.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7110

---

# VIBE7111: No router installed

> {api} needs a router, but the app has none installed.

The router composables read the router that `app.use(router)` provides. They work in the setup of a component of that app, and in guards, redirects, lazy loaders and `afterEach` hooks of the router.

### Fix

- Install the router with `app.use(router)` before mounting the app.
- In a test, pass the router in the `plugins` option of `mount()`.
- Call {api} in a component's setup, not in a timer or an event handler.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7111

---

# VIBE7112: Route guard outside a RouterView

> {api} was called outside a page that a RouterView renders, so the guard is ignored.

A guard of a page runs while the route record that its RouterView shows is leaving or updating. A component that no RouterView renders has no such record. This is a warning, printed in development builds only, so that a page can be tested on its own.

### Fix

- Call {api} in the setup of a route component, or of a component inside it.
- Use `router.beforeEach()` for a guard that does not belong to a page.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7112

---

# VIBE7113: Route name not matched

> useRoute('{name}') was called while the route {path} is shown, which is not {name} or one of its children.

`useRoute(name)` narrows the route to the params of `name`, so it checks that a record named `name` is matched.

### Fix

- Call `useRoute()` without a name in a component that several routes render, and narrow with `route.name === '{name}'`.
- Pass the name of the route that renders this component.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7113

---

# VIBE7114: External link in RouterLink

> RouterLink cannot navigate to the external URL {to}.

A RouterLink navigates inside the app. A URL with a scheme, such as `https:` or `mailto:`, or one that starts with `//`, leaves it.

### Fix

- Use `<a href="{to}">` for a link that leaves the app.
- Pass a path inside the app, such as `/about`, or a named location.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7114

---

# VIBE7115: RouterView with slot content

> RouterView does not take slot content.

A RouterView renders the component of the matched route. Content between its tags is not supported.

### Fix

- Remove the content between `<RouterView>` and `</RouterView>`.
- Put a layout around the view in the parent route's component instead.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7115

---

# VIBE7116: Scroll target not found

> No element matches the scroll target {el}.

After a navigation, the router scrolls to the element of the hash or of the `el` that `scrollBehavior` returns. This is a warning, printed in development builds only.

### Fix

- Give the target element the id of the hash, such as `id="details"` for `#details`.
- Return a selector or an element that exists once the new route rendered.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7116

---

# VIBE7117: Web history without a window

> createWebHistory() needs a browser window, but this environment has none.

A web history reads and writes the URL of the browser window.

### Fix

- Use `createMemoryHistory()` in tests and in environments without a window.
- Create the router in code that runs only in the browser.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7117

---

# VIBE7118: Invalid param value
