> The param {param} of the route {route} must be {expected}.

A param declared with `+` or `*` takes an array, and `+` needs at least one item. Any other param takes a single string or number. A value cannot be `.` or `..`, because a URL removes it as a dot segment.

### Fix

- Pass an array for a repeatable param, such as `['a', 'b']` for `/:segments+`.
- Pass a single value for a param without `+` or `*`.
- Pass a value other than `.` or `..` for {param}.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7118

---

# VIBE7201: No element matches the selector

> get({selector}) found no element in the rendered HTML: {html}

`get()` returns the first element that matches a CSS selector and fails when none does, so a test that expects the element stops at the query and shows what was rendered.

### Fix

- Compare the selector with the rendered HTML above.
- Await the action that renders the element, such as `trigger()`, `setProps()` or `flushPromises()`, before the query.
- Use `find()` and `exists()` when the element is expected to be absent.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7201

---

# VIBE7202: Missing element used

> find({selector}) found no element, so {method}() cannot run on it.

`find()` returns an empty wrapper when no element matches, so that `exists()` can check for absence. Every other call on the empty wrapper fails with this error.

### Fix

- Use `get()` when the element must exist: it fails at the query and shows the rendered HTML.
- Check `exists()` before using the wrapper when the element may be absent.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7202

---

# VIBE7203: Event name with a modifier

> trigger() received the event name {event}, which has a modifier: pass the key in the event init instead, as in {example}.

`trigger()` dispatches a native event, whose name has no modifiers. Keys and modifier keys are properties of the event.

### Fix

- Pass the key as `key` in the event init, such as `key: 'Enter'` for `keydown.enter`.
- Pass modifier keys as booleans in the event init, such as `ctrlKey: true` for `click.ctrl`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7203

---

# VIBE7204: Element without a value

> setValue() cannot set a value on a <{tag}> element.

`setValue()` sets the value of an `<input>`, a `<textarea>` or a `<select>`, or the checked state of a checkbox or a radio, and dispatches the events that a user's input would.

### Fix

- Query the form control itself, such as `get('input')`, before calling `setValue()`.
- Use `trigger()` to dispatch events on other elements.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7204

---

# VIBE7205: Wrapper used after unmount

> The wrapper of {name} was used after the component unmounted.

After `unmount()`, or after the test that mounted it finished, the component's nodes are removed, so its wrappers have nothing left to read or act on.

### Fix

- Read what the test checks before calling `unmount()`.
- Mount the component again in each test that uses it, for example in `beforeEach()`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7205

---

# VIBE7206: Unsupported mount option

> mount() does not take the option {option}: {fix}.

`mount()` takes `props`, `slots`, `provide`, `plugins` and `attachTo`. Plugins and provided values are top-level options, children render as they do in the app, and attributes are passed with the props.

### Fix

- Pass `plugins` and `provide` as top-level options of `mount()`.
- Replace a child component with a mock of its module, as in `vi.mock('./Child.vibe')`.
- Pass attributes and the starting state of the component in `props`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7206

---

# VIBE7207: Several root elements

> The component renders {count} root elements, so its wrapper has no single element.

A component wrapper reads its element, attributes, classes and visibility from the component's root element. A component whose template has several roots, or none, has no such element.

### Fix

- Query the element first, as in `get('header')`, and use that wrapper.
- Use `html()` or `text()`, which read every root node.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7207

---

# VIBE7208: Attach target not found

> mount() could not find the attachTo element {selector}.

`attachTo` takes an element or a CSS selector for one, and the component renders into a new element appended to it.

### Fix

- Check that the document has an element that matches {selector} before calling `mount()`.
- Pass the element itself instead of a selector.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7208

---

# VIBE7301: useAsync called with no owner scope

> useAsync() was called with no owner scope, so nothing could abort its runs or stop it.

`useAsync()` belongs to the component or the effect scope that calls it: its runs are aborted and its watcher stops when that owner unmounts or stops. Called outside of one, nothing would ever stop it, so it throws instead.

### Fix

- Call `useAsync()` in a component's `setup`, or in a composable that `setup` calls.
- Outside of a component, call it inside `effectScope().run()` and stop the scope when the data is no longer needed.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE7301

---

# VIBE8001: Not in a vibe.js project

> No vibe.js project at or above `{cwd}`: no package.json depends on @usevibejs/cli.

Project commands such as `vibejs check` run from the project root: the nearest directory, at or above the current one, whose `package.json` lists `@usevibejs/cli` in `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.

### Fix

- Run the command inside a vibe.js project.
- Add `@usevibejs/cli` to the `devDependencies` of the project's `package.json`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8001

---

# VIBE8003: Missing required input

> Missing required input `{name}` for `vibejs {command}`.

The command needs a value that was not given. The CLI never prompts for it, so a coding agent gets the same answer as a person: the JSON output lists the missing input in `error.missing` with an example, and `next` holds a complete command to run.

### Fix

- Pass `{name}` as shown in `vibejs {command} --help`.
- Run the command from `next` in the JSON output.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8003

---

# VIBE8004: Unknown command or option

> Unknown command or option `{name}`.

The first word after `vibejs` must be a command, and every option must belong to that command or be one of the global options `--json`, `--help` and `--version`. A command takes only the arguments its usage lists. For a common mistake, `next` suggests the intended command.

### Fix

- Run `vibejs --help` to list the commands and their options.
- Run the command from `next` in the JSON output.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8004

---

# VIBE8005: Required tool missing or too old

> `{tool}` is missing or older than {minimum}; install it with `{install}`.

`vibejs check` runs the type checker, linter, formatter and test runner installed in the project, never global copies, so every result matches what the project's own scripts report. It needs TypeScript 7.1 or newer, which runs the content mapper for `.vibe` files.

`vibejs components` reads `.vibe` files with the project's own `@usevibejs/compiler`, so it needs that package installed.

### Fix

- Run `{install}` in the project root.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8005

---

# VIBE8008: Unknown error code

> No error code `{code}` in the catalog of this vibejs version.

`vibejs explain` and `vibejs docs` read the error catalog that ships with the installed CLI, so they work offline. A code is missing when it is mistyped or when it comes from a newer vibe.js version than the installed one.

### Fix

- Check the spelling: a code is `VIBE` followed by four digits.
- Update the vibe.js packages in this project if the code comes from a newer version.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8008

---

# VIBE8010: Overwrite needs consent

> Overwriting {count} file(s) needs the user's consent: set `VIBEJS_USER_CONSENT` to their words.

In agent mode, `vibejs generate --force` overwrites files only when `VIBEJS_USER_CONSENT` holds the user's own words agreeing to it, and the JSON output echoes them in `consent`. Nothing is written until then. This is a speed bump that keeps an agent from replacing a person's edits unasked, not a security boundary.

### Fix

- Ask the user, then re-run with `VIBEJS_USER_CONSENT='<their words>'`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8010

---

# VIBE8101: Target not an empty directory

> `{dir}` is not an empty directory; create-vibejs writes a new project only into an empty or missing directory.

The scaffolder never overwrites or merges files, so an existing project is never changed by accident.

### Fix

- Pass the name of a new directory, as in `npm create vibejs@latest my-app`.
- Empty `{dir}` first if it holds nothing you need.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8101

---

# VIBE8102: Invalid package name

> `{name}` is not a valid npm package name.

The directory name becomes the `name` in the new project's `package.json`, so it must be a valid npm package name: lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `_` and `~`, not starting with `.` or `_`, at most 214 characters.

### Fix

- Use a name such as `my-app`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8102

---

# VIBE8103: Install failed

> `{command}` failed in `{dir}`; the project files are kept.

create-vibejs wrote the project and then ran the package manager's install, which failed, often because of the network or the registry. The output of the install is shown with the error.

### Fix

- Run `{command}` in `{dir}` again.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8103

---

# VIBE8104: Missing or invalid arguments

> {problem}. Usage: create-vibejs [dir] [--pm pnpm|npm|yarn|bun] [--no-install]

The scaffolder takes the project directory and two options. In agent mode (`VIBEJS_AGENT=1`, or when the output is not a terminal) it never prompts, so the directory must be given; the JSON output lists it in `error.missing` with an example.

### Fix

- Run `npm create vibejs@latest my-app`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8104

---

# VIBE8201: Project layout incomplete

> `{path}` is missing; `vibejs {command}` expects `ui/index.html`, `server/src/app.module.ts` and `server/src/main.ts`.

`vibejs dev` and `vibejs build` work on a full-stack project: the UI in `ui/`, the server in `server/` and the shared contracts in `contracts/`, all in one package. The UI starts at `ui/index.html`, the server application is `AppModule` in `server/src/app.module.ts`, and `server/src/main.ts` starts it in production.

### Fix

- Run `vibejs {command}` from a project created with `create-vibejs`.
- Create `{path}` as in the project template.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8201

---

# VIBE8202: Invalid app module

> `server/src/app.module.ts` must export `AppModule` (a module class) and `appOptions` (an object); found {found}.

`vibejs dev` loads `server/src/app.module.ts` and creates the application from its `AppModule` export, a class decorated with `@Module()`, and its `appOptions` export, such as `{ basePath: '/api' }`. Until the module has both exports, every request under the API base path is answered with a 503 problem response, and the dev server keeps running.

### Fix

- Export `AppModule` and `appOptions` as in the template.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8202

---

# VIBE8203: Backend failed to start

> The backend failed to start: {reason}.

Loading the server modules or creating the application threw. The dev server keeps serving the UI, answers every request under the API base path with a 503 problem response, and records the error with its stack in `.vibejs/dev.log`, where `vibejs errors` finds it. The backend restarts when a file under `server/` or `contracts/` changes.

### Fix

- Fix the error at the logged location; the backend restarts on save.
- Run `vibejs errors` to see the error with its stack.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8203

---

# VIBE8204: Port in use

> Port {port} is already in use.

`vibejs dev --port <port>` uses exactly that port and does not try another one.

### Fix

- Pass `--port <free port>` or stop the other process.
- Run `vibejs dev` without `--port` to let it pick a free port.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8204

---

# VIBE8205: Empty base path

> `appOptions.basePath` in `server/src/app.module.ts` is empty.

`vibejs dev` serves the UI and the backend on one port: the UI at the root and the backend under `appOptions.basePath`. With an empty base path the backend would answer every request, including the UI's. Until the base path is set, every request under the previous base path (`/api` before the first start) is answered with a 503 problem response.

### Fix

- Set a base path such as `basePath: '/api'` in `appOptions`, as in the template.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8205

---

# VIBE8301: Unreadable tool output

> `{tool}` exited with code {exitCode} and output that vibejs check cannot read.

The tool crashed or printed something other than the format `vibejs check` parses, often because of a broken configuration file. The diagnostic carries the first 40 lines of the tool's output; the other tools' results are still reported.

### Fix

- Run the tool directly in the project root to see its full output.
- Fix the configuration or the installation the output points to.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8301

---

# VIBE8302: File not fully covered

> `{file}` is not fully covered: {uncovered}.

`vibejs check` reports every file below 100% statement, branch, function or line coverage, with its uncovered ranges. It is a warning: the check still passes. To make it a failure, enable the commented `thresholds` line in `vitest.config.ts`.

### Fix

- Add tests for the listed ranges; never add coverage-ignore comments.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8302

---

# VIBE8303: File not formatted

> `{file}` is not formatted.

The file differs from what oxfmt writes with the project's `.oxfmtrc.json`.

### Fix

- Run `vibejs check --fix`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8303

---

# VIBE8304: Build failed

> Building the {part} failed: {reason}.

`vibejs build` builds the UI into `ui/dist`, then the server into `server/dist/main.js`. The reason holds the error code, location and message of the first build error.

### Fix

- Fix the reported error and run `vibejs build` again.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8304

---

# VIBE8401: Generated files differ

> {count} file(s) differ from what `vibejs generate {kind} {name}` writes: {paths}.

`vibejs generate` never overwrites a file that differs from what it would write, so edits to generated code are never lost. A file equal to the generated one is skipped, which makes a second run of the same command a no-op. Nothing is written while any file differs.

### Fix

- Run with `--dry-run --json` to compare, then rename or `--force`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8401

---

# VIBE8402: Register by hand

> Register `{what}` in `{path}` by hand: {instruction}.

`vibejs generate` registers new code in the files of the template: a module in the `imports` of `@Module` on `AppModule` in `server/src/app.module.ts`, a contract in the `contracts` object of `ui/src/api.ts`, and a page in the `defineRoutes([...])` array of `ui/src/routes.ts`. When such a file is missing or has another shape, it writes the other files and reports the exact code to add instead. The command still succeeds.

### Fix

- Apply the instruction, then run `vibejs check`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8402

---

# VIBE8403: Invalid generator name

> `{name}` is not a valid {kind} name; expected {expected}.

`vibejs generate` takes names verbatim and derives file, class and route names from them. A resource is a camelCase identifier, usually plural (`users`); a component or a page is a PascalCase identifier (`UserCard`, `Users`). JavaScript reserved words and the names the generated code uses itself (such as `app`, `client` or `setup` for a resource, `Page` for a page) are not valid. A resource also needs a valid singular: `--singular <word>` gives it when the derived one is empty or taken; other kinds ignore `--singular`. `next` holds the command with a corrected name.

### Fix

- Use the name from `next`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8403

---

# VIBE8501: App module failed to load

> Could not load `server/src/app.module.ts`: {reason}.

`vibejs di`, `vibejs routes` and `vibejs request` (when no dev server runs) load `server/src/app.module.ts` and the project's `@usevibejs/server` in process. Importing the module, or creating the application for a request, threw an error that has no VIBE code of its own; an error with a code is reported as itself.

### Fix

- Fix the error at the reported location, then run the command again.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8501

---

# VIBE8502: Request failed

> The request to `{url}` could not be made: {reason}.

A `vibejs dev` server is running for this project, so `vibejs request` sends the request to it, but the server did not answer. It may have stopped or crashed while the request was on its way.

### Fix

- Start the dev server again with `vibejs dev`, or stop it so the request runs in process.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8502

---

# VIBE8503: Invalid request input

> Invalid request input: {reason}.

`vibejs request <METHOD> <path>` takes a path that starts with `/`, a `--data` body that is JSON (inline, or `@file` read relative to the current directory) and only for methods that take a body, and `-H` headers written as `Name: value`.

### Fix

- Pass `--data` as JSON or `@file`, and `-H` as `Name: value`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8503

---

# VIBE8504: Routes file not statically readable

> `ui/src/routes.ts` cannot be read statically: {reason}.

`vibejs routes` lists the UI routes without running any UI code: it parses `ui/src/routes.ts` and reads the array literal passed to `defineRoutes([...])` in a top-level declaration. The file has a syntax error, or it has no such array, for example when the routes are built by a function call or imported from another file.

### Fix

- Keep `export const routes = defineRoutes([...])` with an array literal; see the router docs.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8504

---

# VIBE8601: Malformed agent rules markers

> {file} has {problem}; vibejs agents sync only edits text between one BEGIN and one END marker.

`vibejs agents sync`, `vibejs dev` and `create-vibejs` keep the vibe.js rules for coding agents in a block of AGENTS.md between the lines `<!-- BEGIN:vibejs-agent-rules -->` and `<!-- END:vibejs-agent-rules -->`, and never touch the text around it. With a marker missing, out of order or repeated, the block's extent is unknown, so the file is left as it is. `vibejs dev` logs this as a warning and keeps running.

### Fix

- Restore or delete both marker lines, then run `vibejs agents sync`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8601

---

# VIBE8602: Invalid .mcp.json

> .mcp.json is {problem}; vibejs agents sync only sets mcpServers.vibejs in a JSON object.

`vibejs agents sync`, `vibejs dev` and `create-vibejs` register the `vibejs mcp` server for coding agents under `mcpServers.vibejs` in `.mcp.json` and keep every other key. When the file is not valid JSON, not a JSON object, or its `mcpServers` is not an object, that entry cannot be set without losing the file's content, so nothing is written. `vibejs dev` logs this as a warning and keeps running.

### Fix

- Make `.mcp.json` valid JSON with an object `mcpServers`, or delete it, then run `vibejs agents sync`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE8602

---

# VIBE9001: Invalid route path

> The path "{path}" has the invalid segment "{segment}".

A route path is `/` or one or more segments, each starting with `/`. A static segment uses only letters, digits and `.`, `_`, `~`, `-`, and is never `.` or `..`, because URL parsing removes those; a param segment is `:` followed by a name that starts with a letter or `_`. A contract prefix follows the same rules, is never `/` and has no trailing slash. Wildcard, optional and pattern segments are not supported.

### Fix

- Write the path as `/` or as segments such as `/users/:userId/posts`.
- Remove the trailing slash, the empty segment or the unsupported characters from "{path}".

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9001

---

# VIBE9002: Duplicate path param

> The path "{path}" declares the param ":{param}" more than once.

Param names must be unique in the full path of a route, which is the contract prefix followed by the route path.

### Fix

- Rename one of the ":{param}" params so that every param name in the prefix and the route path is unique.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9002

---

# VIBE9003: Not a route

> The contract entry "{key}" is not a route built with get, post, put, patch or del.

`defineContract` accepts only the values that the route builders return. A plain object, `undefined` or a route that is already bound to a contract is rejected.

### Fix

- Build "{key}" with `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` or `del`, for example `{key}: get('/')`.
- Pass the route builders' results to `defineContract`, not the routes of another contract.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9003

---

# VIBE9004: Body on a GET route

> The GET route "{path}" declares a body.

A GET request cannot carry a body: `fetch` rejects it and many servers and proxies drop it. Inputs of a GET route travel in its path params, query and headers.

### Fix

- Move the inputs of "{path}" into `query`, or declare the route with `post` if it needs a body.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9004

---

# VIBE9091: Missing path param

> The call to "{path}" is missing the path param "{param}".

A client call fills each `:param` of the route's full path from `input.params`. The call rejects before any request is sent when one of them is `undefined`. The types already require every path param, so this happens only when the input is cast or built at run time.

### Fix

- Pass `params.{param}` in the call input.
- Check that the route path "{path}" is the one you meant to call.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9091

---

# VIBE9101: inject() outside an injection context

> inject({token}) was called outside an injection context.

`inject()` reads the provider scope of the class or factory that the container is building at that moment. That context exists only while a constructor runs (field initializers and the constructor body), during the synchronous part of a factory and inside `runInInjectionContext()`. It ends at the first `await`, and a class created with `new` outside the container has none.

### Fix

- Move `inject({token})` into a field initializer, such as `private readonly dep = inject({token})`.
- Call `inject()` before the first `await` of a factory or of a `runInInjectionContext()` callback.
- List {token} in the `inject` array of the factory and take it as a factory parameter.

### Example

```ts
class UsersService {
  private readonly db = inject(Db);
}
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9101

---

# VIBE9102: No provider

> No provider for {token} is visible in {module} (requested by {chain}).

A module sees its own providers, the providers exported by the modules it imports and the providers of global modules. The chain lists each dependent, ending in the missing token.

### Fix

- Add {token} to `providers` of {module}.
- Import a module that exports {token} into {module}.
- Pass the option `optional: true` to `inject({token})` when the dependency may be absent.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9102

---

# VIBE9103: Circular dependency

> Circular dependency in {module}: {cycle}.

Every provider is created once, before the application starts, so two providers cannot each need the other to exist first.

### Fix

- Move the part that both providers need into a third provider and inject it in both.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9103

---

# VIBE9104: Constructor parameters

> The class {token} declares constructor parameters, but the container creates providers with no arguments.

Classes listed as providers are created with `new Cls()`. Dependencies are read with `inject()` in field initializers, so they stay explicit under every compiler.

### Fix

- Replace each constructor parameter with an `inject()` field, such as `private db = inject(Db)`.

### Example

```ts
class UsersService {
  private readonly db = inject(Db);
}
```

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9104

---

# VIBE9105: Provider creation failed

> Creating {token} in {module} failed.

The constructor or the factory of the provider threw, or the factory returned a promise that rejected. The original error is the `cause` of this error.

### Fix

- Read the `cause` of this error and fix the constructor or factory of {token}.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9105

---

# VIBE9106: Async provider not ready

> {requester} needs {token} before the factory of {token} has settled.

All factories are awaited before any other class is created, so a class built earlier on behalf of a factory can only inject factories that have already settled.

### Fix

- Add {token} to the `inject` list of the factory that is being built, so that {token} settles first.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9106

---

# VIBE9107: Invalid provider

> A provider in {module} is neither a class nor an object with a token in `provide` and exactly one of `useClass`, `useValue`, `useFactory` or `useExisting`.

A provider entry is either a class with no constructor parameters or an object that names the token in `provide` and says how to create its value: `useClass` takes a class, `useFactory` a function and `useExisting` a token.

### Fix

- List the class itself, or set `provide` and exactly one of `useClass`, `useValue`, `useFactory` or `useExisting`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9107

---

# VIBE9201: Not a module

> {module} is imported at {path}, but the class has no `@Module()` decorator.

Every entry of `imports`, and the `module` class of a dynamic module, must carry its own `@Module()`. The decorator is not inherited, so a subclass of a module class is not a module until it is decorated itself.

### Fix

- Add the `@Module()` decorator to the class {module}; an empty options object is enough.
- Import the module class itself instead of a class derived from it.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9201

---

# VIBE9202: Module import cycle

> The modules import each other in a cycle: {cycle}.

Modules are scanned depth-first, and each module is set up after the modules it imports, so two modules cannot import each other.

### Fix

- Move the providers that both modules need into a third module and import it in both.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9202

---

# VIBE9203: Invalid export

> {module} exports {export}, which is neither one of its providers nor one of its imports.

A module can export the tokens of its own providers and the modules it imports. Exporting an imported module makes that module's exports visible to the importer.

### Fix

- If {export} is a provider token, add its provider to `providers` of {module}.
- If {export} is a module, add it to `imports` of {module}.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9203

---

# VIBE9204: Shutdown hooks failed

> {count} shutdown hooks failed: {hooks}.

Every `onModuleDestroy` and `onApplicationShutdown` hook runs even when an earlier one fails. The errors are collected in an `AggregateError`, which is the `cause` of this error.

### Fix

- Read `cause.errors` of this error and fix each hook that is listed.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9204

---

# VIBE9301: Legacy decorators required

> {decorator} was called with a standard decorator context, but the server decorators need `experimentalDecorators`.

The server decorators use the TypeScript legacy decorator signature. Without `experimentalDecorators`, the compiler passes a standard decorator context instead, and some build tools leave the `@` syntax in their output, where no runtime can execute it.

### Fix

- Set `"experimentalDecorators": true` in `compilerOptions` of the server `tsconfig.json`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9301

---

# VIBE9302: Missing @Controller

> {controller} is listed in `controllers` of {module}, but neither it nor a parent class has `@Controller()`.

A controller serves the routes of exactly one contract, which `@Controller(contract)` names.

### Fix

- Add `@Controller(contract)` to the class {controller}.
- Remove {controller} from `controllers` of {module}.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9302

---

# VIBE9303: Route not handled

> The route {route} of the contract of {controller} has no handler.

A controller handles every route of its contract, so that no declared route is left without an answer.

### Fix

- Add a method to {controller} with `@Handle(contract.route)` for {route}.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9303

---

# VIBE9304: Route handled twice

> The route {route} is handled by more than one method of {controller}: {methods}.

Each route has exactly one handler.

### Fix

- Keep one handler for {route} and remove `@Handle()` from the other methods.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9304

---

# VIBE9305: Foreign route

> The method {controller}.{method} handles a route that is not part of the contract of {controller}.

`@Handle()` takes a route of the contract named in `@Controller()`. A route of another contract, or a route spec that `defineContract()` has not bound, cannot be served by this controller.

### Fix

- Pass a route of this controller's contract to `@Handle()` on {method}.
- Move {method} to the controller of the contract that declares its route.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9305

---

# VIBE9306: Contract served twice

> More than one controller serves the same contract: {controllers}.

A contract belongs to exactly one controller, so each route has a single handler in the application.

### Fix

- Merge the controllers {controllers} into one.
- Split the contract into one contract per controller.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9306

---

# VIBE9307: Static method

> {decorator} is on the static method {controller}.{method}, but it needs an instance method.

Handlers run on the controller instance that the container creates, so they can use its injected fields. Method guards, interceptors, filters and metadata apply to those handlers.

### Fix

- Remove `static` from {controller}.{method}.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9307

---

# VIBE9401: Route conflict

> {method} {path} matches the same requests as another route; the handlers are {handlers}.

Routes are matched segment by segment. A static segment such as `/users/me` may sit next to a param segment such as `/users/:id`, but two routes with the same method and the same shape, such as `/users/:id` and `/users/:userId`, cannot both be reached.

### Fix

- Rename one of the paths so that the two routes differ in a static segment, or change the method of one of them.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9401

---

# VIBE9402: Shutdown timeout

> {inFlight} requests were still running after the shutdown timeout of {timeout} ms, so the server was closed with them in flight.

`close()` stops accepting requests and waits for the running ones before it runs the shutdown hooks. After `shutdownTimeout` it closes the open connections and goes on.

### Fix

- Raise `shutdownTimeout` in the options of `VibeFactory.create()`.
- Make long handlers stop early when `ctx.signal` is aborted.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9402

---

# VIBE9403: Already listening

> listen() was called on an app that already listens or is closing (server: {url}).

An app serves one server. `listen()` cannot be called a second time, or after `close()` has started.

### Fix

- Call `listen()` once per app; create another app with `VibeFactory.create()` for a second server.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9403

---

# VIBE9404: Wildcard origin with credentials

> cors() was called with `origin: '*'` and `credentials: true`, which browsers reject.

A response that allows credentials must name the requesting origin; browsers ignore `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on credentialed requests.

### Fix

- List the allowed origins explicitly, such as `origin: ['https://app.example.com']`.
- Remove `credentials: true` when the requests carry no cookies or authorization headers.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9404

---

# VIBE9405: Invalid base path

> The base path {basePath} is not empty and not of the form `/segment` or `/a/b`.

`VibeFactory.create()` mounts every route under `basePath`. A path without a leading slash, with a trailing slash or with an empty segment would make routes unreachable.

### Fix

- Pass `''` for no prefix, or a path such as `/api` without a trailing slash.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9405

---

# VIBE9501: Response violates the contract

> The value that {route} returned does not match its response schema: {issues}.

With `validateResponses` on (the default), a handler's result is validated against the route's `response` schema before it is sent. A mismatch is a server bug, so the client receives 500 INTERNAL_ERROR and the issues are logged.

### Fix

- Change the handler so that it returns a value that matches the `response` schema, or update the schema in the contract.
- Pass `validateResponses: false` to `VibeFactory.create()` only to diagnose; the client then receives the value unchecked.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9501

---

# VIBE9502: Undeclared error code

> {route} answered with the error code {code}, which the route does not declare.

A route lists the error codes it raises in `errors`, so that clients can handle each of them. The problem is still sent; this warning shows that the contract is incomplete.

### Fix

- Add the code with the status it answers to the route's `errors`.
- Use a built-in code such as `BAD_REQUEST`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN` or `NOT_FOUND` when it fits.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9502

---

# VIBE9503: Unhandled error

> A request failed with an unexpected error, so the client received 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.

Any error that is not an `HttpError` is logged with its cause and answered with a problem that hides the details. Only `HttpError` values and the declared error codes of a route reach the client.

### Fix

- Read the logged `cause` and fix the code that threw it.
- Throw an `HttpError`, or call `ctx.fail()` with a declared error code, when the error is meant for the client.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9503

---

# VIBE9504: Invalid cookie name

> The cookie name "{name}" is not a valid token.

Cookie names follow the token rule of RFC 9110: they contain no spaces, separators or control characters.

### Fix

- Use a name made of letters, digits and ``!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~``.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9504

---

# VIBE9505: Invalid raw result

> {route} declares a raw response but returned a value of type {type}.

A raw route sends its result unparsed, with the declared content type. The result must be a `Response` or a body that `new Response()` accepts.

### Fix

- Return a `Response`, or a `string`, `Blob`, `ArrayBuffer`, typed array, `ReadableStream`, `URLSearchParams` or `FormData` from the handler.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9505

---

# VIBE9601: Invalid configuration

> The environment variables do not match the config schema: {issues}.

`defineConfig()` validates every listed environment variable when the config class is created and reports every failing key at once. The message lists the keys and the schema messages, never the values.

### Fix

- Set the listed environment variables to values that match their schemas.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9601

---

# VIBE9602: Asynchronous config schema

> The config schema of {key} validates asynchronously, but a config is validated synchronously.

The config class is created by a constructor, so its schemas must return their result without a promise.

### Fix

- Use a synchronous schema for {key}, without async checks or transforms.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9602

---

# VIBE9701: Unused provider override

> {module} overrides {token}, but no module of the application provides it.

`overrideProvider()` replaces a provider by its token in every module that provides it, before anything is built. Only providers can be overridden: controllers, guards, interceptors, filters and module classes cannot, and neither can a token that the application never provides.

### Fix

- Provide {token} in a module that the testing module imports, or add its provider to the testing module's `providers`.
- Remove the `overrideProvider({token})` call.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9701

---

# VIBE9801: Unconvertible schema

> The {part} schema of {route} cannot be converted to JSON Schema: {reason}

`generateOpenApi()` converts each schema with its Standard JSON Schema converter (`~standard.jsonSchema`) and falls back to the `toJsonSchema` option. The schema has no converter, or the converter and the fallback both failed. The `cause` of this error is the error that was thrown.

### Fix

- Use a schema that JSON can represent, such as `z.iso.datetime()` instead of `z.date()`.
- Pass converter options through `libraryOptions`, such as the options that make the library emit a placeholder for unrepresentable types.
- Pass a `toJsonSchema(schema, io)` function that returns the JSON Schema for this schema.
- A recursive schema without a name refers to itself with `$ref: "#"`, which in an OpenAPI document points at the document. Give it a name so that it moves to `components.schemas`: an `id` in zod `.meta()`, or valibot `libraryOptions.definitions`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9801

---

# VIBE9802: Schema name collision

> Two different schemas are named {name}; the second one is used by {route}.

The named definitions (`$defs`) of every schema are moved to `components.schemas`, where one name holds one schema. Another route already used the name {name} for a schema that is not the same.

### Fix

- Give one of the two schemas another name.
- A name such as `__schema0` was generated by the converter for an unnamed recursive schema. Give each recursive schema an explicit name: an `id` in zod `.meta()`, or valibot `libraryOptions.definitions`.
- Reuse one schema object under the name {name} wherever the same shape is meant.
- A schema used in a request and in a response must convert to the same JSON Schema both ways; in zod, `z.strictObject()` does, while `z.object()` adds `additionalProperties: false` only to the response.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9802

---

# VIBE9803: Invalid error status

> The error {code} of {route} has the status {status}, which is not between 400 and 599.

`generateOpenApi()` documents each code in a route's `errors` as a problem response under its status. A status outside 400–599 is not an error status: a 2xx status would replace the success response, and other numbers are not valid response keys.

### Fix

- Give {code} a 4xx or 5xx status, such as `404` or `409`.

Source: https://vibejs.org/v0/errors/VIBE9803
